articles.title: Bitcoin Price Sinks Toward $80,000 as Korea’s Stock Rout Worsens
articles.text:
Bitcoin dips to $80.1K as KOSPI closes at its lowest since April
Bitcoin price action continued to see contagion from a Korean tech sell-off after the KOSPI Index fell 7.5% on Thursday.
Bitcoin (BTC) fell to its lowest levels in over three weeks on Thursday as crypto tracked fresh losses on South Korean stock markets.
Key points:
- Bitcoin reached new local lows of $80,154 as downside pressure returned to South Korean equities.
- The KOSPI closed Thursday at 5,554 points, its lowest since early April, driven by a rout in tech stocks.
- Oil prices cooled, with Brent crude dropping more than 2% despite an “unjustifiable” Singapore fuel-tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz.
Bitcoin price nears $80,000 as KOSPI falls 7.5%
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD hitting $80,154 on Bitstamp, a level last seen on Sept. 20.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The weakness came after South Korea’s Korea Composite Stock Price Index, or KOSPI, finished the day 7.5% lower, taking week-to-date losses to 15.5%.
KOSPI Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
As with earlier in the week, tech giants bore the brunt of the sell-off, with SK Hynix down 11% and Samsung Electronics finishing 9.5% lower on the day.
SK Hynix stock one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
As Cointelegraph reported, concerns over AI debt obligations, foreign capital outflows and competition from China contributed to the South Korean market rout, with KOSPI’s 200-day moving average dropping to as low as 5,450 points, a level not seen since late July. It ended Thursday’s trading session at 5,554 points, marking its lowest daily close since April 8.
Talking to local media publication The Korea Herald, Mirae Asset Securities analyst Kim Seok-hwan warned that global macro headwinds would add further friction going forward.
“Volatility is expected to persist in the near term,” he said. “As domestic supply-demand conditions deteriorate, the market has become more sensitive to external risks, while a near-term improvement in the global environment appears unlikely.”
SK Hynix and Samsung will release third-quarter earnings data on Oct. 28 and 29, respectively, potentially adding to downside volatility in investor tech sentiment should the numbers fall short of projections. Samsung is expected to confirm Q3 sales of 195 trillion won ($145 billion) and an operating profit of around 107 trillion won ($80 billion).
Oil falls despite Singapore tanker sinking
Downside pressure on Bitcoin was compounded on the back of Wednesday’s higher-than-expected US inflation data.
The September print of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) came in at 3.7% year-on-year, sparking a hawkish shift in market expectations of further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
“Does the beat force further hiking — or does credit stress prompt policy recalibration?” trading company QCP Capital asked alongside its macro analysis seen by Cointelegraph on Thursday.
Related: CryptoQuant’s 3 charts keeping Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ thesis valid
With high oil prices accounting for a significant portion of the uptick in CPI, both WTI and Brent crude fell on Thursday despite mounting tensions in the Middle East. A Singapore-registered oil tanker was sunk in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, a move that the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore described as “unjustifiable.”
Speaking to CNBC, Firas Bechwaty, head of business development at online trading platform ICM, saw little chance of Hormuz transit volumes returning to levels from before the US-Iran war began.
“At the same time, Saudi crude continues to reach international buyers through alternative routes, while accelerated emergency stock releases by IEA members provide an additional buffer, preventing a sharp rise in prices, even as tensions remain elevated,” he observed.
At the time of writing, WTI traded below $95 per barrel, down 0.5%, while Brent was 2.2% lower at $103.7 per barrel.
CFDs on Brent crude oil one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

articles.title: Bitcoin Whipsaws as Crypto Liquidations Near $1 Billion - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Crypto liquidations reached $948.22 million in 24 hours across 177,440 traders, with long positions accounting for 90.6%, per CoinGlass.
- Bitcoin fell 2.6% and broke support after hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI data revived bets on another Fed rate hike.
- Bitcoin now trades roughly 2% below the average cost of U.S. spot ETF holders near $82,300, putting those buyers back underwater.
Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Thursday for the first time in over a month, extending Wednesday’s inflation-driven slide and wiping out nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets. It's currently trading just about $82,000 after several hours of increased volatility.
Ethereum and XRP dropped close to 5%, Zcash sank almost 10%, and only five coins in the top 100 managed gains above 1%. Pick any coin in the top 100 and it's likely in the red today.
Across the market, 177,440 traders were liquidated in 24 hours for a total of $948.22 million, per CoinGlass, with longs accounting for $858.96 million, or 90.6%. Ethereum led with $282.03 million, with Bitcoin just behind at a little over $200 million.
This was the third-heaviest day for long liquidations in the last 90 days, behind October 8 and August 22. The largest single order liquidated yesterday was a $12.03 million Bitcoin long on Binance, force-closed at $80,208.96.
A liquidation happens when a trader borrows to bet on a price move and the market goes the other way. Once losses eat through the collateral, the exchange sells the position automatically, and that forced selling drags prices lower and trips the next batch of leveraged longs.
The trigger was Wednesday’s inflation report, which showed consumer prices up 3.7% year over year in September against a 3.6% forecast, with core inflation at 2.6% against 2.5%. Thursday’s Producer Price Index, which tracks business input costs, rose 6.3% annually versus a 5.5% forecast.
Much of that inflation comes from oil, with Brent crude near $104 a barrel, about 70% above a year ago amid the war between the U.S. and Iran. That feeds into fuel, shipping, and almost everything else that needs to be transported to reach consumers.
Hot inflation pushes the Federal Reserve toward higher interest rates, which lifts Treasury yields, the return investors earn for lending to the U.S. government. A bond paying around 5% with almost no risk makes Bitcoin a harder sell, while higher rates make borrowing pricier and strengthen the dollar, draining the cheap money leveraged crypto traders run on.
Iliya Kalchev, analyst at Nexo, reads the selloff as a broad exit from risk more than a Fed story, with stocks and copper falling, gold rising and South Korea’s Kospi down about 8%.
“Bitcoin has slipped to the bottom of the $81,000 to $87,000 range it has held since late September, and Glassnode flags $80,000 as the level to watch,” Kalchev told Decrypt. “It is also now roughly 2% below the average cost of U.S. spot ETF holders, near $82,300, after closing above that line on 21 of the 24 days since September 21. That puts ETF buyers back underwater, and reclaiming it is the first test of any rebound,”
On the daily chart, Bitcoin broke below $81,603, the strongest upper support from its August-to-October rally from $62,763 to $87,422, where uptrend pullbacks often stall. The drop reached $79,711 before buyers pulled the price back near $80,925, off a rising trend band near $80,286.
The Relative Strength Index, a 0-to-100 momentum gauge where 50 splits bulls from bears, fell to about 44, while the golden cross still keeps the longer-term uptrend intact.
A daily close back above $81,603 would reopen the path to $84,245 and the $87,422 swing high. Losing $80,286 would expose $78,002 as the next support, and then $75,092.
Kalchev sees early signs the selling is not deepening, including cooling profit-taking, but said a recovery needs more than a bounce.
“Three things need to line up for Bitcoin to push through. ETF flows have to turn consistently positive, after $681 million of outflows last week and a single $177 million inflow day. Selling by long-term holders has to ease,” Kalchev explained.
For Kalchev, a bullish market would require that leverage happens with a sustained buying instead of just a bounce. He added that a “Fed path that stops at one 25 basis point hike would take some pressure off the backdrop.”
The Fed announces its rate decision on October 28, followed by core PCE inflation data the next day and October payrolls on November 6.

articles.title: Ethereum, Altcoins See 'Outsized Drawdowns' Due to Macro Pressures - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ethereum, XRP, and Solana have all dropped in value on the day, with "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin.
- Experts point to Wednesday's consumer price index coming in at 3.7% and expectations of an October interest rate hike as major macro pressures.
- The slide is also a natural hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.
Altcoins have taken a hit over the past 24 hours, with major tokens seeing "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin. Experts say that this has largely been prompted by macro pressures pushing prices down.
With the market cap of all cryptocurrencies dropping by 2.5% to $2.8 trillion, Ethereum dropped by 5.5% to a $289 billion market cap over the past 24 hours, XRP fell by 5.1% to $82.4 billion, and Solana slipped by 3.8% to $60.6 billion. Meanwhile, industry leader Bitcoin has slipped by 3.1% on the day and 2.6% on the week, sitting at a market cap of $1.6 trillion.
It comes after the consumer price index rose 3.7% in the year to September, as Decrypt reported on Wednesday, with Myriad predictors pointing to a 28% chance of an October interest rate hike (Disclaimer: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt's parent company Dastan).
Nick Forster, founder of options trading exchange Derive.xyz, said in a note shared with Decrypt that this shifted traders into "protection mode" as "hedging activity" on the platform doubled, and whales pulled back on optimistic bets made in spring.
"This immediate pull-back from long-term upside bets alongside aggressive short-term hedging shows a dramatic regime shift," he said, "with institutional participants rapidly reassessing their macro risk exposure as the path for interest rates turns murky again."
When markets react like this, Luke Nolan, senior research associate at CoinShares, says that altcoins are impacted the most.
"[It] seems to be high beta assets just got hit harder, similar to in equities as well, where the high flyers have seen outsized drawdowns in recent sessions," Nolan told Decrypt. "Alts are typically more sensitive to financial conditions, and tightening affects the premise of liquidity expanding."
Nolan also highlighted the U.S. dollar hitting a near 18-month high as a downward pressure on the entire crypto market. He said that over a medium-term horizon, crypto tends to have an inverse correlation to the US Dollar Index, or DXY. This is partly due to crypto being priced in dollars, Nolan explained, but also because a rising dollar causes a tightening in liquidity and a fall in risk appetite.
Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt that the slide is also a hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.
Since the start of October, futures open interest in altcoins (excluding Ethereum) has fallen by $8 billion, Shannon said. To him, that shows traders have “taken chips off the table,” which is a natural reaction after such a strong run.
That pattern is playing out with Ethereum, he added. ETH outperformed Bitcoin for three consecutive months, the first time it’s managed that since March 2021, and investors have been cashing in since. Ethereum ETFs saw 11 straight trading days of net outflows totalling $782.8 million, he said, before a brief inflow on Tuesday. Money has been heading back out since, per CoinGlass data, with $129.5 million in net outflows.
"This price action is more of a consolidation period for altcoins that have already done well," Shannon told Decrypt. "Altcoins generally tend to exhibit high correlations with BTC in tough times and lower correlations, especially with idiosyncratic catalysts, in better market environments. Hence, for the near term, it is possible that these altcoins trade in lockstep with BTC, albeit more sensitively."
For prices to recover, Nolan says he wants to see expectations of an interest rate hike in October to fall. Right now, he struggles to call a bottom for altcoins as he sees valid arguments for movements in either direction.
"I could see a situation where Bitcoin loses its support and altcoins likely bleed further," Nolan told Decrypt. "The opposite could also be true: this could be just a short-term correction, and we could be back into decent market conditions soon, which if Bitcoin was to push back decently above 80k, I could very well see an outsized up move for altcoins."

articles.title: CoinShares Expects Modest Inflows Into Thailand Crypto ETFs
articles.text:
Thailand crypto ETFs may see slow start despite new rules: CoinShares
Thailand’s new Bitcoin and Ether ETF rules take effect Friday, but CoinShares expects modest initial inflows as existing investment options compete for demand.
Thailand’s first crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs) may get off to a slow start despite Bangkok’s efforts to expand access to regulated digital asset investments.
“I would expect modest inflows initially, with tens of millions of US dollars across the first products a more realistic starting expectation than billions,” James Butterfill, head of research at digital asset investment firm CoinShares, told Cointelegraph.
The country opens a new route for crypto exposure on Friday as its rules for Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) ETFs to list on the Stock Exchange of Thailand take effect.
The rules will allow retail Thai investors to access locally listed crypto ETFs, while restricting overseas crypto ETF investments through domestic brokers to institutional and ultra-high-net-worth investors.
Thailand’s first crypto funds will need regulatory approval and the necessary custody and distribution arrangements before trading can begin.
Hong Kong offers a cautionary comparison
Butterfill pointed to Hong Kong as an example of how even a major financial center can struggle to attract substantial crypto ETF inflows.
Hong Kong accounts for just 0.42% of assets in global crypto exchange-traded products (ETPs) despite the city’s status as an international financial hub, he said.
Global crypto investment products held $172.9 billion in assets under management, including $733 million in Hong Kong, according to CoinShares data as of late September.
First Thai crypto ETF launches remain uncertain
Butterfill said that existing investment options may limit demand for new Thai ETFs, as some investors already gain Bitcoin exposure through foreign funds or direct crypto trading.
Thailand’s MFC Asset Management, which Butterfill identified as a firm worth watching for potential ETF launches, introduced its Bitcoin ETF Tracker Fund (MBTCETF-UI) in 2024. The fund invests in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF by assets under management.
“Local ETFs therefore need to attract new investors or offer a compelling reason to switch,” Butterfill said.
Apart from MFC, Butterfill pointed to ONE Asset Management as another potential ETF issuer worth watching. In 2024, ONE became the first Thai asset manager to receive approval for a Bitcoin ETF-linked fund.
Related: Bitcoin ETFs shed $261M as XRP funds buck weekly outflow trend
Butterfill said he hadn’t confirmed either company’s plans to launch a locally listed crypto ETF or when the first products might begin trading.
Cointelegraph contacted Thailand’s SEC, ONE Asset Management and MFC Asset Management about potential ETF launches but had not received responses by publication time.

articles.title: Ledger Announces Atom Touchscreen Android Device - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ledger has announced Atom, a touchscreen Android device that incorporates a Secure Element running Ledger OS.
- Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner, with its Seeker app and Solana dApp Store preinstalled on Ledger's new Atom device.
- The launch comes as Ledger investigates hidden implants found in hardware wallets sold through a reseller in Southeast Asia.
Ledger's new Atom device will ship with Solana's Seeker app preinstalled, the companies announced on stage at Ledger's Op3n conference in Paris on Thursday.
Billed as a "signer" rather than a hardware wallet, the Atom is an Android-powered touchscreen device equipped with a data-only eSIM and Ledger's Secure Element, enabling users to send and receive encrypted messages with other Atom users as well as perform crypto transactions in the manner of its range of wallets. To do so, the device switches into a Ledger OS-powered "Secure Mode" for sensitive operations such as signing transactions and authorising AI agent requests.
The Atom sports a 6.77-inch OLED display, rear camera and 4,000mAh battery, and runs on a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip. It also incorporates a hardware privacy switch that physically cuts power to the camera and microphone.
The device also runs third-party apps, and will come preinstalled with Solana's Seeker app after Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner. Seeker combines Solana Mobile's wallet with its Solana dapp Store, which lists more than 1,500 decentralized apps, and will appear on Atom's home screen. Until now, the store was available on Solana Mobile's own Seeker phone.
Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that.
Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum… pic.twitter.com/vHhDNQYipz
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 15, 2026
Ledger Atom runs on the Android Open Source Project, the free, open version of Google's mobile operating system, alongside a Secure Element chip running Ledger OS. Its display and touch controls are physically isolated from Android, according to the release, and approvals in the Seeker app happen in a "Secure Mode" backed by the Secure Element.
"Having the Seeker app on Ledger Atom from day one just makes sense, so Ledger users get access to the Solana ecosystem without giving up any of the security," said Ian Rogers, Ledger's chief human agency officer.
Solana Mobile began opening its software stack to other Android manufacturers in March. Samsung Wallet also recently added USDC transfers on Solana. Seeker has handled more than $13 billion in transaction volume and 154 million transactions, according to the company, which says it has sold more than 200,000 devices across Seeker and its earlier Saga phone.
Hardware makers that integrate the stack can earn rewards in SKR, the native token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem, which also rewards users and developers, the release said.
Existing Seeker phones will remain fully supported, Solana Mobile said. Reservations for Ledger Atom are open now, though neither company has given a price or shipping date.
Ledger investigates tampered devices
The Ledger Atom will include anti-tampering and tamper-evident features from the packaging to the device itself, according to the press release, including ways to help detect whether the enclosure has been opened, and will only be sold through Ledger's official site.
The announcement of the Atom comes at an awkward time for Ledger, as the firm investigates tampered devices in its reseller network linked to a suspected $87 million wallet drain.
The company this week disclosed that its Donjon security team had found an implant in a hardware wallet sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that captures recovery phrases during setup and sends them out over LTE. On Tuesday, it asked resellers in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to pull its devices from shelves.

articles.title: Babylon Moves Bitcoin Lending Proposal Forward on Aave V4
articles.text:
Babylon advances native Bitcoin lending proposal on Aave V4
Babylon’s proposal to bring native Bitcoin collateral to Aave V4 has entered a new governance stage, but further votes and security reviews remain before launch.
Bitcoin-focused developer Babylon Labs has submitted a proposal to let users borrow stablecoins on Aave against native Bitcoin (BTC).
Under the hood, users would lock their BTC in vaults on the Bitcoin network and borrow against it on Aave. A non-transferable token on Ethereum would represent the collateral, while the BTC itself would remain on its native blockchain without being bridged or wrapped.
The Wednesday proposal follows an initial submission on May 25 and a preliminary community vote that passed on June 10, according to Babylon Labs.
Under the proposal, Aave DAO would receive the first $500,000 in qualifying annual revenue generated by the integration.
Aave already supports loans against tokenized Bitcoin through tokens such as Wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) and Coinbase Wrapped Bitcoin (cbBTC). Wrapped tokens rely on custodians to hold the underlying Bitcoin, introducing counterparty risks.
As of Thursday, the proposal remains at the Aave Request for Comment (ARFC) stage, where it faces community feedback and risk analysis.
If community consensus is reached, it can proceed to a three-day offchain Snapshot vote, which requires at least 320,000 AAVE-equivalent votes in favor before advancing to a formal onchain vote, according to Aave’s governance rules.
The onchain vote must meet quorum and approval requirements.
Related: Aave launches V4 on Avalanche, laying groundwork for tokenized credit markets

articles.title: Zcash Tanks Double Digits After 'Meteoric Rise' Sees Leverage Build Up - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Privacy cryptocurrency Zcash has tanked 11% over the past 24 hours.
- Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, says this drop was likely caused by a build up in leverage after the token's "meteoric rise" in recent months.
- Another expert says that growing concerns that AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers might've prompted losses for Zcash.
Privacy-focused cryptocurrency Zcash has fallen 11% over the past 24 hours to a market capitalization of $18.5 billion, per Decrypt data, making it one of the biggest losers of the day.
One expert says this drop in valuation comes after its price has soared in recent months, which has led to a build up in leverage and amplified losses. Others say that growing concerns that AI can break cryptography faster than quantum computers are causing the privacy token to take bigger losses.
Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, highlighted that Zcash's "meteoric rise" means that it is still up 460% from its March lows and that in a "fragile" crypto market the largest gainers tend to take losses too.
"There was a decent build-up of leverage on the way up as this is also a natural consequence of a strong move," Nolan told Decrypt. "More attention brings more perp traders to take on leverage, and when there is a sneeze, the moves get amplified as those leveraged traders are either forced to reduce exposure or get liquidated."
Over the past 24 hours, per CoinGlass data, $17.9 million worth of Zcash long positions were liquidated, a large figure compared to Hyperliquid's $7.3 million over the same period.
The race to quantum-proof Zcash
The price drop comes as other industry-wide concerns start to swirl, some of which could see positive upside for Zcash.
Last week, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warned that the industry needs to plan for "bunker mode" as AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers do. The conversation was sparked after OpenAI published major progress in math, which presented concerns for the future of encryption.
"The OpenAI math breakthroughs has caused a lot concern in crypto given the conspicuous lack of cryptography proofs," Ryan Zurrer, founder and director of investment firm Dialectic, told Decrypt. "More complex privacy protocols such as Zcash have the most to lose in a zero-day event if core primitives are rendered obsolete against AI-driven cryptography attacks."
Zcash has been aggressive with its quest to quantum-proof the network. Zakura, a Zcash full node developer, recently said that its team expects to be quantum-proofed as well as reasonably AI-proofed by January. Its quantum-resistant roadmap "served as a key catalyst" for its recent rally, Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt. "Although actual implementation is still some distance away, it indeed reflects the market's continuous focus on the privacy sector since the beginning of this year."
Privacy continues to be a major crypto industry talking point. Sun added that as traditional finance continues to merge with the crypto industry, the need for privacy will continue to rise.
"As an increasing volume of traditional financial assets and operations migrate on-chain, privacy protection will no longer be merely an optional add-on," Sun told Decrypt, "but rather a fundamental prerequisite for financial institutions adopting blockchain technology."
Last week, French lawmakers progressed a law proposal that would require citizens to report crypto holdings equal to or above €100,000 ($112,000), or otherwise face a penalty. The proposed law received significant backlash in the wake of a wave of crypto-related "wrench attacks," robberies, and kidnappings across the country. Although the law hasn't passed yet, some have looked to privacy protocols as government oversight looms.
Nolan from CoinShares highlights that investors should zoom out when looking at Zcash's recent performance, pushing back on recent narratives pushing its price down.
"I think the French proposed law had little to do with the move, and in my view, it's simply a larger pullback given the meteoric rise," Nolan told Decrypt. "When you put the drawdown in context on the daily chart, even though it's been 35%+, it looks like a blip in comparison to the upmove."

articles.title: Ledger wants customers to trust its new $849 device as criminals compromise existing wallets
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Ledger introduced a $849 crypto device designed to detect physical tampering as criminals exploit hardware implants to steal customer funds.
- Chainalysis revealed that one of the theft's largest victims was an alleged scammer who lost over 60 BTC obtained through fraudulent online tasks.
- Ledger is tightening reseller controls as its new security technology awaits independent evaluation before the device's planned 2027 release.
Ledger unveiled an $849 crypto device with new anti-tamper protections as it investigated coordinated thefts involving modified hardware wallets.
On Oct. 15, the French crypto wallet maker introduced Ledger Atom, which is a mobile device that combines everyday apps with hardware-protected crypto transactions. The company is accepting refundable $100 deposits for a Founders Edition priced at $849, with deliveries targeted for 2027.
The launch coincides with Ledger's investigation into an organized criminal operation that secretly modified genuine hardware wallets before returning them to reseller distribution channels. The attackers allegedly captured customers' recovery phrases and used them to drain cryptocurrency holdings in a coordinated operation.
Ledger Atom
In a separate security announcement, Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet said Atom includes an active protective shield designed to detect attempts to physically open, probe, or modify the device's secure hardware.
The technology addresses a vulnerability exposed by the recent attacks, where malicious components reportedly intercepted information displayed during wallet setup without compromising Ledger's security chips or operating system.
Guillemet explained that existing Ledger devices use cryptographic authentication to verify the integrity of their secure software. However, that process cannot detect an additional component secretly monitoring the screen.
Atom's protective shield is designed to alert its Secure Element when someone disturbs the protected hardware, potentially detecting manipulation before a compromised device reaches a customer.
The device also represents Ledger's attempt to expand beyond conventional hardware wallets into a broader consumer electronics market. It combines an Android-based environment for everyday apps with a separate Ledger operating system that controls private keys and approves transactions.
During sensitive operations, the secure processor takes control of the display, preventing ordinary applications from interfering with the final approval process. Users can also physically disconnect the cameras and microphones through a dedicated privacy switch.
Atom supports 4G and 5G data connections but lacks conventional cellular calling and SMS capabilities, limiting its ability to replace a smartphone. Ledger is positioning the product for users who want integrated crypto management, digital identity services, and secure applications.
The company has also partnered with Solana Mobile to preload its Seeker application, giving Atom users access to the Solana decentralized application ecosystem.
Ledger tightens distribution controls
The new security measures come as Ledger confronts questions about the integrity of its existing distribution network.
In an Oct. 15 statement, the company said criminals spent months purchasing genuine devices, installing custom-built components, and returning the modified products to distribution through Southeast Asian resellers.
The operation involved dedicated infrastructure to collect stolen recovery phrases, transfer cryptocurrency, and launder proceeds, according to Ledger. The company said the attackers invested millions of dollars in preparing the operation before executing the thefts.
Ledger maintained that its internal systems, chips, and operating software remained secure, attributing the attacks to device manipulation after they left its control.
The investigation has prompted Ledger to ask authorized resellers and distributors across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to suspend sales. The company also examined devices purchased from stores and warehouse samples, reporting that the inspected units showed no signs of compromise.
Meanwhile, new blockchain intelligence has revealed an unusual victim of the thefts.
According to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, one of the largest victims was allegedly a scam operator who lost more than 60 Bitcoin, worth approximately $4.8 million, after accumulating the funds through a fraudulent online employment scheme.
The operation reportedly paid participants to create artificial sales and reviews for legitimate products. Victims were subsequently shown negative account balances and instructed to deposit their own money before receiving their promised earnings.
Chainalysis said the suspected operator transferred the proceeds to three separate Ledger addresses on Sept. 22. On Oct. 9, the operator emptied all three wallets through individual transactions, sending the Bitcoin to the same destination address, which investigators identified as holding stolen funds.
The discovery adds another layer to the investigation, linking proceeds from an alleged consumer fraud operation to the broader wallet theft. It also provides investigators with an identifiable trail of funds as Ledger works with law enforcement and blockchain security researchers to trace the attackers.
The security incident has already forced changes to Ledger's reseller operations. Authorized sellers have been reminded that they must never resell returned devices, regardless of their apparent condition. New requirements also prohibit displaying products on store shelves, while unusual customer reports must be escalated to the company.
Those restrictions could complicate retail distribution as Ledger prepares to introduce a substantially more expensive product to its existing customer base.

articles.title: South Korea Plans Cybersecurity Overhaul After Crypto Exchange Incidents
articles.text:
South Korea plans cybersecurity overhaul after attacks hit banks, crypto firms
South Korea is proposing tougher cybersecurity assessments after a review identified security deficiencies at 130 financial firms.
South Korea is planning tighter cybersecurity requirements for financial institutions after an investigation into earlier security incidents involving 16 companies, including crypto exchanges.
The Financial Services Commission (FSC) said it would pursue improved threat monitoring, more frequent security assessments and stronger accountability for executives after an industry-wide review found cybersecurity deficiencies at 130 of 555 financial companies.
The FSC said about 100,000 pieces of customer information had been exposed across the affected firms, including names, contact details and identification numbers.
The affected firms include Gopax operator Streami and crypto trading platform Prabang, which previously disclosed that an Oct. 2 hack exposed personal info of some customers.
Under the proposed reforms, larger financial institutions would undergo vulnerability assessments at least twice every year. The regulator also plans to enhance information-sharing systems and is considering artificial intelligence use in security monitoring for smaller companies.
The regulator is also considering allowing additional cybersecurity inspections outside regular assessment schedules when urgent threats emerge, as part of efforts to prevent future incidents.
The FSC said they are still investigating whether the incidents involved AI use or were linked to the same attackers.
Related: South Korea moves to block 27 crypto websites, including KuCoin, MEXC

articles.title: Morning Minute: Solana Is About To Get Faster - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors fall 3-5% after hot CPI; BTC at $80.9k
- Over $900M liquidated as crypto majors selloff; alts down 5-15%
- Solana sets Oct 21 for Alpenglow on mainnet
- Papertrade flips Circle in daily revenue with $7.5M
- Kalshi says state-level oversight would drive prediction markets offshore
🏎️ Solana Cuts Finality From 12.8 Seconds to 150 Milliseconds
Next Wednesday, Solana rips out the engine and drops in a new one while the car is doing 70 on the highway.
On October 21, around 15:00 UTC, Solana activates Alpenglow on mainnet, retiring the consensus mechanism it has run on since launch. Finality drops from roughly 12.8 seconds to a target of about 150 milliseconds – 85 times faster. Anza, the core dev shop behind it, called it “18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot.”
Finality is the moment a transaction stops being reversible, the point where you can hand over the goods knowing the payment can’t be clawed back. Solana has always felt instant, but there was a roughly 13-second window where a block could in theory still get dropped. Every exchange and payment processor has had to build around that window. Next week it closes.
The old system breaks if more than about a third of staked SOL turns hostile. The new one is built to survive 20% of stake acting maliciously plus another 20% simply offline, and keep finalizing. For a chain whose reputation was built on outages, that’s the number institutions will actually care about.
Now the part that’s going to cause trouble. Validators currently cast their votes as transactions on the chain. Under Alpenglow they vote directly to each other instead, which means Solana’s headline transaction count and TPS figures are about to fall off a cliff. Nothing real changes - same users, same volume, same apps - but the number everyone has quoted for years was mostly validators voting at each other. Expect a wave of “Solana activity collapses” posts next Wednesday from people reading a dashboard.
This is also just phase one of two, and the second piece has no date yet. And Solana has missed an Alpenglow date before - a September 28 activation was announced, then pushed. So, grains of salt.
But clearly Solana is focused on speed as one of its primary differentiators - and it’s about to get a lot faster…

Bitcoin miners plunge up to 13% in Wall Street’s worst selloff since July
TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Cipher Mining and IREN each lost more than 12% as hotter inflation hit AI infrastructure companies.
US stocks suffered their sharpest selloff since July on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected inflation data weighed on technology and AI infrastructure companies, with Bitcoin miners among those hit.
The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, its biggest one-day decline since July 29; the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%, its biggest one-day drop since July 23, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.1% over the day.
Leading decliners among major tech companies included data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16%, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, which fell 11%, and Oracle, which fell 9%.
Of the 23 AI infrastructure stocks tracked by PRISM’s AI Data Center and Infrastructure Index, 21 declined Wednesday, with an average loss of 7.46%.
Related: Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflation
The single-day dip extended to Bitcoin miners, several of which have also expanded into AI infrastructure. TeraWulf fell 12.64% over the day, while Core Scientific, Cipher Mining and IREN fell 12.44%, 12.35% and 12.2%, respectively. Riot Platforms, Bitdeer Technologies, MARA and CleanSpark also fell.
Higher interest rates could increase borrowing costs for AI infrastructure companies, many of which rely heavily on debt to finance data center expansion.
Hotter inflation triggers tech, crypto selloff
US consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6% and well above the Fed’s 2% target, with higher gasoline prices from the Middle East war to blame.
The inflation report also led to increased expectations of an October Federal Reserve interest-rate hike. The implied probability briefly exceeded 50% on Wednesday before retreating.
However, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly told Reuters that while further rate hikes were likely needed to bring inflation under control, there was no urgency to act this month.
“I don’t feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information. I think we have the time that we need,” Daly said.

articles.title: Quantum fixes protect Bitcoin, but legit owners risk lockout
articles.text:
Quick Take
- A modeled 50,000-output Bitcoin sweep fits a 10-block weight budget, assuming hypothetical key recovery and miner inclusion.
- Glassnode's May estimate measured 6.04 million BTC with exposed public keys, leaving permanent key loss and dormant ownership as separate questions.
- Draft sunsets, spending throttles and advance ownership proofs offer different protections, with recovery depending on holders' evidence and adoption.
Crypto investor Nic Carter's worst-case quantum scenario consists of a hostile actor recovering the keys to dormant Bitcoin, then broadcasting a wave of spends across 10 blocks.
In his Oct. 13 interview with Luke Martin, Carter says early coins moving together could shake confidence in the network.
The stakes extend beyond choosing stronger cryptography. Glassnode's May 20 analysis identified 6.04 million BTC, or 30.2% of then-issued supply, with public keys already exposed.
The scenario assumes a future quantum machine capable of breaking Bitcoin's key cryptography. Google's published research models future resources for such an attack, and Bitcoin key recovery remains undemonstrated in that work. Large early outputs can nevertheless make a rapid transfer possible on block-space grounds.
Can millions of BTC fit in 10 blocks?
A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could use Shor's algorithm to recover private keys from exposed public keys, gaining the ability to authorize spending. Early pay-to-public-key (P2PK) outputs reveal those keys directly.
An attacker could work privately, withholding transactions until ready, as Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 361 (BIP-361) explains.
Bitcoin tracks funds in individual unspent outputs, each with its own spending conditions, and a transfer's size depends on how many outputs it consumes and their type.
Consider an explicitly hypothetical set of 50,000 early outputs holding 50 BTC each, totaling 2.5 million BTC altogether. Using the Bitcoin developer reference's P2PK input example, those inputs require about 5.7 million bytes, equivalent to 22.8 million weight units before transaction overhead.
Ten blocks have an aggregate ceiling of 40 million weight units under Bitcoin's block-weight rules. With one compact receiving output per batch, the illustrative set fits beneath that ceiling, including overhead, when split into transactions below Bitcoin Core's 400,000-unit standard weight limit.
An actual sweep's block-space demand would depend on its particular outputs and spending requirements.
Fees, competing traffic, and miner decisions still determine inclusion. Confirmation follows only when miners include the transactions. With Bitcoin's approximately 10-minute block interval, 10 blocks average roughly 100 minutes, with substantial variation.
Glassnode's exposure measure includes active holdings whose keys became visible through earlier spending or address reuse, alongside structurally exposed outputs such as P2PK and Taproot.
Public-key exposure, holder inactivity and permanent key loss are separate questions, as is attribution to Satoshi Nakamoto.
In his May 21 analysis, security researcher Jameson Lopp estimated that about 2.6 million exposed BTC might be unable to migrate, using inactivity and known-entity labels as proxies.
A quantum sweep would transfer control of existing coins without creating additional issuance. A visible transfer could unsettle holders before a sale, while exchange responses and liquidity conditions would determine any subsequent market disruption.
Who could still prove Bitcoin ownership?
Keeping existing spending rules intact preserves the ability to spend with a valid key, including one a future attacker recovers. Restricting legacy signatures changes that bargain: owners who cannot migrate or meet rescue conditions could lose access.
Draft BIP-360 proposes Pay-to-Merkle-Root, a new output type without Taproot's exposed key spending path. It would reduce long-exposure risk when keys stay hidden.
BIP-361 proposed phases would restrict new vulnerable destinations about three years after activation, then tighten legacy-signature spending through rescue conditions about two years later.
For comparison, Google's 2029 target sets its own precautionary migration deadline.
One potential rescue relies on a parent secret in a wallet that uses hardened key derivation. An attacker recovering an individual spending key would ordinarily lack that additional secret. For bare P2PK outputs, the draft's authors describe that kind of ownership proof as an unresolved problem.
Dan Robinson's May 1 PACT concept explores advanced, private timestamps proving address control. Future rules could recognize that evidence after a legacy sunset, and its protection depends on the holder preparing before quantum key recovery becomes possible and preserving the proof, alongside standardization and adoption of future verification rules.
The February Hourglass V2 draft takes another approach: one P2PK spend and one BTC of net spending per block. Throttling would slow the outflow while constraining legitimate holders under the same rules.
These remain proposals and research concepts. Their trade-offs include continued exposure, restricted access, and unequal recovery options.
Under the BIP process, Bitcoin's participants evaluate and adopt proposed changes through software and ecosystem acceptance.
Carter's scenario brings the key choice into focus: safer destinations can protect holders who can move. Bitcoin's community would still have to decide which claims to recognize when an ordinary signature can no longer distinguish an original holder from a quantum attacker.
Bitcoin is +1.08% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

articles.title: Bitcoin Tests $81,000 as Rate Hike Fears Linger After Hot Inflation Data - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin dipped to an intraday low under $81,000, extending losses after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data revived bets on a Fed rate hike.
- HashKey's Tim Sun said slowing demand from spot ETFs and corporate Bitcoin treasuries explains the stalled rally more than macro factors alone.
- Algoz's Stephen Wundke expects Bitcoin to trade between $76,000 and $83,000 for the rest of October unless a clear catalyst emerges.
Bitcoin dipped below $81,000 on Thursday, extending its slide a day after U.S. consumer prices rose faster than expected and revived bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike.
The leading cryptocurrency is currently trading at $81,002, per CoinGecko data, down 2.7% over the past 24 hours and 2.5% over the past week, after slipping to an intraday low of $80,444.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% in the year to September, Decrypt reported on Wednesday. Prices rose 0.6% over the month, the largest monthly increase in five months, driven mainly by energy costs tied to the war with Iran, The New York Times reported.
Traders' odds of a Fed rate hike this month jumped to 43% from 24% after the report, the Times said, though federal funds futures still point to December for the next increase. The Fed raised rates to a range of 3.75% to 4% in September.
CME FedWatch put the odds of an October hike at 29.3% on Thursday, up from 17.7% a week earlier, while traders on prediction markets Myriad and Polymarket priced it at 28%. Polymarket traders put the chance of a December hike at 79%. (Disclosure: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt's parent company, Dastan.)
Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at quantitative investment firm Algoz, argued that those probabilities feed directly into Bitcoin's price. "On the bullish side as long as BTC stays above $79,500 we can keep the dream alive," Wundke told Decrypt.
Inflation has now run above the Fed's 2% target for 66 straight monthly readings, the longest streak this century, according to a CNBC analysis. "They're starting to accept high inflation as just a fact of life," Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wrote in a LinkedIn post last week.
Those pressures are only part of the picture, Tim Sun of HashKey Group told Decrypt. Rising rate hike expectations, a stronger dollar and a pullback in AI tech stocks have weighed on Bitcoin on the surface, he said, "however, the deeper reason lies in the changing structure of incremental capital."
"Over the last two years, the key marginal buyers of Bitcoin primarily came from spot ETFs and corporate Bitcoin treasuries," Sun said. As borrowing costs rise, narrowing valuation premiums at some corporate treasuries have made it less attractive to raise money to keep buying Bitcoin, he added.
"Nevertheless, Bitcoin has not experienced a sustained deep sell-off as a result," Sun said, pointing to growing involvement from major traditional banks that has added long-term capital to the market.
Bitcoin's trading range
Sun expects Bitcoin to stay range-bound in the short term. A breakout depends on whether ETF flows return to sustained net inflows and whether corporate treasuries can improve their ability to raise money and buy, he said.
Wundke also expects a range. "Without a clear catalyst to move things higher I fear we are range bound with BTC between $76,000 and $83,000 for the rest of October," he said, adding that peace with Iran "would change that dynamic instantly."
"In the short term Bitcoin trades as a liquidity asset, and higher for longer means tighter liquidity, so this drop is the market repricing rates, not a change in Bitcoin's story," Abdul Rafay Gadit, co-founder of ZIG Finance, told Decrypt.
"The next few weeks are about the Fed, not crypto," Gadit said. "If it signals it can look through sticky inflation, risk appetite returns quickly; if not, expect choppy trading."
The Fed will announce its next rate decision on October 28.

articles.title: Two firms control corporate Bitcoin buys, even as business adoption broadens
articles.text:
Quick Take
- River’s Oct. 5 snapshot puts Strategy and Strive’s holdings additions above net business growth, showing concentrated accumulation.
- Strive bought 2,822 BTC during Oct. 12-13, while separately reporting $369.2 million in expected gross warrant proceeds.
- Strategy spent $192.4 million on STRC buybacks and $21.5 million on Bitcoin during Oct. 5-11, highlighting competing capital uses.
Bitcoin treasury company Strive bought 2,822 BTC during Oct. 12-13, according to a filing released Oct. 14. The purchase adds fresh demand from one of the two firms dominating this year’s reported corporate accumulation.
The update follows River’s Oct. 8 business-adoption report, which put Strategy and Strive’s combined 2026 holdings additions at 197,000 BTC. That exceeded the 193,000 BTC net increase River reported for businesses overall in charts dated Oct. 5.
Strive’s new purchase accompanies a separate financing disclosure. Meanwhile, Strategy reported buying Bitcoin while spending more on repurchasing preferred shares. Both cases show why an expanding roster of corporate holders does not automatically create an equally broad source of new buying.
River’s category chart shows conventional businesses adding about 20,000 BTC and other Bitcoin treasury companies adding about 8,000 BTC in 2026 through Oct. 5, with River’s text reporting 32,800 BTC sold by large miners.
The roughly 4,000 BTC separating those figures cannot be read as a direct measure of market selling by everyone else. Positive additions in some categories coexist with reductions in another, and the displayed totals are rounded.
River also reports a 10% increase over the past year in the number of public companies holding Bitcoin.
For demand to diversify, purchases outside the leading treasury firms would need to carry more weight. A growing holder count measures the spread of ownership; repeated purchases by a wider group would demonstrate a broader source of demand.
Purchases compete with other uses of capital
Strive’s Oct. 14 filing records that the company bought 2,822 BTC during Oct. 12-13 at an average price of approximately $83,266 per coin, including fees and expenses.
For the same two days, it separately reported warrant exercises expected to generate $369.2 million in gross proceeds. It said no traditional warrants issued in its private investment in public equity transaction remained outstanding at the Oct. 13 close.
Those statements do not show that all expected proceeds settled as cash, how much remained after costs, or that those proceeds funded the concurrent purchase.
The absence of remaining traditional PIPE warrants changes that particular financing channel without establishing the size or funding of Strive’s next purchase. The financing disclosure describes a source of capital, subject to the limits of expected gross proceeds.
That latest purchase follows a separate window covered by Strive’s Oct. 13 disclosure. That earlier update reported buying 3,311 BTC during Oct. 5-9 and holding 32,773 BTC as of Oct. 9. It also recorded $310.3 million in cash and equivalents on that date, alongside increases in reported common and preferred share counts.
Strategy’s Oct. 12 capital update makes the funding link explicit for its Bitcoin purchases. During Oct. 5-11, it bought 250 BTC for $21.5 million, bringing holdings to 848,250 BTC on Oct. 11.
Of that purchase amount, $21 million came from net proceeds of MSTR common-share sales and $500,000 from dollars. In the same reporting period, Strategy spent $192.4 million repurchasing 1,932,145 STRC preferred shares.
The repurchases were not Bitcoin purchases, and the release did not identify their specific funding source, so the figures do not establish that Strategy sold Bitcoin to pay for the buybacks, or that every dollar spent on STRC otherwise would have bought Bitcoin.
Buying back preferred stock returns funds to the holders of those securities, while acquiring Bitcoin adds coins to the treasury. Both can occur in the same week without implying the same demand in the Bitcoin market.
As of Oct. 11, Strategy held $4.88 billion in its USD Reserve intended to support preferred dividends and debt interest, alongside $640.5 million of cash for broader treasury uses.
Merger transfers complicate the demand measure
Strive’s acquisition of Semler Scientific earlier in 2026 illustrates the difference between growth in one issuer’s holdings and fresh buying across the business sector.
The companies’ Jan. 13 shareholder-approval announcement identified 5,048.1 BTC already held by Semler as part of the all-stock transaction. It also reported Strive’s purchase of 123 BTC, which brought Strive’s holdings to 7,749.8 BTC before the acquisition.
The Jan. 16 closing announcement confirmed that the acquisition had completed and put combined holdings at approximately 12,797.9 BTC. The acquired Semler coins enlarged Strive’s consolidated treasury, but their transfer did not represent another purchase of those coins from the market.
River’s published report and category chart do not explain how its Strategy-and-Strive figure treats the Semler transaction. That leaves no basis for mechanically deducting 5,048.1 BTC from either reported total, or for presenting a precise, merger-adjusted percentage of fresh buying.
An exact share of fresh buying requires separating purchases and sales from coins transferred between corporate owners. River’s figures establish reported holdings concentration while leaving that transaction-level calculation unresolved.
The two firms’ recent disclosures cover different purchase windows, both extending beyond River’s Oct. 5 snapshot. Adding them to that snapshot would require a new, consistently dated sector account.
For subsequent demand, the useful signals are completed purchases, financing that becomes available cash, and management’s allocation of that cash. Evidence of larger purchases across other businesses would strengthen the case for a broader corporate bid.
Until then, a growing roster of Bitcoin owners and a diversified source of fresh buying remain different propositions.

articles.title: Australia Proposes Capital, Custody Rules for Crypto
articles.text:
Australia seeks feedback on crypto platform rules ahead of 2027 rollout
The consultation follows Parliament’s passage of digital asset legislation in April, with Australia’s securities regulator now proposing capital, custody and trading standards for crypto platforms.
Update (Oct. 15 at 5:35 am UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Liam Hennessy, partner at Thomsons.
Update (Oct. 15 at 11:44 pm UTC): Added comment from Steven Pettigrove, partner at Piper Alderman.
Australia’s securities regulator opened consultation Thursday on proposed capital, custody and trading requirements for crypto platforms, as it prepares to implement legislation passed in April that expands oversight of the industry.
The proposals include three alternative capital models, restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and quarterly reporting of wallets holding customer assets. ASIC also proposes allowing offshore custody while seeking feedback on safeguards if an overseas parent or related company fails.
“Our proposed guidance and standards acknowledge the increasing role of digital assets and tokenization, including in traditional parts of the financial system,” said ASIC Commissioner Alan Kirkland.
The proposed guidance and standards would give crypto operators greater clarity on requirements to obtain a license, safeguard customer assets and meet financial requirements under the new framework. The consultation follows Parliament’s passage of the Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act earlier this year.
“ASIC’s release of CP 392 is an important milestone for Australia’s digital asset industry,” Amy-Rose Goodey, CEO of the Digital Economy Council of Australia, told Cointelegraph. “After years of engagement on regulatory reform, it’s encouraging to see the focus shift towards practical implementation.”
OKX Australia CEO Shane Chandra also welcomed the proposals, saying they could drive industry consolidation.
“These standards are appropriately onerous,” he told Cointelegraph. “They will reward operators who have already invested in compliance, capital and custody. They will challenge operators who have waited to make that investment.”
Capital, custody and trading rules in focus
ASIC is weighing three alternative capital models, including one requiring operators without qualifying third-party custody arrangements to hold at least 14 million Australian dollars ($9.7 million) in net tangible assets or 10% of average revenue, whichever is greater.
“We’ll be working closely with our members to examine the three proposed capital models in considerable detail, particularly their proportionality across businesses of different sizes and the concessions available for third-party custody,” Goodey said.
Steven Pettigrove, a partner at Piper Alderman, said the proposed financial requirements would favor scale and established custody providers.
“The proposed NTA requirements for DAPs will encourage scale and established custodians,” Pettigrove told Cointelegraph.
“From our perspective, it is not at all contentious that this level of resourcing and care should be taken when clients entrust you with their assets,” said Chandra.
The regulator has also proposed allowing offshore custody, while seeking feedback on whether Australian operators should have emergency access to private keys if the overseas parent or related company fails.
Related: Australia warns unlicensed crypto firms of fines up to 10% of annual turnover
“The proposal not to mandate domestic custody is also significant, recognizing the global nature of digital asset markets,” Goodey said.
Operators would also have to report custody wallet structures and addresses to ASIC quarterly and retain relevant records for seven years.
Thomsons partner Liam Hennessy said the reporting proposal partly reflected the Australian market’s reliance on offshore infrastructure — as global competition means that digital assets are usually held offshore.
ASIC also proposes restrictions on platforms trading for their own account and accepting benefits to favor particular tokens, targeting potential conflicts of interest. Hennessy said this could test existing trading models.
“Under ASIC’s proposal, an order matching DAP (one that brings client orders together, by order book or by matched principal trading) could not trade as principal on its own platform, and its related bodies corporate could not trade as principal through it,” he said. “There are model-specific exceptions. Groups that rely on an affiliated market maker should look at this first.”
The consultation forms part of ASIC’s 18-month implementation roadmap, published after the Digital Assets Framework Act was passed in April.
Feedback is due Nov. 27, with ASIC aiming to publish final standards and guidance in March 2027. The law is set to take effect on April 8, 2027, and operators will have until Oct. 7, 2027, to apply for the relevant license and can operate while ASIC assesses their applications.

articles.title: Brooklyn Prosecutors Take Down 112 Servers Behind Crypto Scam Targeting Russian Speakers - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The Brooklyn District Attorney's Virtual Currency Unit, working with the FBI, disrupted 112 servers and 241 web domains used in a crypto investment scam.
- The operation targeted Russian-speaking Americans through Facebook ads, and prosecutors estimate it stole tens of millions of dollars, some of it victims' entire life savings.
- Prosecutors have seized about $300,000 in stolen funds so far and say they are working to recover more.
Brooklyn prosecutors have dismantled the online infrastructure of a multinational crypto investment scam that targeted Russian speakers in the U.S., seizing and disrupting 241 web domains and 112 servers, District Attorney Eric Gonzalez announced on Wednesday.
The office's Virtual Currency Unit carried out search warrants and other enforcement actions across three time zones last week, working with the FBI. The servers were hosted by Eastern European and American companies, and the scammers relied on infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, according to the release.
"These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money," Gonzalez said.
A large cluster of victims in Brooklyn had each responded to a Russian-language Facebook ad for investment opportunities and then received a call from an "investment advisor" who coached them into opening an account on a crypto investment website, the office said.
With the advisor's help, victims bought crypto and sent it to addresses linked to the platforms. When they tried to withdraw after weeks or months of "investing," they were locked out or told to pay additional fees and taxes.
Data from the seized servers showed the scammers also ran a recovery scam, contacting victims a few weeks after the initial fraud and promising to get their stolen assets back, the DA's office said.
Brooklyn's Virtual Currency Unit
The unit had been investigating the operation for three years. Brooklyn's large Russian-speaking population meant the scam hit the borough's residents disproportionately, according to the release.
Before last week, the unit had already seized or disrupted 400 domains linked to the fraud, but new scam websites kept appearing. Taking down the servers removes the scammers' ability to quickly create new sites and contact existing victims, the office said.
Prosecutors estimate that tens of millions of dollars were stolen in the scheme. The office has seized about $300,000 so far and is working to claw back more.
The takedown is not the Brooklyn DA's only recent crypto fraud case. Its prosecutors previously charged a local man who stole $16 million from nearly 100 Coinbase users through a phishing scheme. He was sentenced to up to 12 years in prison.
