articles.title: Bão "cyclone", bão "typhoon" và bão "tropical storm" có gì khác biệt?
articles.text:
Khi theo dõi thông tin về các cơn bão lớn trên thế giới, chúng ta thường thấy những cụm từ này. Vậy, chúng có gì khác biệt?
Mô hình GFS của Mỹ là mô hình Hệ thống dự báo bão toàn cầu được điều hành bởi Dịch vụ thời tiết quốc gia dự đoán hướng đi của các cơn bão. Nó sử dụng một siêu máy tính để chạy dữ liệu thông qua một thuật toán phức tạp được lấy từ vệ tinh, đài quan sát và bóng bay thời tiết.
Hình ảnh vệ tinh cơn bão Michael 2018 tại Mỹ.
Hành trình bão là diễn biến về vị trí và cường độ của bão trong suốt thời gian của nó. Cách theo dõi tốt nhất bao gồm vĩ độ, kinh độ, sức gió bề mặt tối đa của hệ thống bão và áp suất mực nước biển tối thiểu trong khoảng thời gian sáu giờ, dựa trên đánh giá sau bão của tất cả các dữ liệu có sẵn.
Mô hình châu Âu được các nhà khí tượng học coi là mô hình chính xác nhất để dự đoán bão ở giữa vĩ độ. Trung tâm dự báo thời tiết tầm trung châu Âu (ECMWF) phát triển mô hình, phát triển phương pháp tích hợp dữ liệu khí tượng của thời gian thực vào thuật toán của họ (vì vậy nó bắt đầu với điều kiện ban đầu chính xác hơn) và đầu tư vào phần cứng máy tính tiên tiến . Cả hai mô hình châu Âu và Mỹ đều là các mô hình toán học dự đoán, vì vậy chúng không nhất thiết phản ánh con đường bão do Trung tâm bão quốc gia ban hành.
Thành mắt bão là chùm hoặc vòng mây dông (Cumulonimbus) bao quanh mắt của cơn bão. Mức độ cực đoan của cơn bão được thể hiện trong thành mắt bão: Sấm chớp, mưa lớn và gió giật.
Hiệu ứng Fujiwhara xảy ra khi hai xoáy thuận (cyclone) nhiệt đới quay quanh nhau.
Một cơn bão là một cơn xoáy thuận nhiệt đới với sức gió tối đa 74 dặm/ giờ (119km/h).
Các loại bão là một hệ thống quy ước đặt tên. Bão được phân loại thành năm cấp độ dựa trên cường độ gió duy trì của chúng, được gọi là Thang bão Saffir-Simpson.
Ảnh vệ tinh một cơn bão.
Cảnh báo bão là một thông báo rằng các điều kiện bão (tốc độ gió duy trì từ 119 km/h trở lên) được dự đoán xảy ra ở đâu đó trong khu vực quy định liên quan đến bão nhiệt đới.
Xác định cơn bão là một thông báo rằng các điều kiện bão (tốc độ gió duy trì từ 119km/h trở lên) có khả năng xảy ra trong một khu vực cụ thể liên quan đến bão nhiệt đới.
Ẩn nhiệt là nhiệt độ cần thiết để chuyển hóa chất rắn thành chất lỏng hoặc hơi ẩm mà không làm thay đổi nhiệt độ của nó. Khi hơi nước ngưng tụ tạo thành mây, nhiệt ẩn (năng lượng) được giải phóng, giúp các cơn bão tăng cường bằng cách làm ấm không khí xung quanh và gây ra gây nhiễu động.
Nếu một cơn bão từ cấp 3 trở lên, nó được coi là một cơn bão lớn.
Tốc độ gió duy trì tối đa là thước đo tiêu chuẩn về cường độ của xoáy thuận nhiệt đới. Nó đề cập đến tốc độ gió trung bình cao nhất trong một phút (ở độ cao 10 mét với phơi sáng không bị cản trở) liên quan đến hệ thống thời tiết đó tại một thời điểm cụ thể.
Gió mùa không phải là một cơn bão, mà là sự dịch chuyển gió theo mùa, quy mô lớn trên một khu vực kèm theo những thay đổi lớn theo mùa trong lượng mưa.
Bán kính của mức gió tối đa là khoảng cách từ trung tâm của một xoáy thuận nhiệt đới đến vị trí có tốc độ gió tối đa của vòng xoáy thuận. Trong các cơn bão phát triển mạnh, bán kính của mức gió tối đa thường ở cạnh bên trong của thành mắt bão.
Mức nước biển dâng sau bão là sự gia tăng mực nước biển sau một cơn bão hoặc cơn lốc lớn, lúc mực nước biển quan sát được có chiều cao khác biệt với mực nước lúc không có bão. Mức nước biển dâng sau bão được ước tính bằng lấy mức nước biển đo được sau bão trừ đi lượng triều cường bình thường.
Xoáy thuận nhiệt đới là một thuật ngữ chung cho các hệ thống bão xảy ra trên các luồng nước ấm nhiệt đới, như bão nhiệt đới, cơn lốc biển ở Đại Tây Dương, biển Caribbe, vùng trung tâm và đông bắc Thái Bình Dương; và bão ở Tây bắc Thái Bình Dương. Xoáy thuận nhiệt có một điểm trung tâm được xác định rõ, và hướng gió xoay ngược chiều kim đồng hồ ở Bắc bán cầu và xoay thuận chiều kim đồng hồ ở Nam bán cầu.
Một áp thấp nhiệt đới là một cơn bão nhiệt đới với tốc độ gió duy trì tối đa dưới 39 dặm một giờ (62 km/h).
Một cơn bão nhiệt đới là một xoáy thuận nhiệt đới với tốc độ gió duy trì tối đa giữa 39 và 73 dặm/giờ (62-117km/h).
Bão "typhoon" là một xoáy thuận nhiệt đới được hình thành ở biển Thái Bình Dương, nằm giữa khoảng 180-100 độ Đông, với sức gió lớn hơn 119 km/h. Typhoon là hiện tượng thời tiết giống với bão, khác biệt duy nhất là nơi mà nó hình thành.
Hurricane là từ được sử dụng để nói về những cơn lốc biển ở Đại Tây Dương, biển Caribe, vùng trung tâm và đông bắc Thái Bình Dương. Ở tây bắc Thái Bình Dương, những cơn bão có sức mạnh tương đương được gọi là typhoon.
Trong khi đó, nam Thái Bình Dương và Ấn Độ Dương sử dụng thuật ngữ chung là tropical cyclone, bất kể sức gió và thời tiết.
Các cơn bão ban đầu được hình thành dưới dạng áp thấp nhiệt đới, và khi chúng mạnh lên để có sức gió duy trì tối đa vào khoảng 63 km/h, chúng sẽ trở thành những xoáy thuận nhiệt đới. Các xoáy thuận nhiệt đới ở Bắc bán cầu quay theo hướng ngược chiều kim đồng hồ, trong khi các xoáy thuận ở Nam bán cầu quay theo chiều kim đồng hồ.
Nếu sức gió mạnh nhất đạt ngưỡng 119km/h, nó sẽ được phân loại thành typhoon hoặc hurricane.
Bão nhiệt đới thường tồn tại lâu và được đặt tên để có thể nhận diện một cách nhanh chóng.
Cơn bão đầu tiên của năm sẽ mang một cái tên bắt đầu bằng chữ A, ví dụ như bão Alice. Bão tiếp theo có một cái tên bắt đầu bằng chữ B.
Các nhà khoa học tổ chức họp để quyết định danh sách tên mới cho các trận bão của năm tiếp theo.
Tên các trận bão gây nhiều thiệt hại sẽ không bao giờ được sử dụng nữa.

articles.title: Scientists find a surprising genetic twist behind octopus intelligence
articles.text:
Scientists find a surprising genetic twist behind octopus intelligence
Researchers uncovered an ancient DNA reshuffling that may help explain how octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish evolved their extraordinary intelligence.
- Date:
- October 12, 2026
- Source:
- University of Vienna
- Summary:
- The remarkable intelligence of octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish may trace back to an ancient reshuffling of their DNA that created new connections between genes. Scientists discovered that these changes in the genome's 3D structure may have helped drive the evolution of their unusually complex nervous systems.
- Share:
Octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish possess some of the most sophisticated nervous systems in the animal kingdom, giving them remarkable abilities such as solving problems and rapidly changing their appearance to blend into their surroundings. But how did these extraordinary capabilities evolve? Scientists have uncovered a surprising clue that may lie not in the genes themselves, but in the way DNA is folded and arranged inside cells.
Researchers at the University of Vienna discovered that a massive reorganization of DNA hundreds of millions of years ago brought previously separated genetic regions into contact. These newly formed connections changed how genes could interact and be controlled, potentially helping drive the evolution of the unusually complex nervous systems found in these animals, which are collectively known as coleoid cephalopods.
The findings, published in Nature Communications, suggest that the physical structure of DNA may play a much more active role in evolution than scientists once thought.
How the 3D Structure of DNA Influences Evolution
To investigate this possibility, the research team reconstructed the three-dimensional organization of the genome in octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish. They then compared the arrangement of DNA with patterns of gene activity to understand how changes in genome structure might influence biological complexity.
"The genome isn't just a sequence of genes. It's folded into a complex three-dimensional structure," said lead author Dr. Thea Rogers. "Understanding how that structure evolves is becoming increasingly important for understanding how new forms of biological complexity arise."
Although DNA is often pictured as a long, twisted ladder, it does not simply stretch out inside a cell. Instead, it folds into an intricate three-dimensional arrangement, allowing sections that are far apart along the DNA sequence to come into close physical contact.
These connections matter because they can influence which genes are activated, when they are used, and how strongly they function. Changes in the way DNA folds can therefore alter gene activity without necessarily changing the underlying genetic instructions.
An Ancient DNA Reshuffling Created New Genetic Connections
The researchers found evidence that cephalopod genomes underwent an extensive period of reorganization hundreds of millions of years ago. During this evolutionary upheaval, large sections of genetic material were rearranged, bringing regions of chromosomes that had previously been separated into close proximity.
This reshuffling created opportunities for DNA regions to interact in ways that had not previously been possible. Once these connections formed, they could influence each other's activity, gradually establishing more elaborate networks of genetic regulation.
Over evolutionary time, the interactions could become increasingly interconnected and difficult to separate, creating a process the scientists describe as "regulatory entanglement."
This mechanism offers a possible explanation for how evolution can produce new biological features without disrupting the essential functions organisms need to survive. By establishing new connections among existing genetic elements, the genome may develop different patterns of gene activity while keeping crucial biological systems intact.
Stable DNA Structures and Flexible Genetic Loops
One of the study's most revealing findings was that different parts of the genome responded very differently to evolutionary reorganization.
The researchers discovered that large structural regions called chromatin domains remained remarkably stable over long periods of evolutionary history. These domains help organize DNA into broad sections within the cell, and their persistence suggests that some features of genome architecture are strongly conserved.
Smaller structures known as chromatin loops, however, told a different story.
These loops form when distant sections of DNA are brought together in three-dimensional space. Unlike the relatively stable chromatin domains, the loops showed substantial differences between cephalopod species, between tissues, and across stages of development.
Particularly intriguing was their location. Many of these flexible DNA connections appeared near genes associated with important cephalopod characteristics, including the development and function of the nervous system.
This pattern suggests that smaller, more adaptable structures within the genome may be especially responsive to major genetic rearrangements. By changing which regions of DNA can communicate, these flexible connections could help generate new patterns of gene activity and contribute to the evolution of complex traits.
A New Clue to the Evolution of Octopus Intelligence
The discovery challenges a traditional view of genome architecture as something that primarily changes in response to evolution. Instead, the findings suggest that the physical organization of DNA can itself influence how evolutionary changes unfold.
In octopuses, squid, and cuttlefish, ancient rearrangements of the genome may have helped establish new regulatory networks that contributed to the development of their exceptionally sophisticated nervous systems.
The results do not establish that these DNA changes directly caused the evolution of cephalopod intelligence. However, they reveal a potential mechanism through which large genetic rearrangements could create new biological possibilities while preserving essential functions.
More broadly, the research points to an often overlooked dimension of evolution. The emergence of extraordinary traits may depend not only on which genes an organism inherits, but also on how those genes are physically arranged and connected within the cell.

Những chiếc cầu thang này không dành cho người sợ độ cao.
Bức ảnh selfie đòi hỏi sự can đảm.
Đứng vững được trên chiếc cầu thang này đã là một thành công.
Vừa bước đi vừa cầu nguyện.
Chiếc cầu thang không dành cho người chân ngắn?
Những căn hộ phía trên có mở cửa toang hoác cũng chẳng tên nào dám mò lên chiếc cầu thang này mà ăn trộm.

Người dám trèo lên chiếc thang này hẳn đã gạt bỏ mọi khái niệm về sự nguy hiểm.
Hãy thầm cầu mong đừng có cơn gió lớn nào thổi qua khi bước trên chiếc thang này.
Phải chăng chiếc thang này là đường dẫn "lên trời"?

articles.title: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
articles.text:
Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
Scientists have uncovered a surprising link between popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs and nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation.
- Date:
- October 12, 2026
- Source:
- Beyond
- Summary:
- Popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs, such as Ozempic and Wegovy, have been linked to unexpectedly high rates of nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation, with some problems occurring several times more frequently among users. Researchers found that weight loss alone could not fully explain the differences, suggesting there may be more to these overlooked symptoms.
- Share:
Popular GLP-1 medications used for weight loss and type 2 diabetes (such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound, Victoza, and Trulicity) have been linked to an unexpected problem involving fingernails. A multinational study found that people taking these drugs were more than four times as likely to report nail detachment, a condition in which the nail separates from the skin underneath it.
Researchers found that 39% of GLP-1 users experienced nail detachment, compared with just 9% of people who had never taken the medications. Nail discoloration was also considerably more common, and two-thirds (66%) of users reported at least one nail disorder.
The findings, presented at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Congress 2026, come from the first controlled study to investigate the possible relationship between GLP-1 medications and nail health.
Unexpected Nail Problems Among GLP-1 Users
GLP-1 receptor agonists have become increasingly popular for managing obesity and type 2 diabetes. These medications act on a hormone signaling system that helps regulate blood sugar and appetite, making them effective tools for improving metabolic health and supporting weight loss.
However, scientists are still investigating their potential effects on other parts of the body. Until recently, information about nail changes during GLP-1 treatment came primarily from individual reports of possible adverse reactions, rather than controlled comparisons.
To investigate the connection, researchers examined 575 people using GLP-1 medications and compared them with 1,329 individuals who had type 2 diabetes and/or obesity but had never used the drugs. Participants were recruited from France, the United States, Brazil, and Mexico.
The results revealed a consistent pattern. Overall, 66% of GLP-1 users reported at least one nail disorder, compared with 53% of the control group. Nail discoloration showed an especially large difference, affecting 46% of users versus 17% of nonusers.
Nail detachment was even more striking, with reports more than four times as common among those taking GLP-1 medications.
Weight Loss Alone May Not Explain the Nail Changes
One important question was whether the nail problems might simply be related to weight loss, rather than to the medications themselves. Rapid changes in body weight can affect nutrition and other physiological processes, potentially influencing nail and hair health.
However, the researchers found that weight loss did not fully account for the differences. Even when they limited their analysis to participants who had lost weight, GLP-1 users continued to report significantly more nail problems than those who had not used the medications.
"Until now, nail changes associated with GLP-1 therapies had essentially been anecdotal," said study author Dr. Charles Taïeb. "Our findings show a clear association, but they also underline an important point: not everything that happens during GLP-1 treatment is necessarily caused by the treatment itself."
The researchers emphasized that their findings do not prove that GLP-1 drugs cause nail disorders. Approximately half of the medication users said they had experienced nail problems even before beginning treatment.
When the researchers accounted for existing skin conditions and nutritional deficiencies, some of the differences between the groups became smaller. Nevertheless, nail detachment and discoloration remained approximately two to three times more common among GLP-1 users after these adjustments.
Scientists Also Find Higher Rates of Hair Loss and Scalp Problems
The unexpected findings were not limited to fingernails.
A companion study examining the same participants identified significant differences in hair and scalp health among people taking GLP-1 medications.
Half of GLP-1 users reported unusual hair loss, compared with 34% of nonusers. Reduced hair volume or density was also substantially more common, affecting 42% of users versus 19% of the control group.
Researchers additionally examined hair loss that began after treatment started. This was reported by 26% of GLP-1 users, compared with 12% of nonusers, making it more than twice as common in the medication group.
Scalp redness was approximately three times more frequent among GLP-1 users.
A particularly interesting finding was that hair loss rarely appeared by itself. Most users who reported shedding also experienced other scalp symptoms, including itching, redness or flaking skin.
These accompanying symptoms raised the possibility that inflammation could be contributing to the changes, rather than the hair loss being explained entirely by rapid weight reduction.
"This suggests that what is happening on the scalp may go beyond the classical shedding seen after rapid weight loss and involve an inflammatory component," explained study author Dr. Bruno Halioua. "Scalp inflammation was the rule rather than the exception, which clinicians do not currently look for and which may be treatable. Taken together, our findings suggest that factors beyond weight loss alone may contribute to the hair, scalp and nail changes observed among GLP-1 users."
What the Findings Mean for People Taking GLP-1 Drugs
Despite the relatively high frequency of reported symptoms, the researchers stressed that the findings should encourage awareness rather than alarm.
"These changes are frequent, usually benign, and are not a reason to stop an effective treatment on one's own initiative," he said. "Anyone who notices hair shedding, an itchy or red scalp or nail changes should mention it to their doctor rather than discontinue therapy."
There are also important limitations to consider. Both investigations were cross-sectional studies, meaning they examined participants' experiences without following them over time to establish how symptoms developed. The findings also relied on symptoms reported by participants rather than standardized clinical examinations.
As a result, the studies can reveal patterns and associations, but they cannot determine whether GLP-1 medications directly caused the reported nail, hair, or scalp problems.
To investigate these questions more thoroughly, the research team plans to conduct prospective studies that follow patients from the beginning of treatment. These investigations will include standardized skin, hair and nail examinations along with biological monitoring.
The goal is to establish when the changes first appear, identify the mechanisms behind them, and determine whether they improve or disappear over time.
The research received institutional support from DUCRAY Laboratories (Pierre Fabre Group), a company specializing in dermatological and hair care products developed to help manage skin and scalp conditions and improve quality of life.

articles.title: Độc lạ loài bò lớn nhất thế giới ở Việt Nam: Nặng tới 2 tấn, mang nguồn gene quý hiếm
articles.text:
Loài bò này mang nhiều đặc tính quý và được coi là một nguồn gene hiếm cần được bảo tồn.
Theo Báo Công an nhân dân, từ những năm 2009 đến đầu năm 2015 tại thôn Bạc Rây 2 (xã Phước Bình, huyện Bác Ái, tỉnh Ninh Thuận) là vùng đệm vườn quốc gia Phước Bình, có một con bò đực thường xuyên xuất hiện mùa mưa tầm tháng 6 đến tháng 9, nhập đàn bò nhà của nông dân và kiếm ăn chung trên cánh đồng cỏ ven rừng. Con bò đực này cao khoảng 1,7m, dài hơn 2m, nặng khoảng 1 tấn.
Con bò đực hoang dã nhập vào đàn bò của người dân được nhận định là loài bò tót Đông Nam Á. (Ảnh: VTC News)
Thân mình con bò màu đen, từng khối cơ nổi lên, bốn chân trắng, nó không có cục u trên lưng như bò nhà mà có hẳn một sống cơ nổi lên chạy dài dọc sống lưng. Nó có cặp sừng to, cong vút, mút sừng nhọn hoắt vươn ra phía trước. Người cho rằng đó là trâu rừng, có ý kiến lại bảo phải là bò hoang mới đúng. Sau đó cán bộ kiểm lâm tới quan sát và nhận dạng thì nó đích thị là bò tót.
Bò tót Đông Nam Á là loài bò mang nhiều đặc tính quý hiếm. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Theo báo cáo của nhóm chuyên gia tới nghiên cứu, con bò tót đực này thuộc nhóm bò tót Đông Nam Á (Bos gaurus), rất hung dữ. Độ hung hãn chỉ đứng sau loài hổ. Bò tót sẵn sàng tấn công nếu phát hiện nơi ẩn nấp của thợ săn. Chúng luôn phản kháng đến cùng khi cảm thấy bị đe dọa. Là loài thú hung dữ, có vóc dáng khổng lồ nên bò tót hầu như không có thiên địch. Trên đồng cỏ vùng Bạc Rây, bò tót đực trở thành bá chủ và chinh phục đàn bò nhà giống cái.
Loại bò này còn được gọi là bò rừng Mã Lai hay bò rừng bison Ấn Độ, trên thực tế, chúng không hề có quan hệ gần gũi với loài bò rừng bison ở châu Âu và Bắc Mỹ.
Tại Việt Nam, loài bò tót Đông Nam Á được người dân tộc thiểu số gọi là con min. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Theo VTV, tại Việt Nam, bò tót Đông Nam Á được người dân tộc thiểu số gọi là con min, nghĩa là trâu rừng, do có hình dáng tương tự loài trâu. Nhìn ở đằng trước, chúng giống như trâu và ở phía sau lại giống như bò. Bò tót sống thành đàn từ 2 đến 10 cá thể. Những con bò đực già thường sống đơn độc hoặc hợp với nhau thành từng nhóm nhỏ.
Bộ lông ngắn mềm mượt màu nâu thẫm hoặc đen xám hơi phớt xanh bóng ở lưng. Lông ở bụng dài màu nâu nhạt. Con cái thường có màu hung đỏ. Đuôi dài màu đen.
Loài bò tót này nhìn ở đằng trước, chúng giống như trâu và ở phía sau lại giống như bò. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Bò tót thích ăn lá non, mầm tre non, cỏ non mới mọc ở nương rẫy hoặc các khu vực giáp ranh với rừng. Bò tót Đông Nam Á được các chuyên gia động vật học trên thế giới công nhận là một loài bò rừng lớn nhất trên thế giới. Một con bò đực trưởng thành có thể cao trên 2 mét và nặng tới 2 tấn, to lớn hơn cả trâu rừng châu Á và bò rừng ở Bắc Mỹ. Với kích thước này, bò tót là loài thú lớn thứ 3 về chiều cao, chỉ xếp sau loài hươu cao cổ và voi. Chúng là loài có trọng lượng cơ thể đứng thứ 5 trong các loài động vật trên cạn: sau voi, tê giác trắng, tê giác Ấn Độ và hà mã.
Bò tót Đông Nam Á sinh sản thường vào tháng 6, 7. Mỗi năm đẻ 1 lứa, mỗi lứa một con. Bò tót mang thai khoảng 270 ngày, đẻ mỗi năm một lứa, mỗi lứa một con. Nơi sinh sống của bò tót là rừng già thường xanh, rừng khộp, rừng hỗn giao tre nứa, rừng thứ sinh địa hình tương đối bằng ở độ cao 500 - 1500m so với mặt nước biển.
Bò tót Đông Nam Á được các chuyên gia động vật học trên thế giới công nhận là một loài bò rừng lớn nhất trên thế giới. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Bò tót Đông Nam Á mang nhiều đặc tính quý như tầm vóc lớn, khả năng chống chịu tốt với điều kiện khí hậu khắc nghiệt…, được coi là một nguồn gene quý hiếm cần được bảo tồn và có thể phát triển để phục vụ nhân giống.
Chúng đã được liệt kê là loài dễ bị tổn thương trong sách đỏ IUCN kể từ năm 1986. Số lượng toàn cầu được ước tính tối đa là 21.000 cá thể trưởng thành vào năm 2016. Chúng đã giảm hơn 70% trong ba thế hệ gần đây và có lẽ đã tuyệt chủng ở Sri Lanka và cũng có thể ở Bangladesh. Trong các khu vực được bảo vệ tốt, số lượng chúng ổn định và ngày càng tăng.
Chúng đã được liệt kê là loài bò dễ bị tổn thương trong sách đỏ IUCN kể từ năm 1986. (Ảnh: Pixabay).
Hiện nay, tại Việt Nam chỉ còn khoảng 300 con bò tót, phân bố chủ yếu tại vườn quốc gia Mường Nhé (Điện Biên), vùng rừng núi Tây Nguyên, vườn quốc gia Chư Mom Rây (Kon Tum) và vườn quốc gia Cát Tiên (Lâm Đồng), sân bay Phú Bài (Huế).Tuy nhiên, những đàn bò tót này đang đứng trước hiểm họa diệt chủng cao do rừng bị chặt phá và nạn săn trộm thú quý.
Số lượng của loài bò tót này ngày càng giảm do 2 nguyên nhân chính:
Loài bò tót này đang đứng trước hiểm họa diệt chủng cao do nạn săn trộm để lấy túi mật. (Ảnh: VTC News).
Theo trang VTC News, nhiều người đồn rằng mật bò tót có thể giúp: tráng dương, mạnh gân cốt, bổ khí, tốt cho sinh lý của đàn ông và hỗ trợ chữa nhiều chứng bệnh nan y… Mật bò tót còn được cho là có dược tính cao hơn cả mật rắn hổ chúa hay mật gấu. Tuy nhiên, trên thực tế, các chuyên gia đã chứng minh rằng mật bò tót không khác gì mật trâu, bò.
Hơn nữa, trong cơ thể người, mật chỉ tiết ra một lượng nhỏ vừa đủ giúp tiêu hóa thức ăn hằng ngày, nếu đưa thêm một lượng mật, dù của động vật nào, vào cơ thể cao hơn mức bình thường đều có nguy cơ gây ngộ độc. Chưa kể nếu uống phải mật động vật bị bệnh (nhiễm khuẩn, thương hàn, bệnh do sán lá Fasciola gigantica ký sinh trong gan và ống dẫn mật gây ra) thì càng nguy hiểm hơn.

articles.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
articles.text:
Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
- Date:
- October 12, 2026
- Source:
- PLOS
- Summary:
- Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days. Even more surprisingly, supplementing with a simple amino acid called D-serine improved memory and learning, offering a potential new approach to age-related cognitive decline.
- Share:
What if some of the changes we associate with aging begin with the loss of a single protein deep inside the brain? Scientists investigating that possibility found that restoring a protein called Menin in older mice improved memory, balance, bone mass, and skin thickness in just 30 days. Even more surprisingly, supplementing the animals with a naturally occurring amino acid improved their learning and memory in only three weeks.
The findings, originally published in March 2023 in PLOS Biology, came from researchers led by Lige Leng of Xiamen University in China. Their experiments identified a previously overlooked connection between inflammation, brain chemistry, and aging throughout the body. Although the results were obtained in mice, they raised an intriguing possibility: Some effects of aging may be influenced by biological processes in the brain that scientists could eventually learn to modify.
Research published since then has added evidence that the brain plays an important role in regulating aging. It has also revealed why the seemingly simple supplement findings deserve careful interpretation.
How a Hidden Brain Protein May Influence Aging
At the center of the discovery is the hypothalamus, a small but powerful region near the base of the brain. It helps regulate essential functions such as body temperature, hunger, metabolism, sleep, and hormone production. Because these systems affect nearly every organ, changes in the hypothalamus can have consequences throughout the body.
Scientists have increasingly recognized the hypothalamus as an important player in aging. One possible reason involves neuroinflammation, the brain's inflammatory response. Although inflammation helps protect against infections and injuries, persistent inflammation can interfere with normal cellular function and contribute to age-related deterioration.
Earlier work by Leng and colleagues had identified Menin as a protein that helps restrain inflammation in the hypothalamus. Menin also participates in regulating gene activity, allowing it to influence multiple biological pathways.
The researchers wanted to understand what happens when this protective protein begins to disappear with age.
They discovered that Menin levels gradually declined in certain hypothalamic neurons as mice grew older. Interestingly, the same decrease was not observed in astrocytes or microglia, two other important types of brain cells involved in supporting neurons and managing immune responses.
To investigate whether this decline actually contributed to aging, the team developed genetically modified mice in which Menin could be selectively disabled.
The results were striking. Mice with reduced Menin activity developed greater inflammation in the hypothalamus, thinner skin, reduced bone mass, and worsening cognitive performance. Their lifespans were also modestly shortened.
Rather than simply accompanying aging, the loss of Menin appeared capable of helping drive several of its characteristic changes.
Restoring Menin Reversed Several Signs of Aging in 30 Days
The researchers then asked an even more interesting question: If declining Menin contributes to aging, could restoring the protein reverse some of the damage?
To find out, they used a gene delivery technique to increase Menin production in a specific part of the hypothalamus in older (20-month-old) mice. This region, called the ventromedial hypothalamus, helps coordinate metabolism, energy balance, and other bodily functions.
Just 30 days after treatment, the animals showed measurable improvements.
Their skin became thicker, bone mass increased, and performance improved on tests measuring learning, memory, and balance. Researchers also observed reductions in inflammation and improvements in certain metabolic changes associated with aging.
In a separate survival analysis, mice receiving the Menin treatment also lived longer than untreated controls.
These findings suggested that some biological changes associated with old age could be at least partially reversed by restoring Menin activity in a specific group of brain cells.
But the researchers also uncovered an important clue about how Menin produced these effects.
A Simple Amino Acid Offers a Surprising Clue
When Menin levels declined, the researchers noticed that concentrations of D-serine, an amino acid involved in brain signaling, also fell.
Amino acids are best known as the building blocks of proteins, but some perform other important functions. D-serine helps regulate NMDA receptors, specialized proteins on nerve cells that are essential for communication between neurons, learning, and the formation of memories.
D-serine is closely related to L-serine, an amino acid commonly found in foods such as soybeans, eggs, fish, and nuts. The two forms have different biological roles. Although D-serine is also available as a dietary supplement, consuming ordinary serine-rich foods is not equivalent to taking the form used in the experiments.
Further investigation revealed that Menin helps control the production of PHGDH, an enzyme involved in the biochemical pathway that generates serine (which was in turn regulated by Menin). When Menin activity decreased, this pathway became less active, reducing the amount of D-serine available to the brain.
Restoring Menin increased D-serine levels in the hippocampus, a region especially important for learning and memory.
This connection suggested that the cognitive effects of declining Menin might be partly explained by disruptions in D-serine signaling.
To test the idea directly, the scientists gave older mice D-serine in their drinking water for three weeks.
The supplementation improved their performance on learning and memory tests, even without directly restoring Menin.
However, there was an important distinction. While increasing Menin improved both cognitive function and physical signs of aging, D-serine supplementation primarily improved cognition. It did not restore the age-related losses in bone mass and skin thickness.
That difference suggests Menin influences aging through several biological mechanisms, with D-serine accounting for only part of its effects.
Later Research Strengthens the Link Between the Brain and Aging
Since the original 2023 discovery, additional studies have provided evidence that the hypothalamus helps coordinate aging across the body.
In a 2024 study published in Cell Metabolism, researchers at Washington University School of Medicine identified a different group of hypothalamic neurons that communicates with fat tissue. By maintaining or stimulating this communication pathway, they increased physical activity, improved age-related metabolic function, and extended lifespan in mice.
That work involved a different protein and neural circuit from Menin, but supported the broader idea that signals originating in the hypothalamus can influence how the rest of the body ages.
Another 2024 study in the Journal of Physiology and Biochemistry provided additional insight into Menin itself. Researchers found that increasing Menin helped protect cultured hippocampal cells against inflammation and a form of programmed cell death triggered by exposure to the stress hormone corticosterone. Although these laboratory experiments did not establish an anti-aging effect, they supported the idea that Menin has important protective functions in brain cells.
An even larger picture emerged in January 2025, when scientists published a detailed analysis of approximately 1.2 million mouse brain cells in Nature.
The researchers discovered that some of the brain cells most sensitive to aging were concentrated around the third ventricle, a fluid-filled cavity in the hypothalamus. Many aging cells showed reduced activity in genes involved in normal neuronal function and increased activity in genes associated with inflammation and immune responses.
These findings highlighted the hypothalamus as a potential center of vulnerability during brain aging, although they did not directly test the Menin pathway.
New Findings in 2026 Reveal More Aging Pathways
Research published in 2026 has further strengthened the connection between hypothalamic activity and longevity.
In a study published in Cell, scientists found that strengthening daily biological rhythms in a specific hypothalamic region improved several aging-related measurements and extended lifespan in male mice. The intervention also reduced estimates of biological age based on DNA methylation, chemical modifications to DNA that change with age.
Another 2026 study in Cell Metabolism identified a protein called Mimecan that helps skeletal muscles communicate with the hypothalamus and brown fat, a specialized tissue involved in generating body heat. Restoring circulating Mimecan levels in older mice improved this communication and extended lifespan.
Together, these discoveries suggest that aging involves complex communication between the brain and the rest of the body. Rather than depending on one master switch, multiple neural circuits, hormones, and metabolic signals appear to help determine how age-related changes unfold.
Could D-Serine Supplements Protect the Human Brain?
The possibility of improving memory with a relatively simple amino acid is especially appealing. However, evidence that D-serine can reverse age-related cognitive decline in humans remains limited.
A small randomized clinical trial published in 2016 tested D-serine in 50 healthy older adults. Participants performed better on one assessment of spatial learning and problem-solving after receiving the amino acid, but researchers did not find significant improvements across the other cognitive tests or mood measurements.
More importantly, later research suggests that the effects of D-serine depend on the biological circumstances.
In an April 2025 study published in Cellular and Molecular Life Sciences, scientists investigated D-serine in mice genetically engineered to develop features of Alzheimer's disease.
Unlike the Menin experiments, which associated reduced D-serine with age-related memory impairment, this study found that an early increase in D-serine accompanied disruptions in brain signaling. Removing the enzyme responsible for producing D-serine prevented or reduced several later cognitive impairments in those mice.
These findings do not invalidate the earlier results. Instead, they suggest that D-serine signaling is more complicated than simply having too little or too much. Its effects may depend on the condition being studied, the timing of treatment, and how the brain's signaling systems are functioning.
There are also unanswered questions about the long-term safety of D-serine supplementation. High doses have raised kidney safety concerns in animal experiments, and research has not established whether prolonged supplementation is a safe or effective way to prevent age-related memory loss in otherwise healthy people.
For now, D-serine should be considered an experimental approach rather than a proven treatment for brain aging.
Can Scientists Eventually Slow Aging by Targeting the Brain?
Despite the encouraging mouse experiments, researchers still need to answer several fundamental questions.
Why does Menin decline in the hypothalamus as animals age? How many of its effects could be reversed by treatment, and how long would those improvements last? Could restoring Menin influence other biological systems in unexpected ways?
It is also unclear whether treatments targeting Menin or D-serine could reproduce similar results in humans.
Nevertheless, the original researchers believe the pathway deserves further investigation.
"We speculate that the decline of Menin expression in the hypothalamus with age may be one of the driving factors of aging, and Menin may be the key protein connecting the genetic, inflammatory, and metabolic factors of aging. D-serine is a potentially promising therapeutic for cognitive decline," said Leng.
Leng adds, "Ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH) Menin signaling diminished in aged mice, which contributes to systemic aging phenotypes and cognitive deficits. The effects of Menin on aging are mediated by neuroinflammatory changes and metabolic pathway signaling, accompanied by serine deficiency in VMH, while restoration of Menin in VMH reversed aging-related phenotypes."
The growing body of evidence points toward a potentially important shift in how scientists understand aging. Instead of viewing it only as the gradual deterioration of individual organs, researchers are investigating how specific brain pathways may actively shape the process.
The possibility that restoring those pathways could improve memory, physical function, or longevity remains experimental. But the Menin discovery, together with subsequent findings, offers a compelling reason to explore whether some of the biological changes associated with aging are more reversible than previously thought.

articles.title: 2 giant Ramesses II statues, one wearing a double crown, discovered by man in Egypt
articles.text:
2 giant Ramesses II statues, one wearing a double crown, discovered by man in Egypt
The remains of two Ramesses II statues — one of which would have originally stood around 28 feet tall — were found by a villager in Egypt.
While working on his land in a village in northern Egypt, a man made an astonishing discovery: the remains of two massive statues of Ramesses II.
The man, Khaled el-Shahat, immediately notified the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, which sent a team to the village of Behbeit El Hagar to excavate and study the statues, the ministry said in a translated statement.
Ramesses II had one of the longest reigns in Egypt's history, ruling from around 1279 to 1213 B.C. During his 66 years in power, Egypt controlled an empire that stretched as far northeast as modern-day Syria. He initiated many building projects throughout the empire, and numerous Ramesses II statues have been found throughout Egypt.
Archaeologists had previously found architectural fragments bearing the name of Ramesses II at Behbeit El Hagar, which is known for its temple dedicated to Isis, a goddess associated with healing and magic, said Mahmoud Emam, an Egyptologist at Cairo University who has worked on remains from the site but was not involved with the recent excavation. He noted that the newly found statues were unearthed on the western side of the temple complex.
"Strong Bull"
Both of the newfound statues were once larger than life, with the bigger one likely standing nearly 28 feet (8.5 meters) tall when it was originally built. However, most of what remains is its head, which is 5.2 feet (1.6 m) tall and depicts the pharaoh wearing the double crown of Upper and Lower Egypt.
Part of this large statue's back pillar has a hieroglyphic inscription that gives the pharaoh's "Horus" name: Hor-Ka-Nakht-Mery-Maat. This name means "Strong Bull, Beloved of Right, Truth," Joyce Tyldesley, a professor emeritus of Egyptology at the University of Manchester in the U.K., wrote in her book "Ramesses: Egypt's Greatest Pharaoh" (Penguin Books, 2001). In Egypt, it was common for pharaohs to have several alternate names with a Horus name, given in honor of the sky god Horus.
The second statue, which stands about 7.9 feet (2.4 m), also likely depicts Ramesses II, the statement said. The king is shown wearing the "Nemes" headdress, a type of striped headcloth that pharaohs wore, the Egypt Exploration Society notes on its website.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
Near this statue is a block of pink granite with two hieroglyphic inscriptions that name Ramesses II and describe him as "King of Upper and Lower Egypt" and the "Son of Ra," an ancient Egyptian sun god, the statement said.
Previous Ramesses II finds
The new finds add more evidence that Ramesses II was heavily invested in the site.
Related Stories
Previous discoveries include two architectural fragments bearing the name of Ramesses II near the Isis temple at Behbeit El Hagar, Emam and his colleagues reported in a 2017 paper. One is believed to be from the upper part of a statue, and another seems to originate from the upper part of a wall.
"We concluded that Ramesses II had undertaken major building works at the temple and recommended further archaeological investigations to shed more light on the early history of the site," Emam said. He noted that the site is threatened by urban growth and that excavation work should be carried out at the temple.
Live Science reached out to the team but did not hear back by the time of publication.
Are you a fan of mummies and hieroglyphs? Find out with our ancient Egypt quiz!
Owen Jarus is a regular contributor to Live Science who writes about archaeology and humans' past. He has also written for The Independent (UK), The Canadian Press (CP) and The Associated Press (AP), among others. Owen has a bachelor of arts degree from the University of Toronto and a journalism degree from Ryerson University.

articles.title: NASA captures a stunning transformation in Australia's red outback
articles.text:
NASA captures a stunning transformation in Australia's red outback
- Date:
- October 12, 2026
- Source:
- NASA Earth Observatory
- Summary:
- Australia's normally dry, rust-colored outback has erupted into a spectacular carpet of wildflowers after unusually heavy rains, potentially producing its most impressive bloom in nearly 20 years. NASA satellite images capture the stunning transformation, which has even brought rare flowers to the grounds of a remote deep-space observatory.
- Share:
A spectacular explosion of wildflowers has transformed the normally dry, rust-colored landscape of Western Australia into a vibrant patchwork of green and colorful blooms. The remarkable display followed months of unusually wet weather, awakening seeds that had been lying dormant beneath the soil.
By late winter 2026 in the Southern Hemisphere, large stretches of the region's arid shrubland were covered in flowers. Local experts believe this could be the most impressive wildflower season the area has experienced in nearly 20 years.
NASA satellite imagery reveals just how dramatically the landscape changed in a single year.
NASA Satellite Images Reveal a Dramatic Transformation
The images above were collected by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) aboard the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite. They show the same part of Western Australia in late August 2025 (left) and late August 2026 (right), highlighting the striking increase in vegetation following the unusually wet conditions.
The location is in the Murchison region, approximately 600 kilometers (370 miles) north of Perth. This remote stretch of the Australian outback is an important grazing area for sheep and cattle, with a landscape typically dominated by hardy plants adapted to limited rainfall.
Much of the region's vegetation consists of grasses, saltbush, and mulga, a slow-growing evergreen tree capable of surviving in dry conditions. Wildflowers also emerge periodically, but their abundance can vary dramatically depending on how much rain falls.
Unusually Heavy Rains Trigger a Wildflower Explosion
The exceptional display in 2026 was made possible by a series of cold fronts that carried much-needed moisture into the region.
According to Australia's Bureau of Meteorology, June brought above-average rainfall, while August was much wetter than normal. These favorable conditions allowed seeds that had remained inactive in the dry soil to germinate, producing an extraordinary variety of wildflowers across the landscape.
The colorful transformation extended into the grounds of a radio astronomy observatory operated by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Australia's national science agency.
Among the flowers were several threatened species, adding ecological significance to the seasonal spectacle. The observatory has helped track these vulnerable plants on land that was previously used for livestock grazing.
Where Wildflowers Bloom Beneath Deep-Space Telescopes
While the flowers created an extraordinary scene on the ground, the observatory's usual work takes place far beyond Earth's atmosphere.
Known as Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara, the CSIRO Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory is a remote research facility dedicated to studying the universe through radio astronomy. Its antenna arrays detect radio signals from celestial objects, allowing scientists to observe and catalog sources across the southern sky.
The observatory's isolated location is particularly important for this work. It sits within a designated "radio quiet" zone, where communication systems and electronic equipment are restricted to reduce interference with sensitive scientific instruments.
Even relatively weak signals generated by human technology can interfere with radio observations, so limiting these disturbances helps astronomers detect faint emissions traveling across space.
Australia's Radio Telescopes Have Helped NASA Explore Space
Australia's radio astronomy facilities have a long history of supporting some of NASA's most important space missions.
The Murriyang radio telescope, located in Parkes, New South Wales, helped track Mariner 2 in 1962. That spacecraft became the first successful planetary science mission, marking a major milestone in the exploration of other worlds.
The telescope also played a significant role during the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969, serving as an important receiving station for communications from the historic mission.
CSIRO additionally manages the Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex, one of three major facilities that make up NASA's worldwide Deep Space Network.
This global system maintains communications with spacecraft traveling throughout the solar system and beyond, while also supporting radar measurements and radio astronomy research.
Both the Murriyang telescope and the Canberra complex contributed to NASA's Artemis II mission in April 2026, continuing Australia's decades-long involvement in space exploration.
For a brief period in 2026, however, one of Australia's most remote astronomical research regions offered a remarkable spectacle much closer to home. While its telescopes continued scanning the distant universe, unusually generous winter rains brought the surrounding outback to life in a brilliant display of wildflowers.

articles.title: Top 11 sự thật đáng kinh ngạc về quốc gia giàu thứ 2 trên thế giới
articles.text:
Đây là một quốc gia nhỏ bé nằm trong châu Âu nhưng có GDP bình quân đầu người cao thứ 2 thế giới.
Với diện tích khoảng 160.579.263 m2, đây là quốc gia nhỏ thứ tư ở châu Âu, sau Thành phố Vatican, Monaco và San Marino. Ngôn ngữ chính thức của Liechtenstein là tiếng Đức.
Liechtenstein trên bản đồ thế giới. (Hình ảnh: Insider.com).
Schaan là thành phố lớn nhất của Liechtenstein có 6.000 người sinh sống, nhưng thủ đô Vaduz, chỉ cách Schaan khoảng 11 dặm, thậm chí còn có ít cư dân hơn: khoảng 5.400 người.
Theo Tổ chức Du lịch Thế giới, Liechtenstein chỉ đón 85.000 du khách trong năm 2018. Không có những cơ sở giao thông cơ bản như sân bay quốc tế, cảng biển hay nhà ga xe lửa, Liechtenstein khiến cho du khách ngần ngại về việc di chuyển đi lại khi đến tham quan nước này.
Ga tàu chính tại Schaan, Liechtenstein vào buổi tối. (Hình ảnh: Insider.com).
Trong blog chia sẻ chuyến đi du lịch đến đất nước này, blogger du lịch Nota Bene nói rằng không có nhiều việc để làm hay trải nghiệm ở thành phố thủ đô: "Chúng tôi đã đi dạo toàn bộ trung tâm thành phố chỉ trong… 20 phút! Chúng tôi đã uống cà phê và bánh ngọt trong một quán cà phê. Bất tiện là quán cà phê chỉ chấp nhận tiền mặt".
GDP của Liechtenstein chỉ bị vượt qua bởi Monaco, thành phố giàu có xa hoa ở vùng duyên hải Pháp và ước tính một phần ba dân số là triệu phú.
Bảng xếp hạng GDP bình quân đầu người. (Hình ảnh: World population review).
Liechtenstein có ngành dịch vụ tài chính thịnh vượng, với các ngành công nghiệp chính khác bao gồm điện tử, sản xuất kim loại, sản phẩm nha khoa, dụng cụ quang học và dược phẩm. Thuế suất thấp, các quy tắc thành lập, quản trị công ty lỏng lẻo và truyền thống giữ bí mật ngân hàng nghiêm ngặt đã góp phần đáng kể vào khả năng của các trung gian tài chính ở Liechtenstein trong việc thu hút vốn từ bên ngoài đất nước.
Theo Tổ chức Chính sách Công và Luật Hiến pháp của Liechtenstein, đất nước này có tỷ lệ nợ trên GDP là 0,5%.
Người đàn ông giàu nhất Liechtenstein. (Hình ảnh: Internet).
Christoph Zeller - người đã có 13 năm làm Giám đốc điều hành của công ty sản phẩm nha khoa Ivoclar Vivadent AG, có tài sản trị giá 3,1 tỷ USD - chiếm một nửa trong GDP 6,2 tỷ USD của quốc gia châu Âu nhỏ bé này.
Chính vì vậy mà đôi khi nó vô tình bị xâm chiếm bởi quân đội Thụy Sĩ khi họ đang tiến hành các bài tập huấn luyện trong rừng gần biên giới với Liechtenstein.
Theo Tổ chức Chính sách Công và Luật Hiến pháp của Liechtenstein, vào năm 2016, 54% lực lượng lao động của Liechtenstein đến từ các quốc gia như Thụy Sĩ, Áo và Đức.
Khung cảnh đẹp của đất nước nhỏ bé. (Hình ảnh: Internet).
Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp của quốc gia là 2,1%, theo Văn phòng Thống kê Liechtenstein.
Sân bay gần đất nước này nhất là ở Zurich - cách thủ đô của Liechtenstein khoảng một tiếng rưỡi lái xe. Đây có lẽ là điểm trừ rất lớn khiến quốc gia này khó có thể phát triển du lịch.
Liechtenstein khi nhìn từ trên cao. (Hình ảnh: Internet).
Cư dân cũng không được khuyến khích gây ra bất kì tiếng ồn nào trong 90 phút nghỉ trưa từ 12:00 đến 13:30 và cũng đừng cố tình gây ồn ào sau 10 giờ tối nếu không muốn gặp cảnh sát.

articles.title: 'We're not a competitor to fusion. We are fusion': Inside the race to harness unlimited solar power in space
articles.text:
'We're not a competitor to fusion. We are fusion': Inside the race to harness unlimited solar power in space
Space-based solar power has the potential to meet Earth's energy needs many times over. Will it see the light of day?
The year is 2050, and as the sun sets, the night's first constellations emerge in perfect rows. But these amber-glowing arrays aren't stars at all; they're satellite clusters, harvesting the day's last rays before beaming their power back to Earth.
If it reads like science fiction, that's because it started that way. Called space-based solar power (SBSP), the concept featured prominently in the techno-utopian imaginations of 20th-century visionaries and writers. But for decades, it was dismissed — a pie in the sky proposal.
Now, as a new space race heats up, governments and private companies in China, the U.S., the U.K. and Japan are developing several projects to reassess the idea's feasibility. These include China's ZhuRi ("Chase the Sun") program, Japan's OHISAMA project, the U.K.'s Space Solar, and power-beaming experiments by Caltech and the Air Force Research Laboratory in the U.S., all of which are targeting test launches in the next five years.
Proponents say the technology has the potential to meet Earth's energy needs many times over while causing minimal harm to the environment. But first it needs to get off the ground: In the eyes of critics, space-based solar power is exorbitantly expensive, riddled with untested assumptions, and far too complex to be deployed in time for an urgent green-energy transition.
The challenges include getting the massive solar-panel-covered satellites into space; assembling them; getting those solar panels to constantly face our star; and then finding ways to convert, concentrate and transmit their collected power back to Earth.
Despite these hurdles, researchers keep returning to the idea. Perhaps because the most crucial step — generating energy in the first place — is already being done by the sun. Every second, our star fuses hydrogen atoms to expel the same energy as nine trillion atomic bombs. All that's left to do is catch it.
"We're not a competitor to fusion. We are fusion," Peter Garretson, the U.S. Air Force's former chief of future technology and an SBSP expert, told Live Science.
From science fiction to NASA proposal
The first glimmers of SBSP as a concept came from the Russian rocket scientist and astronautics pioneer Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, who, in 1923, suggested deploying space-based mirrors that could concentrate sunlight to Earth with enough intensity to boil 10 cups of coffee.
Tsiolkovsky's fanciful proposal soon entered science fiction, appearing in the British writer Olaf Stapledon's 1937 novel "Star Maker" as a "gauze of light traps" that an advanced alien civilization used to focus "the escaping solar energy for intelligent use" — an idea later formalized by theoretical physicist Freeman Dyson as a Dyson sphere.
Then, in 1941, Isaac Asimov made the clearest, most famous early sketch of SBSP in his short story "Reason," in which a robot colony toils aboard a power station that collects solar energy and fires it back to Earth in the form of microwaves. Asimov provided few details on the fictional station's engineering, instead focusing on the robots' religious worship of the vessel.
But the transformation from science fiction to a concrete proposal didn't take long. In 1968, aerospace engineer Peter Glaser, a consultant and project manager for the Apollo 11 mission's distance-measuring laser reflectors, drew up an engineering design for a "solar power satellite" consisting of three key elements: a ray-collecting device, a converter and a transmitter.
Glaser's collector was a disk of photovoltaic panels that would be lifted some 22,400 miles (36,000 kilometers) off the ground. Locked in a geostationary orbit above Earth and bathed in near-constant sunlight, the satellite would harvest solar rays before converting them into microwaves to be beamed, largely unimpeded through the atmosphere, to receiving antennae on the ground. Once there, the microwaves would be converted into electricity and distributed across the grid.
NASA awarded Glaser a contract to study the concept further, with both domestic and international energy crises (such as the 1973 oil crisis and the 1979 Three-Mile Island nuclear accident) adding wind to his solar sails.
But Glaser's design hit technical and financial roadblocks, the most forbidding being the project's sheer size. By 1981, when the U.S. Department of Energy's four-year study of space-based solar power was released, it estimated that a "meaningful" contribution of 300 gigawatts (sufficient to power hundreds of millions of homes) would require 60 satellites, each spanning 21 square miles (55 square kilometers) and weighing 50,000 tons (45,000 metric tons). The plan was deemed unaffordable.
Later reassessments, such as a 1997 report by NASA physicist John Mankins, pointed to advances such as improved solar cells that made the concept more realistic. Yet the overall consensus remained hostile. A 2015 report released by the Strategic Studies Institute (SSI) of the U.S. Army War College stated that while SBSP systems are "technically feasible," there was "no compelling evidence that such systems will be economically competitive" with terrestrial power systems. It concluded that "the reality is that such systems always seem to be seen as just 10 years away by their advocates."
Aiming high
But a lot can change in a decade, including the cost of firing rockets. Since the SSI report, SpaceX's reusable Falcon 9 rocket has sent launch costs plummeting to around 30 times less than those of NASA's Space Shuttle, with satellites also getting cheaper due to mass production and advances to the clean rooms where they're made. And SpaceX's even bigger Starship rocket promises to more than quintuple Falcon's payload capacity, lowering prices further.
"What you have is a cadre of people in the space community that have grown up before Starlink and SpaceX," Garretson said. "They literally could not believe that, as your launch rate goes up and you amortize your costs, [the launch cost] approaches the cost of fuel." Some took notice. A 2021 assessment commissioned by the U.K. government estimated that a 2-gigawatt, mile-wide space-based solar power array would cost 17.3 billion British pounds ($23.4 billion) and generate energy at 50 British pounds ($68) per megawatt hour over its century lifetime.
That's the equivalent output of a large power station in the U.K., with the initial costs being 39% to 49% cheaper than biomass, nuclear or the most efficient gas energy sources, according to the assessment. And while it's still 14% to 52% more expensive than current terrestrial wind and solar energy, the technology could be beamed anywhere, even to remote locations.
Based on these findings, in 2023, the U.K. government awarded 4.3 million British pounds ($5.8 million) in seed funding to a handful of companies and universities to develop SBSP further.
The U.K. report chose one satellite design as its reference architecture: CASSIOPeiA. Belonging to the U.K. SBSP company Space Solar, the satellite's design is an attempt to crack a significant challenge faced by early solar satellite blueprints: how to keep solar panels constantly aligned with the sun to maximize radiation collection.
Unlike other satellite designs, such as China's Multi-Rotary Joint Solar Power Satellite or Mankins' SPS-ALPHA, which rotate the panels or use a system of mirrors to constantly redirect sunlight onto them, CASSIOPeiA is shaped like a gigantic DNA strand.
This design, alongside a sun-synchronous orbit and a slow spin, enables CASSIOPeiA to constantly receive and transmit solar energy without any heavy or failure-prone moving parts. Space Solar claims that a single CASSIOPeiA satellite, which would be about 1 mile (1.6 km) in diameter, could microwave-beam as much as 2 gigawatts of constant power to a fixed point on the ground — enough to supply a city of 2 million people.
Space Solar says that once the satellite is in space, it will be far more efficient and economical than gathering sunlight on the ground could ever be. That's because the light hitting the space-based power station isn't deflected or attenuated by the atmosphere.
"You use a lot less materials compared with terrestrial solar, and you utilize them more," Sam Adlen, co-founder and co-CEO of Space Solar, one of the funding recipients, told Live Science. "So it's 100% utilized in space rather than 10% if you're on the ground — and you've got 13 times more instant energy, so you're getting much more out of the materials."
Beaming down
However, the next step — beaming gigawatts of energy down and across tens of miles of atmosphere and through potential cloud cover — remains a major technical hurdle.
Proposed power-beaming methods are currently split between two types: lasers and microwaves. California-based startup Aetherflux, which has plans to beam power from satellites in low Earth orbit, has developed an infrared laser transmission system that it will test using a demonstration satellite launched on October 1. The microwave energy will be transmitted at around one kilowatt (enough to supply the basic electrical demands of a household).
Meanwhile, Caltech and Overview Energy, another U.S. startup, have both demonstrated respective microwave and laser-power beaming from orbit and from a plane, respectively, albeit in negligible amounts ( less than a kilowatt).
Despite their efficiency and proven ability to travel vast distances, optical beams in the infrared and near-infrared ranges are easily scattered by water droplets in the atmosphere, preventing power from being transferred on cloudy days. Persisting efficiency issues with optical power transmission also worsen at gigawatt power levels, meaning lasers are less feasible for use at the utility scale.
Microwaves, on the other hand, can be beamed at frequencies with much higher power and suffer relatively little atmospheric attenuation. That's why Space Solar, Japan's OHISAMA project and China's ZhuRi program all plan to use microwave-beaming systems. Nonetheless, microwaves have comparatively longer wavelengths, so their beams diffract more widely across longer distances. This means that even if beams are sent by transmitters hundreds of meters wide, they would need Earth-based receivers spanning dozens of square miles.
These limitations mean that "it's going to take many years" before gigawatt-scale power beaming is achieved, Remo Proietti Zaccaria, head of the DELTA Lab at the Italian Institute of Technology, told Live Science.
Improvements in power-beaming efficiency will bring their own challenges. Even battery-powered laser pointers can blind or burn, so prototypes by laser-beaming SBSP companies like Aetherflux must be designed with that possibility in mind. They promise safety mechanisms that switch off their lasers if anything flies between the transmitter and the receiver.
"Definitely for the weapon side, this technology now can be used efficiently," Proietti Zaccaria said.
If you're imagining an orbital weapon devised by a Bond villain, you may be disappointed — even fully developed power-beaming lasers and microwaves would take a while to cook an egg, or boil Tsiolkovsky's coffees. But beaming technology could still have potent military use: Scrambling communications systems on Earth to create havoc with relatively little effort.
"If you throw even that amount of intensity of power to our antennas, you're going to freeze the electronics; that's for sure," Proietti Zaccaria said. "It's not necessary to destroy them. As long as you freeze the electronics, you've done the job."
The challenges associated with power beaming have pushed some engineers to simpler concepts. One (going full circle back to Tsiolkovsky's original proposal) envisions the deployment of space-based mirrors that reflect sunlight back to Earth after sunset, with a single reflector extending the daylight delivered onto solar panels by around 20 minutes.
This may not seem like much on its own, "but then you can increase this with multiple reflectors," Onur Celik, a researcher in space technology at the University of Glasgow, told Live Science. "If you have 10 or more of them, you can arrange them in space in such a way that you can extend this to up to two hours or so at that altitude."
"The sunlight that you deliver, if it all turns into electricity, could power thousands of homes," he concluded.
The light of day
The trillion-dollar question is whether that power will be cheaper and more efficient than that generated on the ground. The median cost of the electricity generated by SBSP as estimated by the U.K. government is 50 British pounds per megawatt hour ($68), putting it roughly in line with the costs of offshore wind and terrestrial solar power.
However, this estimate is orders of magnitude too sunny for the 2024 NASA cost report, with its projections suggesting SBSP's baseline electricity costs fall between $610 and $1,590 per megawatt hour, depending on the array design. NASA concluded that the U.K.'s median estimate was achievable only after drastic future reductions in launch and manufacturing costs.
Independent studies are also divided over feasibility. One assessment suggests that SBSP could reduce Europe's need for land-based renewable energy by up to 80%, while another counters that the costs could be 12 to 80 times more expensive than those for terrestrial alternatives. This variability exists within the studies themselves, with research published in the journal Acta Astronautica estimating that SBSP could contribute to meeting anywhere from 3% to 31% of global electricity demand, depending on possible constraints in how many satellites can safely fit into an orbit, the receiver size, and where power is beamed to.
"For the numbers we found, I don't believe that this technology could actually be employed to generate energy for Earth," said Proietti Zaccaria, a co-author of the Acta Astronautica study. If humanity had used up all available space for solar panels on Earth, "then I will tell you it would make sense, because at that point, 3%, 5%, 10% could make a difference."
Proietti Zaccaria does see use cases for SBSP schemes for future moon or Mars missions, but otherwise, "the cost for building technology of this kind is really very, very high," he said. "Vice versa, the cost nowadays of buying and installing a solar panel on the roof of any building has become extremely cheap."
Among the challenges would be ferrying the raw materials for the systems into space and then assembling them. Such a feat would make the construction of the International Space Station — currently the most complex structure built in orbit — seem like child's play. Maintaining arrays and preventing them from crashing into other satellites in Earth's increasingly crowded orbits would also take significant international coordination.
Then there are the unweighed environmental costs. All modern rockets use methane, a potent greenhouse gas, to propel them into space, and they release much of it into Earth's upper atmosphere, where its effects are the strongest.
"And so clearly, there is a question there on how launching 100,000 of these superheavy vehicles into the atmosphere will actually impact the atmosphere itself, as opposed to the benefit that we get in the next 20 years or so from having solar power from space," Matteo Ceriotti, a senior lecturer in space systems engineering at the University of Glasgow, told Live Science. "It's not entirely clear."
Ceriotti said the likeliest route for overcoming all of these difficulties come from smaller companies running, and then streamlining, proof-of-concept tests in space.
Exclusive to Live Science Pro
- 'Everything we know about space travel is going to change within a decade': The fusion breakthrough that could unlock a path to the stars
- US military confirms weapons in orbit: Why a space 'arms race' could be extremely hard to stop
- 'River in the Sky': China's doomed plan to create a 'cloud seeding corridor' tells us how far the country will go to solve its climate crisis
"Obviously, it's not something that we have ever done," he said. "So clearly, we need to start somewhere, and we need to start small."
The hopes of SBSP proponents remain unclouded by gloomy estimates. They cite several technologies, from personal computers to reusable rockets, that were once thought to be impossibly expensive, even fictitious, that are now ubiquitous and cheap. Their eyes remain fixed on demonstration missions to be launched over the next four years by the likes of Space Solar, Reflect Orbital, Aetherflux and Virtus Solis. If these missions succeed, another once-impossible idea could appear much brighter.
"The private sector is good at this, because it has to be," Sanjay Vijendran, an SBSP consultant who led the European Space Agency's now-shuttered SOLARIS project to test the feasibility of SBSP, told Live Science. "It can break the problem down to quite a small level and start to do things with today's technology and today's way of doing things, and start to show that this can be valuable."
Help us improve Live Science Pro: We're always trying to make our content better. Leave us feedback about Pro here.
Ben Turner is a U.K. based writer and editor at Live Science. He covers physics and astronomy, tech and climate change. He graduated from University College London with a degree in particle physics before training as a journalist. When he's not writing, Ben enjoys reading literature, playing the guitar and embarrassing himself with chess.
