articles.title: Volvo makes a bigger bet on Nvidia for hands-free automated driving | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia. The companies announced on Thursday that Volvo will use three pieces of Nvidia hardware and software in its future vehicles to provide an automated driving system that can navigate urban streets and highways.
Under the expanded partnership, Volvo will combine its vehicle safety systems and engineering with Nvidia’s Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Alpamayo driving software stack, and Halos safety evaluation layer.
The Alpamayo stack is redundant and diverse, according to Ali Kani, who heads up Nvidia’s automotive division. It combines Alpamayo, a family of AI models, datasets, and simulation and development tools used to build autonomous-driving software, with classical software that uses machine learning and camera and radar perception, he said.
“The point is we run these two stacks at the same time, and we have multimodal sensors in our philosophy because it’s a safer product that way,” Kani said, adding that the open source Alpamayo software has now been downloaded by more than 650,000 developers.
Volvo didn’t reveal the value of the partnership or which vehicle model would be the first to use this new Nvidia tech stack. But Alwin Bakkenes, Volvo’s head of software development, hinted at the scale of the deal and how it represents the automaker’s evolution toward developing a full-tech stack designed for its electric vehicles as well as its plug-in hybrids and gas-powered vehicles.
“Automakers used to be very much like car-line-based development and working with various suppliers, etc. and we have completely changed and migrated into being a full-tech stack company,” Bakkenes said, adding that Volvo will start this partnership with a brand new vehicle that “will come in the not-too-near future.”
He said the first vehicle with this new Nvidia tech stack will debut within the decade, and “then of course the technology can go beyond that.”
While Volvo’s relationship with Nvidia isn’t new, the expanded partnership represents the automaker’s effort to bring the latest automated driving software to all of its vehicles — not just its EVs.
All of Volvo’s battery-electric vehicles use Nvidia’s Orin computer chip, which processes information from cameras, radar, and other sensors to help a vehicle understand its surroundings and make driving decisions.
“What we’re going to do in the future is actually standardize more on Hyperion — also from a sensor set perspective — to really open up the stack for the wider partnership with Nvidia,” Bakkenes said.

articles.title: NVIDIA's RTX Spark is good for Windows, even if you don't need local AI - Engadget
articles.text:
NVIDIA's RTX Spark is good for Windows, even if you don't need local AI
Windows PCs may finally catch up to Apple Silicon.
Last week, I spent two days hearing how Microsoft and NVIDIA are "reinventing the PC" with RTX Spark, the new system-on-a-chip powering the Surface Laptop Ultra and several other Windows PCs this fall. It's the first time we've seen powerful Arm CPUs joined together with NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU technology and up to 128GB of ultra-fast unified memory on a single chip. Theoretically, RTX Spark should allow for thin-yet-powerful laptops (and a few small desktops) that can handle AI tasks locally, as well as tackling content creation and gaming. So sure, I suppose NVIDIA and Microsoft have a reason to gloat a bit.
But, just like the launch of Snapdragon-powered Copilot+ systems two years ago, it was hard to ignore the elephant in the room: RTX Spark is clearly a response to Apple Silicon and the transformational changes it brought to Macs six years ago. Apple's chips are also made up of a powerful Arm CPU, capable GPU and fast unified memory, and they span the company's lineup from the tiny Mac mini to the super-powerful Mac Studio and 16-inch MacBook Pro. With RTX Spark, Windows users finally have a way to see the benefits of an efficient Arm-based SoC on high-end PCs, while the recent batch of Qualcomm chips covers the low-end and mid-range.
There weren't many surprises at Microsoft's AI launch event (featuring the Surface Laptop Ultra), or at NVIDIA's RTX Spark Editor's Day, which I attended alongside other media and analysts. Both companies want to sell us a future where we can run AI models and agents right from an RTX Spark-powered Windows laptop, something that seemed clear since the chip was announced at Computex. But even if that future doesn't come to pass, RTX Spark could still lead to some intriguing changes in the PC world.
Under the hood with RTX Spark
The RTX Spark SoC is powered by up to 20 NVIDIA Grace Arm CPU cores (10 performance cores and 10 efficiency cores), a Blackwell GPU with up to 6,144 CUDA cores, and up to 128GB of unified LPDDR5x memory running at 9,400 Mbps. There's also a slightly less powerful configuration with 18 CPU cores and 5,120 GPU cores. RTX Spark also includes much of what you'd find on NVIDIA's latest GPUs, including fifth-gen tensor cores, fourth-gen ray tracing cores, and a Blackwell video engine (with support of AV1 UHQ and 4:2:2 encoding and decoding).
By shoving all of this hardware onto a single chip, NVIDIA claims the RTX Spark is twice as efficient as a laptop powered by an Intel Core Ultra 9 285H and RTX 5070 dedicated GPU, while gaming at 60 watts. NVIDIA has previously said RTX Spark systems should be similarly powerful to RTX 5070 laptops, though as you can tell from the chart below, those dedicated GPU systems can also draw a lot more energy for better performance.
If you plan to be connected to power most of the time and don't need to travel with your laptop, you may see little benefit from choosing an RTX Spark system. But if you need to do serious creative work on the go, RTX Spark's improved efficiency allows PCs to work as fast on battery as they are while plugged in, according to NVIDIA. From my brief time with the Surface Laptop Ultra, I didn't notice any performance drops while playing Gears of War: E-Day on battery power. The game still looked silky smooth in 1440p with high graphics settings.
RTX Spark is built for AI, but also helps content creation and gaming
With its support for tons of unified RAM, RTX Spark systems should appeal to AI developers and researchers who need as much memory as they can to run large AI models locally, like the 125B parameter Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. An RTX Spark system could significantly reduce the amount of money spent on cloud AI tokens, or replace that demand entirely. One researcher I spoke with was jealous that his colleagues were able to easily run AI models on modern Mac laptops, and he was excited about the possibility of doing the same on a Windows notebook. RTX Spark is also coming along as Microsoft is adding more support in Windows 11 for on-device AI tools like Perplexity, as well as simplified ways to set up AI agents like OpenClaw and GitHub Copilot.
Not surprisingly, NVIDIA is also touting RTX Spark's gaming capabilities. Since it features a Blackwell GPU front and center, it'll deliver all of the features you'd expect from RTX 50-series cards, including support for DLSS 5. As I mentioned before, you can expect performance similar to an RTX 5070 — NVIDIA is specifically touting 1440p as the intended resolution for RTX Spark systems, though I'd be interested to see how they perform in 4K with DLSS. A new performance mode for DLSS Frame Generation can push Cyberpunk 2077 up to 280fps with 6x frame gen, compared 213fps without performance mode. (It's unclear what you lose to achieve that frame bump, though.)
Since RTX Spark is Arm-based, it won't natively run every game on Windows, but NVIDIA claims recent titles like Control Resonant and the aforementioned Gears of War: E-Day will be supported at launch thanks to Microsoft's Prism emulator for x86 software. NBA 2K27, the main DLSS 5 launch game, will also be supported, alongside World of Warcraft: Forever. NVIDIA says it's also working with major anti-cheat providers to support their products, something that's prevented multiplayer games from working on Arm Windows systems in the past.
I'll have to spend more time with RTX Spark systems to see how well they actually handle gaming, beyond my minutes with Gears of War: E-Day. But if playing games is a priority, you'd still be better off with an Intel or AMD system with a dedicated GPU. At least then you wouldn't have to worry about potential emulation issues.
RTX Spark systems will also be useful content creation — again, as you'd expect from PCs with RTX Blackwell GPUs. You can lean on hardware acceleration in tools like Blender, and notably, Adobe is re-architecting Photoshop and Premiere specifically for NVIDIA's platform. That's a major sign of faith from one of the biggest software companies around, though I suppose Adobe is also reading the tea leaves and seeing a bright future for Arm-based Windows systems in general.
RTX Spark isn't for everyone, but that's okay
NVIDIA isn't targeting casual consumers with RTX Spark, not with a starting price of $2,600 for 18-core systems, or an eye-bleeding $3,700 for the full-powered 20-core models. Both NVIDIA and Microsoft are targeting AI developers and researchers who have the money to spend on insane amounts of RAM. And they should be prepared to open their wallets — a Surface Laptop Ultra with 128GB of RAM will cost a smooth $5.900. Still, that's a good deal cheaper than a fully-equipped M5 Max 16-inch MacBook Pro with 128GB of RAM, which costs $7,000.
Simply by existing, the RTX Spark platform will likely push Intel and AMD in creative new directions. AMD is trying to accomplish something similar with its Ryzen AI Max 400 chips, which can also house a ton of unified memory, but can also run existing x86 software without any emulation. And Intel has been eager to prove itself against AMD for the last few years, which has resulted in its powerful Core Ultra Series 3 chips. As always, competition is great for consumers.

articles.title: Vinpearl là doanh nghiệp lớn được người lao động yêu thích nhất năm 2026
articles.text:
Dấu ấn dẫn đầu trên cả hai bảng xếp hạng tiếp tục khẳng định vị thế thương hiệu tuyển dụng hàng đầu Việt Nam của Vinpearl, đồng thời củng cố lợi thế thu hút nhân tài của doanh nghiệp trong chiến lược phát triển toàn cầu.
Kết quả xếp hạng năm 2026 được xác lập từ khảo sát quy mô lớn với hơn 82.000 người tham gia bình chọn cho 7.301 doanh nghiệp thuộc 30 ngành nghề trên toàn quốc. Chương trình “Doanh nghiệp yêu thích” là khảo sát thường niên phi lợi nhuận do CareerViet - thành viên tập đoàn nhân sự quốc tế Kariera Group - tổ chức năm thứ 13, với sự cố vấn về phương pháp nghiên cứu của Amco Việt Nam, đơn vị có hơn 30 năm kinh nghiệm nghiên cứu thị trường.
Vị trí số 1 ở cả bảng xếp hạng khối doanh nghiệp lớn và ngành Du lịch - Khách sạn năm 2026 tiếp tục nối dài chuỗi thành tích của Vinpearl trên thị trường nhân sự. Trước đó, năm 2025, Vinpearl đã dẫn đầu ngành Du lịch/Ẩm thực/Nghỉ dưỡng trong bảng xếp hạng “Nơi làm việc tốt nhất Việt Nam” do Anphabe công bố. Việc liên tiếp giữ vị trí cao nhất tại các hạng mục xếp hạng của các khảo sát độc lập cho thấy sức hấp dẫn của Vinpearl đối với người lao động, đồng thời củng cố uy tín thương hiệu tuyển dụng trong lĩnh vực du lịch - nghỉ dưỡng tại Việt Nam.
Sức hấp dẫn của Vinpearl trên thị trường tuyển dụng gắn liền với quy mô và sự phát triển của hệ sinh thái du lịch - nghỉ dưỡng - vui chơi giải trí hàng đầu Việt Nam. Sau hơn hai thập kỷ phát triển, Vinpearl hiện vận hành 67 cơ sở tại 20 tỉnh, thành, bao gồm 36 khách sạn và khu nghỉ dưỡng 5 sao, 17 công viên chủ đề VinWonders, 7 sân golf, 5 trung tâm hội nghị và nhà hát cùng nhiều sản phẩm vui chơi, giải trí quy mô lớn. Không chỉ mang đến cơ hội nghề nghiệp đa dạng, mạng lưới hoạt động rộng khắp còn tạo điều kiện để người lao động phát triển chuyên môn, tích lũy kinh nghiệm và tiếp cận các mô hình vận hành dịch vụ theo tiêu chuẩn quốc tế.
Bà Ngô Thị Hương, Tổng Giám đốc Vinpearl, chia sẻ: “Đối với Vinpearl, con người là nền tảng cốt lõi tạo nên chất lượng dịch vụ và sức mạnh cạnh tranh của doanh nghiệp. Chúng tôi xác định xây dựng môi trường làm việc chuyên nghiệp, phát triển đội ngũ nhân sự chất lượng cao là ưu tiên chiến lược, bảo đảm năng lực vận hành hệ sinh thái dịch vụ quy mô lớn và hiện thực hóa mục tiêu đưa thương hiệu du lịch - nghỉ dưỡng Việt Nam vươn tầm thế giới".
Song hành với những thành tựu trên thị trường nhân sự Việt Nam, Vinpearl còn ghi dấu bước tiến quan trọng trên thị trường quốc tế. Năm 2026, Brand Finance vinh danh Vinpearl là Thương hiệu khách sạn mạnh nhất thế giới, với 95,4/100 điểm Brand Strength Index và xếp hạng AAA+ - cấp độ cao nhất trong hệ thống đánh giá. Giá trị thương hiệu tăng 86%, đạt 381 triệu USD, đưa Vinpearl lần đầu tiên gia nhập Top 50 thương hiệu khách sạn giá trị nhất thế giới.
Những thành tích nổi bật trong năm 2026 tiếp tục khẳng định tầm vóc và vị thế của Vinpearl trên cả thị trường du lịch quốc tế và thị trường nhân sự Việt Nam. Đây là nền tảng quan trọng để Vinpearl phát huy sức mạnh thương hiệu, nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh và mở rộng hiện diện trên thị trường toàn cầu, từng bước hiện thực hóa mục tiêu trở thành thương hiệu du lịch - nghỉ dưỡng hàng đầu thế giới, góp phần nâng cao vị thế du lịch Việt Nam trên bản đồ quốc tế.

articles.title: Steam can now show game achievements in separate ‘sets’
articles.text:
Valve is introducing a major new feature for Steam achievements called “achievement sets” that lets developers list different groups of achievements for a base game and DLCs.
Steam can now show game achievements in separate ‘sets’
Developers with games on Steam can split achievements from a base game and its DLC into sets with their own progress bars.
“In games that support sets, you still unlock achievements by playing the game as usual,” Valve says. “But when you browse what you have unlocked afterward, Steam will break the long list of game achievements into the developer-created sets, making it easier to see what you have completed and to find other related achievements you can unlock next.” Achievement sets have their own progress bars, and if you finish a set, you’ll get a “set complete” trophy that’s visible on your profile.
Steam will support seasonal achievement sets that developers can archive, too. “We think there are a lot of fun ways games can take advantage of the temporary nature this can add, such as adding achievements to season-based games or enabling time-limited holiday achievements,” Valve says.
A handful of games already support achievement sets, per Valve:
Against the Storm
Age of Wonders 4
American Truck Simulator
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
Crusader Kings III
DREDGE
Euro Truck Simulator 2
Forza Horizon 5
Flock Around
He is Coming
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
Left 4 Dead 2
Portal 2
PowerWash Simulator
PowerWash Simulator 2
Team Fortress 2
Victoria 3
The company is also refreshing the Steam Achievements page to show “a summary of your overall progress, progress in each achievement set, and details on individual achievements.”
The new achievements features are available in the latest Steam client beta, Valve says.

articles.title: SK Hynix bargains for chip equipment exports to its China facility in return for building a factory in US | TechCrunch
articles.text:
SK Hynix appears to be navigating choppy U.S.-China chipmaking waters. The company’s flash memory unit, Solidigm, is seeking U.S. approval to send American chipmaking equipment to its factory in Dalian, China, as a condition to continue building a semiconductor factory in the U.S., Reuters reported, citing anonymous sources.
Solidigm has been reportedly chalking up plans to build a NAND flash memory chip factory in the U.S. and is considering upstate New York as a potential location for the facility.
NAND flash chips are primarily used in solid-state storage drives, which are employed in everything from laptops and smartphones to AI data centers. But the global component shortage, thanks to skyrocketing demand for AI data centers, has driven up prices for everything that goes into data centers, including high-speed RAM chips and SSDs. Research firm TrendForce expects NAND prices to rise 15% to 20% in the fourth quarter.
Reuters cited its sources as saying that Solidigm wants to install more chipmaking equipment in spare space at SK Hynix’s Dalian factory in China to boost NAND chip production.
SK Hynix told TechCrunch it is not seeking to expand capacity at its Dalian Mod B facility, which was completed in 2023. The chip giant added that the equipment installation is being carried out in consultation with and under authorization from the U.S. government.
Washington first imposed sweeping restrictions on advanced chips and chipmaking equipment exports to China in October 2022, citing national security concerns, and further tightened the rules in 2023. Then in September 2025, the Trump administration revoked special export exemptions for certain SK Hynix, Samsung, and Intel facilities in China. The U.S. has since granted an annual license to Samsung and SK Hynix for sending chipmaking equipment to their plants in China.
The U.S. has also been pushing foreign chipmakers to build and expand their manufacturing facilities in America. In July, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said he wanted Samsung and SK Hynix to build chip plants in the country and that he was in talks with both companies.
Solidigm is said to be preparing for a 2027 U.S. IPO that could raise around $10 billion and value it at up to $100 billion.

articles.title: Thị trường laptop đứng trước sức ép kép: Giá linh kiện tăng, sức mua suy yếu
articles.text:
Theo TrendForce, lượng máy tính xách tay xuất xưởng toàn cầu có thể giảm tới 10% vào năm 2027 do chi phí linh kiện cao và nhu cầu tiêu dùng suy yếu.
Trong báo cáo ngành mới nhất, TrendForce dự báo rằng lượng xuất xưởng máy tính xách tay toàn cầu có thể giảm từ vài phần trăm đến gần 10% vào năm 2027. Các nhà sản xuất máy tính xách tay sẽ phải xem xét lại chiến lược sản xuất của họ, khi chi phí gia tăng khiến việc sản xuất bên ngoài Trung Quốc trở nên kém hấp dẫn.
Dự kiến, tỷ lệ sản xuất máy tính xách tay toàn cầu bên ngoài Trung Quốc sẽ giảm từ 24% vào năm 2025 xuống 21% vào năm 2026 và có thể xuống dưới 20% vào năm 2027.
Mối lo ngại lớn nhất hiện nay không còn là vấn đề nguồn cung linh kiện, mà là nhu cầu tiêu dùng suy yếu. Các nhà sản xuất vẫn phải đối mặt với giá cao của CPU, DRAM và SSD. TrendForce cảnh báo rằng nếu giá linh kiện tiếp tục duy trì ở mức cao, các thương hiệu có thể chuyển phần lớn chi phí này sang người tiêu dùng.
Dự báo cho thấy lượng máy tính xách tay xuất xưởng sẽ tăng nhờ nguồn cung CPU được cải thiện và các nhà sản xuất tích trữ linh kiện nhiều hơn trong năm 2026. Tuy nhiên, điều này không đảm bảo nhu cầu thị trường sẽ ổn định. Nhiều khách hàng đã nâng cấp thiết bị sớm hơn dự kiến do lo ngại về giá cả, dẫn đến việc ít người có nhu cầu mua máy tính xách tay mới vào năm 2027.
Khi lượng hàng tồn kho mua với giá thấp dần cạn kiệt, các nhà sản xuất sẽ phải đối mặt với áp lực lớn hơn trong việc gánh chịu chi phí linh kiện cao hoặc chuyển gánh nặng đó sang người tiêu dùng.
Việc tăng giá bán lẻ có thể làm suy yếu thêm nhu cầu, trong khi việc gánh chịu chi phí bổ sung sẽ làm giảm biên lợi nhuận. Các nhà sản xuất cũng có thể điều chỉnh thông số kỹ thuật, như dung lượng bộ nhớ, để kiểm soát chi phí sản xuất, điều này có thể khiến sản phẩm của họ kém cạnh tranh hơn.
Theo ước tính, CPU, DRAM và SSD chiếm khoảng 68% chi phí linh kiện (BOM) của các dòng máy tính xách tay phổ thông với giá bán lẻ đề xuất là 900 USD trong quý 3 năm 2026. TrendForce cho biết các nhà sản xuất khó có thể duy trì đồng thời giá cả, thông số kỹ thuật và lợi nhuận trong năm 2027.
Chi phí linh kiện tăng cao sẽ tiếp tục gây áp lực lên các nhà sản xuất. Trong khi nguồn cung DRAM có thể vẫn khan hiếm do nhu cầu về AI, nguồn cung NAND flash lại có thể được cải thiện trong nửa cuối năm 2027.
Thách thức lớn nhất của ngành sẽ là liệu người tiêu dùng có chấp nhận mức giá máy tính xách tay cao hơn hay không. Nếu các nhà sản xuất quản lý để hạn chế việc tăng giá bằng cách điều chỉnh thông số kỹ thuật và gánh chịu một số chi phí, lượng hàng xuất xưởng có thể giảm nhẹ trong năm 2027. Tuy nhiên, nếu chi phí cao hơn được chuyển sang người tiêu dùng, mức giảm có thể lên tới một con số hai chữ số.

articles.title: Meta opens a weaker AI model while keeping the frontier closed
articles.text:
Meta has published the weights for Muse Spark Open, a coding and agent model it says is less advanced than the Muse Wonder frontier model it launched on Monday. Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said Meta will generally not open-source its most powerful models, which is the split the EU AI Act’s open-source exemption is built around.
Meta has published the weights for a model it says is deliberately not its best, and put the policy on the record. In Europe, that split is the one the AI Act’s open-source exemption is built around.
Bloomberg reported the release on Thursday. Muse Spark Open is built for coding and agents, and Meta says it is less capable than Muse Wonder, which launched on Monday.
“Because of both safety and capabilities, we will generally not open-source our most powerful models,” Alexandr Wang said. He said Meta intends to keep releasing good open models.
The weights sit on Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI and Google Cloud Model Garden. One platform serving it is Nebius, the Dutch firm Meta has committed up to $27B to.
Meta said on Monday that Muse Wonder had reached the frontier, and published no benchmarks. That model stays closed.
This is the second open release from the Muse line. Meta published Glimmer in August, a 30-billion-parameter model distilled from Muse Spark, under Apache 2.0. It also worked with Apple so the new model runs on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios.
In September the company had not decided whether to publish the weights for Muse Spark 1.3. It has answered with a different model instead.
Article 53 of the AI Act exempts a genuinely free and open model from the documentation owed to the AI Office. The exemption stops at systemic risk, where every obligation applies whatever the licence.
Meta’s founder said close to the opposite five weeks ago. Zuckerberg told the Sources podcast that rivals training more advanced models and then not releasing them was quite dangerous. He named no company.
The Commission can fine 3% of global turnover and demand evaluations before release. Meta declined to sign the code of practice written to operationalise those duties, and Joel Kaplan said last year that Europe was on the wrong path.
Wang said most of the world’s AI will run on open models, and that they should be American. Eight days earlier, Alibaba chairman Joe Tsai told a Turin conference that open source was Europe’s only way to independence.
Wang expects Chinese developers to build on Muse Spark Open, and said it might even be good if they adopted its principles.
Europe’s own answer is already in the market. Mistral launched Large 4, a trillion-parameter open-weight model, to take on China’s lead in this category.

articles.title: CitizenLab details new spyware triggered by online advertising - Engadget
articles.text:
CitizenLab details new spyware triggered by online advertising
It requires 'no interaction' from victims to infect devices.
A new type of spyware dubbed "AdFection" is infecting phones and computers via global online advertising networks, according to a new report from Citizen Lab. The attack is unique in that it can infect devices just by showing an ad, with no need for the victim to click on a link or file. The researchers said that AdFection is the first confirmation of zero-click government-backed spyware attacks being delivered through online ads.
The ad-infiltrating technology was reportedly developed by Israeli company called Discover-Tech. Researchers said it has been used to target journalists and staff at the Al Jazeera news network, along with officials and employees at organizations including NATO, the European Commission, NVIDIA and Arm.
"Discover-Tech has leveraged the advertising ecosystem for years to turn trusted websites and popular apps into a zero-click spyware delivery platform," Citizen Lab senior researcher Bill Marczak told The Financial Times. Discover-Tech presents itself as a legitimate advertising firm but instead serves as a "bridge between ad vendors and the mercenary spyware ecosystem," Citizen Lab's report states
Google was among the major ad platforms targeted by the spyware, but it has now suspended Discover-Tech from its global vendor list. "Following a joint investigation with Citizen Lab and Confiant, Google blocked Discover-Tech from our ad platforms for systematically violating our policies," the company said in a statement.
Targeted online advertising is a highly desirable medium to spread malware because it's prevalent on the web globally. It works though an automated real-time bidding auction system that lets advertisers compete to show ads to specific internet users. Discover-Tech's software used the system instead to profile and de-anonymize such users before targeting them with spyware, the report states. Victims were then sent malicious malware code buried in innocent-looking ads.
Discover-Tech reportedly displayed 442 million ads on more than 120,000 websites, including the BBC and New York Times, along with mobile apps like Duolingo, Badoo and Grindr. The ads were shown on devices used by militaries, governments, critical infrastructure and national cyber agencies. Citizen Lab researchers found login records on Discover-Tech's site, including details belonging to employees of the spyware maker Candiru.
The discovery is "surely just the tip of the iceberg," Marczak said in the blog post. "If you might be targeted based on who you are or what you do, it's time to disable ad tracking on your devices or even block ads altogether." Discover-Tech and other players in the scheme have yet to comment.

articles.title: AI agents are coming to Rivian's cars | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Rivian recently rolled out an AI assistant that lets drivers and passengers interact with the company’s electric vehicles just by talking to them. But the carmaker’s founder and CEO, RJ Scaringe, said at TechCrunch Disrupt this week that, in the future, Rivian’s cars will be able to run AI agents made by other companies like Anthropic.
“That’s where it becomes magical,” Scaringe said onstage.
Scaringe didn’t say when Rivian would implement this, and the company declined to offer more details, pointing instead to the “AI & Autonomy Day” event it’s hosting in December.
But it’s not hard to imagine how Rivian might integrate something like Claude, OpenAI’s Dots, or Meta’s Muse assistant into its software. The company has developed its in-car software from the ground up, instead of leaning on Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, and built a lot of its own applications, like navigation (though it has worked to integrate popular in-car apps like Apple Music).
Rivian says it has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. Most of the time, that involves what you’d expect: asking the car to turn down the temperature, activate the seat warmers, or summarize the news.
“Think of it as like a traffic light. So if you ask the vehicle something, it decides what model it’s going to use. It can use a local model that’s running on the edge and the vehicle. If it’s a more complex question, it can go up to the cloud. And then even for that, we have different models that we use,” Scaringe said.
As of May of this year, the agent could access external apps like Google Calendar. And Scaringe said at Disrupt the next step would be to add products from the frontier AI companies, though making them work in the car won’t be easy.
“There’s a lot of plumbing behind the scenes we have to do to make sure that that works, and it’s not just within Rivian. That’s also a lot of coordination with the labs to make sure they enable that plumbing,” he said, adding that putting this kind of software near safety-critical systems means Rivian has to be extremely careful.
“You wouldn’t want an agent to determine, ‘hey, it’s time to apply the brakes, or time to steer the vehicle.’ So anything that’s vehicle-level controls are not being handed to an agent,” he said.
Instead, he thinks the implementation will look more like an extension of how people currently use these agentic apps. That would mean Rivian would have to find a way to connect the vehicle to all of the context that apps like Muse collect on their users.
For example, Scaringe said, a driver could ask the Rivian assistant to turn on the ventilated seats before going deeper. “And then simultaneously say, ‘We were talking yesterday about this meal. I’m planning to have guests over on Friday. Can you help me think through what we’re going to make?’,” he said. The car could then pull the driver’s context from a conversation they had with the assistant on another device.
Of course, Rivian wouldn’t be the first American car company to add AI agents to a car’s software. Earlier this year, Tesla added a feature that let users talk to both SpaceX’s Grok chatbot and also its Grok Bot assistant.

articles.title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
articles.text:
OpenAI’s ChatGPT Atlas browser is gone, but now ChatGPT’s Google Chrome extension is getting some upgrades that allow it to use the browser tabs you already have open. With the extension installed, OpenAI says ChatGPT can now view your browser tabs when you tag Chrome in ChatGPT’s web or desktop app, posting a demo video showing someone asking ChatGPT to compare the three tabs they have open with sofas they’re considering.
ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
With the ChatGPT extension installed, it can pull information from your open tabs or bring the AI bot into the sidebar.
Here are some of the sample queries OpenAI listed for using the upgraded add-on:
- Use the details in this event brief to fill out the registration form, and stop before submitting.
- Put the vendors in these tabs into my comparison sheet, with pricing, key features, and source links.
- Look at all the tabs I have open and compare the contractor services. Then draft an email to the one that fits my home renovation.
- Fill out the form I have open in @chrome ahead of seeing my new dentist. Also, can you add the appointment to my work and personal calendar.
It’s also updated ChatGPT in the sidebar, with “the full power of ChatGPT” and your entire conversation history in Chat or Work to use without leaving the page you’re viewing. It also enables ChatGPT Work to “control” your Chrome tabs for tasks like “sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files,” similar to Google’s Gemini-powered “auto browse” feature, as well as organize or group open tabs.

articles.title: Sự trỗi dậy của những "trang trại" streamer AI: Chiêu làm giàu mới đang càn quét ngành thương mại điện tử ở Trung Quốc
articles.text:
Không cần ánh đèn studio lộng lẫy, không tiếng hô hào của ê-kíp, những "trang trại người ảo" với hàng trăm chiếc điện thoại chạy song song đang âm thầm thao túng ngành thương mại điện tử Trung Quốc, tạo ra doanh số khổng lồ với chi phí gần như bằng 0.
Tại các đô thị công nghệ của Trung Quốc như Hàng Châu hay Shenzhen, một mô hình vận hành thương mại điện tử mới đang mọc lên như nấm: Các trang trại người ảo (Digital Human Farms).
Khác với hình ảnh một studio chuyên nghiệp chỉ có 1-2 streamer người thật, những "trang trại" này thực chất là những căn phòng chất đầy các kệ kim loại. Trên đó xếp hàng trăm, thậm chí hàng nghìn chiếc điện thoại thông minh hoặc máy tính đang cắm sạc liên tục. Trên mỗi màn hình là một "bản sao kỹ thuật số" (Digital Human) đang thao thao bất tuyệt giới thiệu sản phẩm, phát mã giảm giá và chốt đơn 24/7.
Chỉ với một vài kỹ thuật viên điều khiển trung tâm, toàn bộ "quần thể" streamer AI này có thể phủ sóng cùng lúc hàng nghìn phòng livestream trên Douyin (TikTok Trung Quốc), Taobao, Kuaishou cho đến TikTok Shop quốc tế.
Từ vài phút dữ liệu đến "đội quân" streamer số
Bí mật đằng sau các trang trại này là sự bùng nổ của công nghệ AI tạo hình và mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn (LLM).
Để "sản xuất" ra một streamer ảo, doanh nghiệp chỉ cần quay một đoạn video mẫu dài khoảng 3 - 5 phút của người thật và thu âm vài câu nói. Thuật toán AI sẽ lập tức trích xuất khuôn mặt, khẩu hình, cử chỉ tay chân cho đến ngữ điệu giọng nói để tạo ra một bản sao kỹ thuật số hoàn chỉnh giống thật đến 99%.
Sau khi tạo mẫu, "người ảo" sẽ được nạp kịch bản bán hàng và kết nối với hệ thống AI xử lý thời gian thực. Bằng cách quét bình luận (comment) của khán giả, người ảo có thể tự động ngắt lời để trả lời thắc mắc về kích thước quần áo, phí ship hay chính sách đổi trả, tạo cảm giác tương tác tự nhiên như người thật.
Một cỗ máy "in tiền" không bao giờ ngủ
Động lực cốt lõi khiến các trang trại livestream người ảo mọc lên như nấm tại thị trường Trung Quốc chính là bài toán tối ưu hóa chi phí đến mức tối thiểu về gần bằng 0. Nhìn vào một phòng livestream truyền thống, doanh nghiệp phải gánh một bộ máy vận hành cồng kềnh với khoản ngân sách đắt đỏ. Họ không chỉ trả lương và chia hoa hồng cao cho streamer người thật, mà còn phải nuôi cả một ê-kíp rườm rà gồm trợ lý, đạo diễn hình ảnh và kỹ thuật viên âm thanh.
Bên cạnh gánh nặng tài chính, mô hình cũ còn chứa đựng hàng loạt rủi ro vận hành kinh điển, streamer nghỉ việc đột ngột, đòi tăng thù lao khi đã gây dựng được tệp fan, hoặc dính bê bối đời tư làm phá hỏng hợp đồng truyền thông. Quan trọng hơn, sức người luôn có giới hạn. Một streamer dù dẻo dai đến đâu cũng chỉ có thể đứng trước ống kính tối đa 4 - 6 tiếng mỗi ngày.
Trái ngược hoàn toàn với thực trạng tốn kém đó, việc bổ sung thêm một streamer vào trang trại người ảo lại sở hữu mức giá rẻ đến bất ngờ. Doanh nghiệp chỉ cần bỏ ra chi phí khởi tạo ban đầu khoảng 1.000 USD (tương đương 25 triệu đồng) cho một bản sao kỹ thuật số, sau đó duy trì hệ thống phần mềm với mức phí vô cùng "bình dân" chỉ vài chục USD mỗi tháng cho mỗi tài khoản.
Điểm cộng đắt giá nhất của dàn người ảo này là khả năng livestream liên tục 24/7 mà không cần nghỉ ngơi. Cỗ máy AI này dễ dàng phủ kín các khung giờ "thấp điểm" xuyên đêm từ 1h đến 6h sáng, thời điểm các streamer người thật phải đi ngủ nhưng nhu cầu chốt đơn ngẫu hứng của tệp khách hàng thức khuya vẫn rất cao.
Dù doanh số phát sinh trên từng thiết bị ở các khung giờ muộn có thể không tạo nên cú bùng nổ tức thì, nhưng khi nhân với quy mô hàng trăm chiếc điện thoại hoạt động đồng thời trong trang trại, tổng doanh thu tích lũy thu về lại đạt đến một con số cực kỳ khủng khiếp, đi kèm biên lợi nhuận gần như tuyệt đối cho chủ sở hữu.
Khi cuộc chiến bán hàng không còn dành cho con người
Sự bùng nổ của các trang trại người ảo đang giáng một đòn nặng nề vào thị trường lao động, đẩy hàng trăm nghìn streamer tầm trung và những người mới bước chân vào nghề tại Trung Quốc đối mặt với nguy cơ mất việc làm hàng loạt. Khi đặt lên bàn cân, sức người hoàn toàn bất lực và không thể cạnh tranh lại sự kiên trì không biết mệt mỏi, độ chính xác tuyệt đối trong kịch bản cùng mức chi phí "rẻ như cho" của các cỗ máy AI.
Tuy nhiên, đằng sau sự tối ưu hóa tàn khốc đó, mô hình trang trại số này lại đang kéo theo hàng loạt hệ lụy cho toàn bộ hệ sinh thái thương mại điện tử. Đáng quan ngại nhất là rủi ro lừa đảo và xả hàng giả. Các đối tượng xấu có thể dễ dàng dựng lên những trang trại ảo với hàng ngàn tài khoản chạy cùng lúc để đẩy đi các lô hàng kém chất lượng, sau đó lập tức xóa tài khoản và biến mất không dấu vết trước khi cơ quan chức năng kịp can thiệp.
Bên cạnh đó, vấn nạn xâm phạm bản quyền hình ảnh cũng diễn ra vô cùng phức tạp khi không ít đơn vị cố tình "đánh cắp" khuôn mặt, biểu cảm và giọng nói của các hotgirl, KOLs nổi tiếng để đưa vào dàn livestream chui mà không hề xin phép. Hệ quả là các nền tảng bán hàng lớn đang đứng trước nguy cơ bị bóp nghẹt bởi thứ "rác thông tin" (Content Slop), hàng triệu luồng phát sóng vô hồn, công nghiệp, làm tụt giảm nghiêm trọng trải nghiệm mua sắm của người dùng thực.
Bất chấp việc các gã khổng lồ công nghệ như Douyin hay Tencent đã bắt đầu ban hành các chế tài siết chặt kiểm duyệt, đồng thời bắt buộc dán nhãn "Nội dung do AI tạo ra", các trang trại digital humans vẫn liên tục tìm ra kẽ hở để "lách luật".
Không dừng lại ở thị trường nội địa, mô hình này đang nhanh chóng lan rộng sang các nước Đông Nam Á. Cuộc đua thương mại điện tử giờ đây đã chính thức chuyển trục, không còn là cuộc chiến tài năng hay sự duyên dáng giữa các streamer, mà đã biến thành cuộc đấu trí khốc liệt về quy mô phần cứng và sức mạnh thuật toán giữa các trang trại AI./
Thiên Minh

articles.title: Sony revives the Walkman with a $5,899 gold-plated flagship
articles.text:
Sony has revived the Walkman with three digital music players priced from $1,899 to $5,899, the flagship built around a gold-plated oxygen-free copper chassis. No European price or release date has been given, and the EU’s rule on user-replaceable batteries applies from 18 February 2027.
Sony has brought back the Walkman with a flagship costing $5,899. It is built around gold-plated copper and weighs 670g, against 490g for the model it replaces. Sony has not said when it ships, or whether Europe will get one.
Bloomberg reported the launch on Thursday. Three players are on pre-order, from $1,899 to $5,899, the first new hardware in several years to carry the name.
The NW-WM1ZM3 uses an oxygen-free copper chassis of 99.99% purity, gold-plated, with screws given their own gold-plated treatment.
Sony says those screws provide “a stable ground connection that delivers powerful bass, an expansive soundstage, and smooth, extended high frequencies“.
The $2,999 NW-WM1AM3 and the $1,899 NW-ZX900 pair an aluminium chassis with a gold-plated copper back. All three run Android. The cheapest model jumps to Android 16 from the Android 12 on its predecessor, and to a 1080p screen from 720p.
Rivals undercut every tier. Astell and Kern’s SP4000 sells for $4,290 and Cayin’s N8iii for $3,999, while the iBasso DX340 and FiiO M27 both come in below the cheapest Sony at $1,799.
For compressed files, Sony says the players use AI to identify the genre and lift the high frequencies. It also quotes battery life on 128kbps MP3, a format nobody spending $5,899 would play. TNW once failed a blind test between a 320kbps stream and a lossless file on $400 headphones.
A 2013 survey cited in that piece put 151 listeners through the same comparison. Fifty-two per cent preferred the lossy files.
Europe is the part Sony has not addressed. EU battery rules require portable batteries in electronic devices to be removable and replaceable by the owner from 18 February 2027.
Spare batteries must stay available for five years after the last unit is sold, and a compatible battery from another brand has to work. Sealed players of this kind sit inside that definition.
The Dutch company Fairphone sells a $650 phone with twelve user-replaceable parts and a battery the owner can take out. Sony’s flagship is sealed.
Sony says the packaging for all three uses no plastic. A footnote excludes coatings and adhesives, and adds that this varies by region.
The EU banned unsubstantiated generic environmental claims on 27 September, eighteen days before this launch. Sony has still not said when Europe can buy one. It built the same thing in 2016, when the NW-WM1Z cost $3,680.

articles.title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Expense management company Ramp said on Thursday that it had raised $1.85 billion in a new funding round that values it at $60 billion, just four months after raising $750 million at a $44 billion valuation.
The financing was co-led by Dragoneer Investment Group, Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital, and Avenir Growth.
Ramp said its annualized revenue has crossed $2 billion, up from a reported $1.5 billion in June, and that its revenue growth is 25% faster than it was around this time last year. The company claims it now facilitates annualized purchase volume of over $275 billion, up 175% from a year earlier. It also says it has 85,000 customers, up from 70,000 in June, including Visa, Uber, Shopify, Robinhood, Anduril, Notion, Cursor, and Figma.
The funding comes as Ramp has been expanding beyond expense management into payments, fraud detection, procurement, vendor management, and, of late, even accounting.
The startup has also built an AI story around itself, embedding AI agents into its procurement, expense management, accounting, budgeting, and other products. It also launched a corporate credit card specifically designed for AI agents to use, and in August entered the model routing business to tap the booming AI inference market and give existing clients a model routing service that fits neatly with its current products, including AI token usage monitoring and token spend management.
Earlier this month, Ramp launched Glass, a workspace that collects and remembers the AI automations, prompts, and skills that an organization’s employees build so others can take advantage of the company’s collective knowledge and skills.
“In just a few years, Ramp has become a much broader financial operations platform, with AI deeply embedded in how the company builds and operates. We believe Ramp is well on its way to becoming one of the defining companies of this era,” Christian Jensen, partner at Dragoneer, said in a statement.
Other investors in the round include Capital International, Fidelity Management & Research Company, T. Rowe Price, D1 Capital Partners, Greenoaks, ICONIQ, GIC, 8VC, 1789 Capital, Alpha Wave Global, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Coatue, D.E. Shaw, Definition Capital, FirstMark, General Catalyst, Generation Investment Management, Glade Brook Capital Partners, Khosla Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pinegrove Opportunity Partners, Soma Capital, and Stripes.
The company has now raised about $5 billion in funding.
As Ramp has widened its product lineup, it has increasingly run into Rippling, the HR and payroll software company that has pushed into corporate cards, expense management, and bill payments. The overlap puts the two companies in direct competition for the same finance-team budgets.
Early investor Keith Rabois, who has backed Ramp through two firms, Founders Fund and Khosla Ventures, both of which participated in this round, spoke to TechCrunch last month about Ramp’s strategy and his own big ambitions for the company.
“Ramp is not worried about Rippling,” Rabois said. “We’re going to compete with Anthropic,” he continued. “That’s the goal. I want to be larger and more successful and more important than Anthropic. Ramp is going to be the primary way people manage their token spend, how they optimize it, how they measure ROI, and that will lead us to collide probably with Anthropic in many ways.”
— With additional reporting from Connie Loizos

articles.title: Bee unveils two AI note-taking devices, its first new products since being acquired by Amazon - Engadget
articles.text:
Bee unveils two AI note-taking devices, its first new products since being acquired by Amazon
The Eclipse and Frontier are cheap and colorful, but you'll need a Pro subscription to make the most of them.
Just over a year after being acquired by Amazon, wearable AI startup Bee has quite a few products to unveil. It's introducing two new AI devices today, alongside a Pro subscription offering and some software updates.
First up is the Bee Frontier, which is essentially a follow-up to and replacement of the previous Pioneer. Like it, the Frontier is basically a Fitbit-like module that you can slot into a bracelet or a clip so you can attach it to your clothes or bags. It has an onboard button, like the Pioneer, to initiate a note-taking session or invoke the app's Buzz AI assistant, as well as an LED indicator to convey when it's listening or charging, for instance.
But the Frontier has evolved from its first-gen predecessor, which cost $50 and seemed like a product that would appeal most to early adopters. This new version is not only smaller and lighter, but also comes in more colors. The original was only available in one version, and in the box with it came a black band and a yellow band, along with a clip attachment. That selection might fit the bee (insect) vibes, but certainly isn't the most sartorially versatile. I'm a fan of the Lavender and Sage color options for the Bee Frontier, and those who want something more generic can opt for the black (Onyx) version.
Additionally, the Frontier is rated IP67 for dust and water resistance, according to Amazon, whereas the Pioneer was not even water-resistant. Both models have dual microphones with noise filtering to tune out background chatter, though the effectiveness of the Frontier's attempts at this will require in-depth testing to determine.
Those are the main physical differences between the Frontier and the Pioneer. The two share the same 7-day battery life estimate, USB-C charging port and similar functionality. One press of the button can initiate a recording session, where Bee listens to your surroundings and delivers transcripts and summaries of conversations. Pressing and holding the button allows you to ask a question of the AI assistant or leave yourself a voice note.
The Bee Frontier is available now for $75 at Amazon, and you may want to wait till full reviews are out to decide if the water resistance, new colors and smaller size are worth the money. The Pioneer is no longer available to purchase.
The Bee Eclipse is a magnetic AI note taker for your phone
The other piece of hardware that Bee is announcing today is the Eclipse — a magnetic, rectangular puck you can snap onto your phone. It's like a thicker credit card with three onboard microphones, a button on the top left corner and an LED indicator light next to it. The Eclipse is a lot bigger than the Frontier, which also means it can last a lot longer. In fact, it offers three times the battery life, with Bee promising it will last "more than 21 days."
This is a new type of device for Bee, since it's not really a wearable for people and more like a wearable for phones. But at its core the Eclipse basically performs the same functions as a Frontier (or Pioneer). You can push a button to start a session, the indicator light turns on and the AI gets to work, summarizing your discussions and attempting to identify who is speaking or what is being said.
The company said that "like all Bee devices, audio is never stored, cannot be accessed or shared, and users are prompted to gain permission from call participants each time a recording is started." It added that the Eclipse, like the Frontier, "is designed with privacy at its core, with one button to turn it on or off and a visible indicator light on when it's summarizing a conversation."
While the rationale behind a little light signaling to people nearby that a device might be recording is sound, it's worth noting that the shape, size and magnetic attachment of the Eclipse means it closely resembles a portable battery charger. Those things have indicator lights as well, and it can be easy to see how someone might assume an indicator LED means something is charging, rather than listening.
Still, Bee is far from the only company making AI note-taking devices that snap onto your phone. There's Pocket, Plaud, Comu, Innaio, Ruune, Raycon and undoubtedly countless more littering the venture capital-fueled grounds of Silicon Valley. And the issues that Bee's Eclipse will run into relating to its form factor will likely be faced by the entire category as well.
If Bee's offering is of interest and you have $100 to spare, you can get the Eclipse in one of four admittedly attractive colors — Silver, Midnight, Honey and Blush. Amazon says it will be "available soon," and nothing more specific on time frame has been shared.
Bee Pro subscription, plus Amazon and Alexa+ integrations
The company is also unveiling the Bee Pro subscription plan today. For $11.99 a month, it offers some additional features like unlimited recent conversation summaries, suggested to-dos, daily memories, conversation templates, daily memories and a few new integrations that were also announced today.
Before I get into those, though, a quick note for existing Bee users. If you're feeling nervous as these sound like features you've been enjoying and you're concerned they might suddenly be wrested away and put behind a paywall, you might not be affected. Bee's founder Maria Zollo told me in a briefing that for the customers that have been with the company since its early days, "as a sign of gratitude, we're giving to them the Bee they have today." Zollo added that for them, the "entire featureset is free forever." (All new Bee customers also get 30 days of free Bee Pro use.)
If you want the features I'm about to mention, then you'll need a Pro subscription. First, the company is expanding its in-app integrations, which previously included Google Calendar, Gmail and Apple's HealthKit. It's introducing "the ability to connect to Alexa+ and Amazon.com." If you connect it to your Amazon account, your Bee can suggest items you might have mentioned in conversations that you wanted to purchase. These product recommendations will show up on Amazon's homepage, as well as in the Bee apps. You'll also be able to create custom shopping lists including things that came up in your conversations.
If you connect Bee to Alexa+, you can ask your Echo or other Alexa-enabled device for information that your Bee might know. This could be anything from conversation summaries, to-dos or book recommendations from friends. With this enabled, you won't have to hunt for and open the Bee app on your phone and ask for what you want — you can just ask your speaker or TV to do so. Amazon said that the Alexa devices would use voice identification to ascertain that it's you and not, say, a random interloper or nosy partner, before sharing the information.
Amazon stressed that both these features are opt-in, so the user has to give permission before information is shared.
Finally, Bee is launching a desktop app for Mac or Windows, which you can access with a Pro plan. This doesn't just give you access to your recaps and chats on your computer, but also allows you to do additional transcribing from the desktop. It's as full-featured as the mobile app.
A refresher on Bee Private Compute
Given the recent controversy around Apple's Audio Intelligence features — specifically Siri Recap and Live Rewind — it's worth bringing up Bee's "Private Compute." It's what the company described in a blog post on September 24 (about two weeks after the Apple launch) as a "secure and isolated processing environment that no one, including Amazon and Bee, can access." That's not to say this did not exist prior to the Apple event — the post does not make that very clear, other than saying that "Amazon and Bee developed Private Compute from the ground up, and the technology builds on the foundation of the AWS Nitro System and its AWS Nitro Trusted Platform Module."
In today's announcement, Amazon reiterated the tenets of Bee Private Compute, including reminders that no audio is ever stored. "Audio is processed into insights in real time and deleted after processing," the company said in a press release. It also said that no one can access your data unless you choose to share it, transcripts are encrypted using keys that can only be created and controlled by your device and that you can delete your transcripts and summaries whenever you want.

articles.title: Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
articles.text:
Sega is removing Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from storefronts following a disastrous launch where users complained about issues like bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI.
Sega pulls Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale following disastrous launch
Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition is being removed after users discovered bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI.
Complete Edition, a remaster of the 2011 strategy game, launched on Tuesday, and it bundled the main game and all of its DLC with promised upgrades including “improved visuals,” “1440p and 4K UI scaling,” and modernized controls. It has an “Overwhelmingly Negative” rating on Steam, where it has already been pulled, and posts on Reddit showcase artwork that users believe AI messed up.
“We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Sega and developer Creative Assembly wrote in a post. “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.” The two companies say they will “reinstate the original game,” and existing owners will “still be able to access” Complete Edition.
Sega and Creative Assembly say that they are “working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 - Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.” A studio called Mataboo is also listed as a developer for the game on Steam, and Mataboo highlights its work on the game on its website.

articles.title: United will now let you check if your flight has Starlink Wi-Fi - Engadget
articles.text:
United will now let you check if your flight has Starlink Wi-Fi
The airline says nearly half of its daily departures now offer Starlink.
United has launched a new tracking tool that will give you a way to make sure your flight has Starlink Wi-Fi. The airline first announced its partnership with SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service in September 2024 and started testing it a few months later, in January 2025. Now, the company has revealed that it already has 635 United mainline and United Express Starlink-equipped planes and that the satellite internet service is now available on nearly half of its daily departures.
The airline will still tell you if your flight offers Starlink Wi-Fi in its pre-flight emails and text notifications. But the new tracker can keep you updated in case of any changes, such as if United had to swap your plane. You can enter your flight number and your travel date within three days of your departure, and the tracker will show you any updates or last-minute hardware changes in real time. It can also show you the daily departures with Starlink onboard, as well as let you explore how many regional, narrowbody and widebody airplanes offer the speedier Wi-Fi option. You can view the availability of Starlink flights per hub, as well, specifically flights in Chicago, Newark, Washington, DC, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Houston and Denver.
According to Starlink Flights, which tracks the satellite internet's availability per airline, United has the most number of Starlink flights at the moment. The airline says it's expanding availability further and installing the satellite internet on 20 planes per week, in hopes of completing installations by the end of 2027. Other airlines that offer Starlink internet including Emirates, Qatar Airways, WestJet, SAS, Alaska Airlines and Air France.

articles.title: Thực hư việc mua iPhone Duo phải cọc 30 triệu đồng, hủy cọc mất phí 5%?
articles.text:
Khách hàng muốn mua iPhone Duo được thông báo phải đặt cọc 30 triệu đồng từ ngày 16/10, nhận máy từ ngày 23/10. Trên mạng xã hội, thông tin người mua có thể mất phí 5% nếu hủy cọc đang gây chú ý.
Theo thông tin ghi nhận từ một số chuỗi bán lẻ, khách hàng đặt trước iPhone Duo sẽ phải cọc 30 triệu đồng mỗi máy. Cụ thể, mỗi số điện thoại được đặt tối đa một máy. Thời gian nhận đặt cọc bắt đầu từ 19h ngày 16/10/2026, thời gian mở bán và trả hàng dự kiến từ 8h ngày 23/10/2026. Số lượng máy có hạn, khách hàng đặt cọc sớm được ưu tiên.
Tuy nhiên, bên cạnh thông tin về mức cọc, trên mạng xã hội đang xuất hiện những xôn xao về khả năng khách hàng phải chịu phí 5% nếu không nhận máy.
Theo tìm hiểu, hiện chưa có thông tin chính thức được xác minh cho thấy khách hàng hủy đặt cọc iPhone Duo sẽ phải chịu khoản phí 5%.
Trao đổi với một số đại diện chuỗi bán lẻ tại Việt Nam, được biệt hiện các chuỗi không có chính sách về việc khách hàng phải chịu phí khi bỏ cọc. Người mua cần kiểm tra điều khoản cụ thể của đơn vị nhận cọc để xác định quyền lợi và nghĩa vụ khi hủy đơn.
Một người am hiểu trong ngành nhận định, việc yêu cầu khách hàng đặt cọc số tiền lớn nhằm hạn chế tình trạng đầu cơ, đồng thời giúp nhà bán lẻ xác định nhu cầu thực tế trong bối cảnh nguồn cung hạn chế.
Theo người này, động thái trên cho thấy doanh nghiệp muốn xác thực nhu cầu thị trường do lượng máy có thể cung ứng chưa đáp ứng đủ. Việc đặt cọc trước cũng giúp hệ thống bán lẻ ghi nhận nhu cầu và phân bổ số lượng máy trong giai đoạn đầu mở bán.
Theo công bố của Apple, iPhone Duo là mẫu iPhone gập đầu tiên của hãng, có giá khởi điểm 64,999 triệu đồng tại Việt Nam. Máy có hai màu Trắng Ánh Sao và Trời Đêm, các tùy chọn bộ nhớ 256GB, 512GB, 1TB và 2TB.
Thiết bị sở hữu màn hình OLED bên trong kích thước 7,6 inch và màn hình ngoài 5,4 inch, hỗ trợ tần số quét thích ứng ProMotion lên đến 120Hz. Khi mở ra, máy có độ dày 5,2 mm, sử dụng khung titan và bản lề được thiết kế cho dạng điện thoại gập.
Về cấu hình, iPhone Duo trang bị chip A20 Pro, hệ thống camera sau gồm camera chính Fusion 48MP và camera góc siêu rộng Fusion 48MP, cùng camera trước 12MP Center Stage. Máy có hệ thống hai pin, cảm biến vân tay Touch ID tích hợp ở nút sườn và thiết kế eSIM.
Động thái đặt cọc 30 triệu đồng cho iPhone Duo diễn ra sau khi bộ đôi iPhone 18 Pro và iPhone 18 Pro Max ghi nhận nhu cầu lớn tại Việt Nam. Trong ngày nhận cọc dòng sản phẩm trên, các hệ thống bán lẻ trong nước nhận gần 300.000 đơn đặt cọc cho hai mẫu máy trong chưa đầy một ngày kể từ khi mở chương trình đặt trước tối 12/9.
Với iPhone Duo, mức cọc 30 triệu đồng cao hơn đáng kể so với khoản cọc 1 triệu đồng phổ biến khi đặt trước iPhone 18 Pro và Pro Max tại các đại lý. Do đó, bên cạnh sức hút của mẫu iPhone gập đầu tiên, điều khoản hủy đơn và hoàn tiền sẽ là yếu tố người mua cần cân nhắc trước khi quyết định đặt cọc.

articles.title: Nvidia's Huang says CoreWeave needs no backstop, as its credit swaps hit a record
articles.text:
Jensen Huang told Bloomberg in Stockholm that CoreWeave’s cost of capital is decreasing and that Nvidia does not need to backstop the company. On the same day CoreWeave’s five-year credit default swaps hit a record 1,194.5 basis points, pricing a more than 60% chance of default within five years.
Jensen Huang said in Stockholm on Thursday that CoreWeave is getting financially stronger and that Nvidia has no need to backstop it. On the same day, the credit market priced a better than 60% chance that CoreWeave defaults within five years.
“CoreWeave’s strength is improving every day,” the Nvidia chief executive told Bloomberg. “I’m optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing.”
CoreWeave’s five-year credit default swaps rose by as much as 74.5 basis points to 1,194.5, the highest intraday level on record, according to ICE Data Services.
Nvidia is CoreWeave’s second-largest shareholder, with a stake of about 10%. It also sells the company the chips its business is built on.
In June those same contracts had fallen to 452 basis points from a December 2025 peak, and a bond backed by a CoreWeave lease priced at 7%. The spread has since roughly tripled.
CoreWeave’s total debt stood at about $30B in June, roughly three times the level a year earlier, on a speculative-grade rating. Its backlog had reached $99.4B by July, against a 2026 capital spending budget of $31B to $35B.
Huang says no backstop is needed here. Nvidia is separately reported to be in talks to backstop $250bn of OpenAI’s data-centre financing.
That guarantee would cover the lease and construction debt on a 10-gigawatt campus in Ohio. Neither company has confirmed it.
Nvidia’s own credit has been repriced as well. Its five-year swaps hit a record 82 basis points in July, when its own credit market flinched at $750B of announced deals.
The concern is circularity. Nvidia takes stakes in, or guarantees debt for, customers who spend the money on Nvidia hardware, which critics say inflates demand. Huang has called the idea “ridiculous“, while the IMF and the Bank for International Settlements have flagged it as a systemic risk.
He is in Europe selling the opposite story. In Paris on Monday he said Europe needs to get in the race, and promised $2B of European investment within a week.
Swedish media reported that he would appear in Stockholm with Sferical AI chief executive Jenny Nordlow and the financier Marcus Wallenberg, before opening an evening event for Nordic business leaders.
Nvidia and the Norrsken Foundation announced a Stockholm AI lab the same morning, opening in 2027. The pitch to Europe and the price of CoreWeave’s debt landed on the same day.

articles.title: Google’s Universal Cart shopping tool launches in the US | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google on Thursday said “Universal Cart,” a tool that lets users collect and monitor products they find across search and in the Gemini app, is now available to U.S. users. The company first previewed the tool at Google I/O in May.
The idea is to make online shopping easier to manage. Find something you like, save it to your cart, and move on. When you return later, your items and shopping progress are still there, so you don’t have to hunt down the same products or start over. Universal Cart can collect items from multiple retailers, turning it into a central hub for browsing and keeping track of potential purchases.
Google says the cart can also help shoppers stay on top of deals and availability. The tool can send notifications when a saved product’s price drops or when an out-of-stock item becomes available again.
The tool is also designed to offer more tailored help during the shopping process. Google says it can take credit card perks into account when helping users choose how to pay, and also surface relevant promo codes.
Checkout is tied to Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, or UCP, an open standard the company introduced earlier this year. UCP is designed to help AI agents and retailers work together across different parts of the shopping journey, including checkout.
Google is already deeply invested in AI-powered shopping, and Universal Cart is its latest effort to make the experience more convenient. It joins features such as conversational product discovery in Search’s AI Mode and Google’s “Let Google Call” tool, which uses an AI agent to contact nearby stores and check whether an item is in stock.
Google isn’t the only company bringing AI into e-commerce. Amazon, OpenAI, and other rivals have added agentic commerce features as companies look for ways to make chatbots useful beyond answering questions.

articles.title: Đăng Quang Watch: Đồng hồ nữ sang trọng, ưu đãi tới 50% dịp 20/10
articles.text:
Mùa quà tặng năm nay Đăng Quang Watch mang đến chương trình giảm tới 50% cho nhiều mẫu đồng hồ nữ. Đây là cơ hội để người mua dễ dàng lựa chọn món quà phù hợp dành tặng mẹ, vợ, người yêu hay những người phụ nữ đặc biệt trong cuộc sống.
Có những món quà được nhớ đến bởi giá trị, nhưng cũng có những món quà ở lại lâu hơn bởi chúng mang dấu ấn của người nhận. Với phụ nữ, một món quà đẹp càng ý nghĩa khi thể hiện được phong cách, sở thích và cá tính riêng.
Đó cũng là lý do đồng hồ nữ ngày càng được lựa chọn trong những dịp đặc biệt. Không chỉ là phụ kiện hoàn thiện trang phục, đồng hồ còn đồng hành trong những khoảnh khắc đời thường - từ ngày làm việc bận rộn, buổi hẹn cuối tuần đến những cuộc gặp gỡ quan trọng.
Mỗi người phụ nữ đều có một “ngôn ngữ” thời trang riêng. Có người yêu vẻ thanh mảnh, nhẹ nhàng; có người chuộng sự sang trọng, nổi bật; cũng có người chọn thiết kế hiện đại để thể hiện cá tính.
Tại Đăng Quang Watch, những phong cách ấy được đáp ứng qua đa dạng mẫu đồng hồ nữ - từ thanh lịch nơi công sở, nữ tính dành tặng người thương đến những thiết kế nổi bật cho người phụ nữ muốn tạo dấu ấn riêng.
Với ưu đãi giảm tới 50%, việc tìm một thiết kế vừa hợp gu, vừa phù hợp ngân sách trở nên dễ dàng hơn trong dịp lễ năm nay.
Chọn quà cho mẹ có thể là một thiết kế trang nhã, dễ đeo và phù hợp với trang phục thường ngày. Với vợ hay người yêu, một mẫu đồng hồ nữ tính, thời trang hoặc có điểm nhấn riêng có thể thay lời muốn nói theo cách tinh tế.
Đôi khi, điều làm nên giá trị của món quà không nằm ở việc nó cầu kỳ hay đắt giá đến đâu, mà ở cảm giác người nhận có thể thấy được sự tinh tế của người tặng. Một thiết kế khiến họ yêu thích, dễ đeo và có thể sử dụng thường xuyên sẽ khiến món quà hiện diện lâu hơn trong cuộc sống.
Vì vậy, thay vì chọn quà theo khuôn mẫu, bạn có thể bắt đầu từ phong cách của người nhận: cô ấy yêu sự tối giản hay nổi bật, nữ tính hay hiện đại? Những chi tiết nhỏ ấy sẽ là gợi ý để tìm ra chiếc đồng hồ phù hợp.
Sức hấp dẫn của đồng hồ nằm ở chỗ nó không chỉ đẹp trong khoảnh khắc trao tặng, mà còn đồng hành cùng người nhận qua thời gian, trở thành một phần phong cách và đôi khi là món quà gợi nhớ về người đã trao.
Với khả năng kết hợp cùng nhiều trang phục và sử dụng trong nhiều hoàn cảnh, đồng hồ nữ mang đến sự cân bằng giữa giá trị thẩm mỹ và tính ứng dụng.
Cùng chương trình giảm tới 50%, đây là thời điểm thuận lợi để lựa chọn một thiết kế yêu thích, biến món quà 20/10 thành món quà vừa tinh tế vừa thiết thực.

articles.title: The tech backlash is now in theaters
articles.text:
Though movies about disruptive tech founders are nothing new, 2026 has been unusually stacked with features that take a much more critical look at how Silicon Valley is reshaping our reality. Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoningframes Mark Zuckerberg as a robotic villain whose ambitions are destabilizing society. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s You Can See Everything paints a damning picture of Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes as she prepares for her ongoing stint in prison. After years of being widely celebrated as a visionary, you can see how the larger narrative around Elon Musk has shifted in projects like Alex Gibney’s Musk documentary. And while Luca Guadagnino’s Artificialis a dark comedy, it is also a character study that makes Sam Altman look like a manipulative sociopath.
The tech backlash is now in theaters
Between The Social Reckoning, You Can See Everything, Musk, and Artificial, filmmakers are taking Big Tech to task.
The tech backlash is now in theaters
Between The Social Reckoning, You Can See Everything, Musk, and Artificial, filmmakers are taking Big Tech to task.
Even though some of these movies are fictionalized dramas, each of them draws from the wealth of critical reporting that has revealed their subjects to be less-than-savory characters. You get the sense that these filmmakers are trying to tell stories that are meant to resonate with audiences whose views of Big Tech have long since begun to dim. But it also feels like some of Hollywood’s biggest studios are finally embracing the idea that the tech backlash isn’t letting up anytime soon.
Especially when you compare them to classics like The Social Network, the latest wave of cinematic dramas based on Silicon Valley power struggles has been far less sympathetic to their central figures. David Fincher’s 2010 film starring Jesse Eisenberg presented Zuckerberg as a complicated and misunderstood savant, but The Social Reckoning builds its story around the idea that the Facebook / Meta head is a man whose obsession with growth poses an existential threat to democracy. By focusing on the allegations leveled by whistleblower Frances Haugen, the movie is able to highlight Zuckerberg’s public transformation into a powerful executive who wields autocratic control over a multibillion-dollar social media empire.
What The Social Reckoning lacks in timeliness (The Wall Street Journal began reporting Haugen’s warnings in 2021) and stylistic flair, it makes up for in the way it connects Facebook / Meta’s past internal decisions to events that are still playing out in real time. The movie’s scenes that dig into Instagram’s negative impacts on teens’ mental health and the relationship between Facebook’s algorithm and the spread of misinformation feel as if they’re speaking directly to present-day concerns about how much influence Meta has over people’s lives. Similarly, Gibney’s Musk documentary acts as both a chronicle of the xAI / SpaceX head’s past and an inquiry into why the public was ever willing to let Musk accrue so much power within governments across the world.
Musk’s response to Gibney’s film has been telling. X has blocked the feature from being advertised on the platform, and Musk — a self-proclaimed “free speech absolutist” — has threatened to take legal action against Gibney for producing a “hit piece.” It wasn’t entirely surprising to see Musk personally badmouthing a project that casts him in a negative light, but it was curious to see the Musk ads initially missing from other social media platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok.
Though the Meta subsidiaries and YouTube ultimately reversed their decisions, TikTok has stuck to its guns — which feels notable given the company’s indirect connections to the Trump administration by way of Skydance Corporation CEO David Ellison. David’s father — Oracle cofounder Larry Ellison — is a longtime Donald Trump supporter and one of the American billionaires who led the consortium of investors that purchased TikTok’s US business late last year. Ellison has reportedly promised Gibney that Musk will air on HBO (now a part of Skydance) sometime next January. The film is currently screening in select theaters, but it is hard to argue that it hasn’t had to deal with an unusual amount of outside interference in the weeks leading up to its release.
Guadagnino’s Artificial — which was originally going to be released by Amazon — also faced unexpected marketing challenges this year. The streaming giant backed out of its deal to distribute the film this past June, just months after announcing that it was investing $50 billion in OpenAI. All of that made it seem very much like Amazon and other studios financially involved with AI companies might be cooling on the idea of releasing projects critical of the technology’s creators. Now that Artificial has begun screening and people have a sense of how it takes Altman to task, it’s easy to see why Amazon didn’t want to have its name attached. More than anything else, that decision may be what convinces people to see Artificial in theaters when it releases widely on December 25th, and OpenAI’s impending IPO could make the movie’s messages about Altman feel that much more relevant.
What sets Fielder’s You Can See Everything apart from each of these other recent tech films is how direct a view it gives you into the actual life of its subject. The documentary’s production began well after Holmes had already been sentenced to more than 11 years in prison, and Fielder uses his access to grill her about why she doesn’t believe that she defrauded Theranos investors. Invited to live with Holmes and her partner William Evans in a rental home during the month before she was set to begin her sentence, Fielder allows himself to become a character who can’t entirely tell whether his hosts’ supposed wish for radical transparency is genuine.
That central tension turns You Can See Everything into a surprisingly fascinating watch that challenges you to consider who’s actually in control of the documentary. Throughout the movie, Fielder repeatedly wonders if Holmes is using him as part of her recent PR campaign, and he leaves the audience to draw their own conclusions.
It often feels like Fielder is asking viewers to really listen to how Holmes presents herself on camera and then reconcile that person with what you might have read about Holmes in the news or seen in Hulu’s The Dropout. Whether or not Holmes is really just a committed performer who’s trying to manipulate the public shapes every beat of the film, and it makes You Can See Everything feel like a truly in-depth and honest examination of one of Silicon Valley’s most infamous figures — one who’s already captured so much of the public’s attention.
Even though some of these films have been box office flops, their existence reflects a larger cultural shift in how people are thinking about modern technology and the powers behind it. Hollywood has spent years poking fun at and mythologizing founders, and portions of the industry are finally beginning to take a more critical view. As we continue to deal with the fallout of things like Elon Musk’s tenure at DOGE and OpenAI’s quest to bake generative AI into every aspect of our lives, audiences’ appetites for movies like these could grow. And with all of these founders racing to monopolize the next tech frontier, the entertainment industry will probably have plenty of source material to draw from.

articles.title: Adobe rebuilt Photoshop and Premiere for NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform - Engadget
articles.text:
Adobe rebuilt Photoshop and Premiere for NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform
The apps were optimized to work faster on RTX Spark computers.
Adobe has "rearchitected" its creative apps, including Photoshop, its video editing software Premiere and its 3D design platform Substance 3D to "take full advantage" of NVIDIA's RTX Spark, according to company VP Deepa Subramaniam. RTX Spark is NVIDIA's new system-on-chip (SoC) that's meant to give Windows laptops and small desktops the capability to run AI tasks locally on device. Unlike NVIDIA's DGX Spark, which mainly targets companies and AI developers, RTX Spark is more accessible to creatives and novice developers.
"Our apps like Photoshop, Premiere and Substance are trusted by the world's most talented storytellers, from photographers and designers creating iconic campaigns, to filmmakers and editors bringing award-winning film and television to life, to artists creating characters and visual effects that bring those stories to the screen," Subramaniam said. "For this audience, performance across creative workflows is critical to allow them to stay focused on their story and craft."
Subramaniam said the optimized apps are two times faster when it comes to AI tasks and editing across workflows. The redesigned Photoshop will be more responsive and faster at rendering complex workflows on computers with RTX Spark. Users will be able to see the changes they make in real time, such as when they're applying effects like Light Leaks (example in the image above) or removing elements from images with the Remove tool.
Meanwhile, Premiere users will be able to enjoy "real, tangible speed gains" when it comes to rendering, applying effects, AI-powered editing and color-grading for audio and video. Finally, the optimized Substance 3D Painter "speeds up the heaviest steps around texturing," as well as many other tasks, such as opening and saving large projects and exporting textures.
