articles.title: Loạt sản phẩm vừa bị Apple cho vào diện "lỗi thời"
articles.text:
Các Apple Store và trung tâm dịch vụ ủy quyền được yêu cầu ngừng sửa chữa phần cứng cho ba sản phẩm này, trừ pin của MacBook.
Ngày 14/10/2026, Apple thêm MacBook 12 inch (2017), iPad thế hệ 6 và tai nghe BeatsX vào danh sách sản phẩm lỗi thời trên trang hỗ trợ. Hãng xếp một sản phẩm vào diện này khi đã qua 7 năm kể từ lần cuối Apple phân phối, kể cả cho đại lý bán lẻ.
Theo quy định, Apple Store và trung tâm dịch vụ ủy quyền phải ngừng sửa chữa phần cứng cho các sản phẩm lỗi thời, đồng thời thường không thể đặt linh kiện. Ngoại lệ là MacBook, vốn có thể vẫn được thay pin trong tối đa 10 năm kể từ khi ngừng phân phối, tùy tình trạng linh kiện.
Trong ba sản phẩm, MacBook 12 inch là cái tên có nhiều chuyện để nhắc lại nhất. Máy ra mắt tháng 3/2015, nặng khoảng 0,9 kg và là chiếc Mac đầu tiên không có quạt tản nhiệt. Máy cũng là Mac đầu tiên có cổng USB-C, nhưng chỉ có đúng một cổng dùng cho cả sạc lẫn truyền dữ liệu, thêm giắc tai nghe 3,5 mm. Ngoài ra, MacBook 12 inch còn mở đầu cho trackpad Force Touch và bàn phím cánh bướm, hai chi tiết sau đó xuất hiện trên dòng MacBook Pro.
Cái giá của thiết kế mỏng nhẹ khá rõ. Bàn phím cánh bướm có hành trình phím ngắn và dễ hỏng. Chip Core M cũng bị đánh giá là sự đánh đổi để giữ máy mỏng, nhẹ và im lặng. Bản cập nhật năm 2017 tăng tốc độ xử lý, nhưng dòng máy vẫn bị Apple ngừng bán ngày 9/7/2019, cùng đợt làm mới MacBook Air và MacBook Pro 13 inch. Bản 2017 dừng ở macOS Ventura, còn bản đời đầu 2015 đã nằm trong danh sách lỗi thời từ giữa năm 2023.
Gần 7 năm sau, Apple vẫn chưa có MacBook nào kích thước dưới 13 inch dùng chip Apple silicon. Trước khi hãng chuyển chip, nhiều người từng dự đoán MacBook 12 inch sẽ là máy đầu tiên được đổi sang chip tự thiết kế, nhưng điều đó chưa xảy ra. Gần nhất là MacBook Neo, công bố ngày 4/3/2026 với màn hình 13 inch và chip A18 Pro của iPhone 16 Pro, không dùng quạt tản nhiệt. Máy nặng khoảng 1,2 kg, nặng hơn MacBook 12 inch chừng 300 g. Tại Việt Nam, MacBook Neo có giá từ 16,49 triệu đồng (tương đương mức 599 USD tại Mỹ), là MacBook rẻ nhất từ trước đến nay.
iPad thế hệ 6 ra mắt ngày 27/3/2018 tại sự kiện giáo dục của Apple ở Chicago. So với đời trước, máy dùng chip A10 Fusion và bổ sung hỗ trợ Apple Pencil. Đây cũng là chiếc iPad cuối cùng có màn hình 9,7 inch nguyên bản. Tháng 9/2019, Apple thay máy bằng iPad thế hệ 7 với màn hình lớn hơn. iPad thế hệ 6 dừng ở iPadOS 17.
BeatsX được Apple công bố cùng iPhone 7 hồi tháng 9/2016, nhưng phải đến 10/2/2017 mới bán ra do bị hoãn. Tai nghe dây đeo sau gáy này dùng chip W1 giống AirPods, giúp ghép nối nhanh với thiết bị Apple, và là sản phẩm Beats đầu tiên sạc qua cổng Lightning. Pin dùng khoảng 8 giờ, sạc nhanh 5 phút cho 2 giờ nghe. Tháng 10/2020, Beats Flex thay thế BeatsX với cổng sạc USB-C.
Với người đang dùng MacBook 12 inch, pin là hạng mục duy nhất Apple có thể còn hỗ trợ. Nếu tính từ khi ngừng bán tháng 7/2019, thời hạn thay pin tối đa 10 năm kéo dài đến khoảng năm 2029, nhưng chỉ khi linh kiện còn.

articles.title: CarbonAI raises $12M to automate commercial real estate underwriting with AI agents
articles.text:
CarbonAI has raised $12M led by Cowboy Ventures for AI agents that handle underwriting, due diligence and post-close monitoring on commercial real estate loans. The EU AI Act treats consumer credit decisions as high-risk but not corporate lending, a line that blurs when a sponsor gives a personal guarantee.
CarbonAI has raised $12M for AI agents that do the analytical work behind commercial property loans. The New York company sells only in the US. In Europe the same software would sit outside the AI Act’s credit rules, until a sponsor signs a personal guarantee.
Cowboy Ventures led the round, according to the announcement, with Timber Grove Ventures, Bling Capital and Max Ventures. Neither a stage nor a valuation was disclosed.
The agents pull figures from rent rolls, leases, financial statements and legal documents, build the underwriting model, draft the memo and flag risks. Each number links back to its source document. Decisions needing human judgment go to the lending team.
Co-founders Jeff Saul and Josh Kaufman underwrote commercial property loans at Starwood Capital, Morgan Stanley and Guggenheim, then built the deal platform Nativ and sold it to Built. Greystone is the only customer named.
Mortgage underwriting agents are high-risk in Europe. Vesta raised $30M last week for agents that make mortgage decisions, work the EU treats very differently.
Annex III of the AI Act covers systems used to evaluate “the creditworthiness of natural persons” or set their credit score, with one carve-out for fraud detection. Companies are not natural persons.
Berlin’s Taktile raised $110M in June for agents that underwrite business loans, and sits outside the same provision for the same reason.
CarbonAI says its customers include debt funds, mortgage real estate investment trusts and agency multifamily lenders. Its borrowers are companies.
The line is not clean. Commercial property loans routinely carry personal guarantees from their sponsors, and the provision bites the moment an individual’s creditworthiness is assessed. Those duties were pushed to December 2027.
The announcement cites a $20 trillion US commercial property market and $875B of mortgages maturing this year, on Mortgage Bankers Association figures, against roughly $50B a year spent underwriting them.
Europe’s market is not in that condition. Revolut’s property lending chief left this month, less than two years after being hired to build the business.
Lenders there are competing for fewer deals as rates stay high, Bloomberg reported, which is squeezing their margins.
CarbonAI’s own figures are the ones to watch. It reports seven-figure contracted revenue within six months, and up to 90% of time saved on selected underwriting tasks, with no methodology given. Build, a British-founded firm doing the same for data centres, claims over 95%.

articles.title: Quán cà phê sắp đóng cửa sau 10 năm hoạt động đột nhiên nổi tiếng trên mạng
articles.text:
Một quán cà phê tại Biên Hòa (Đồng Nai) bất ngờ thu hút sự chú ý trên mạng xã hội khi thông báo ngừng kinh doanh sau 10 năm hoạt động. Chủ quán cho biết quyết định này xuất phát từ điều kiện kinh tế khó khăn và gửi lời cảm ơn khách hàng đã đồng hành trong suốt một thập kỷ.
Bài đăng nhanh chóng thu hút hàng chục nghìn tương tác, nhiều bình luận và lượt chia sẻ. Nhiều người kể lại những kỷ niệm gắn với quán, trong khi một số người bất ngờ vì chỉ biết đến địa điểm này qua thông báo đóng cửa, dù chưa từng ghé thăm.
Trên thực tế, các bài đăng trước đây của quán có ít tương tác. Thông báo đóng cửa lại được lan truyền rộng rãi, thu hút lượng lớn bình luận và chia sẻ.
Bài viết còn được chia sẻ trên trang cá nhân của người dùng ở nhiều nơi, từ Hà Nội đến Đức, Nhật Bản và Canada.
Tuy nhiên, mức độ lan truyền trên mạng xã hội không đồng nghĩa với việc hoạt động kinh doanh có thể duy trì. Bản thân chủ quán cũng đã quyết định ngừng hoạt động, dù nhận được nhiều lời động viên.
Trước đó, một quán cà phê tại TPHCM cũng gây chú ý khi chủ quán chia sẻ hành trình 30 ngày trước thời điểm đóng cửa. Theo người này, doanh thu không đủ bù đắp chi phí vận hành. Có ngày, quán chỉ bán được vài ly nước, trong khi tiền thuê mặt bằng, lương nhân viên và các khoản chi khác vẫn phải chi trả.
Chủ quán sau đó thực hiện chuỗi video ghi lại 30 ngày cuối cùng, đồng thời triển khai chương trình tri ân với các loại đồ uống đồng giá.
Những video gần gũi, chân thực thu hút sự quan tâm của cộng đồng mạng. Một số người biết đến quán qua các video đã tìm tới mua hàng, giúp doanh thu cải thiện trong giai đoạn cuối. Dù vậy, chủ quán vẫn quyết định dừng kinh doanh.
Một trường hợp khác là anh Nguyễn Văn Hoang, người từng xây dựng thương hiệu giày Banuli. Anh cho biết đã quyết định thanh lý máy móc, khuôn mẫu, nguyên liệu và hàng tồn kho để chuyển sang lĩnh vực kiến trúc, xây dựng và nội thất.
Theo Hoang, mô hình kinh doanh hiện tại không còn phù hợp, trong khi anh không đủ khả năng để tiếp tục mở rộng. Quyết định dừng lại thu hút sự chú ý trên mạng xã hội. Nhiều người bày tỏ tiếc nuối, thậm chí nhắn tin hỏi mua giày để ủng hộ anh.
Vì sao làn sóng ủng hộ chưa đủ?
Chuyên gia Trần Khánh Minh Sơn cho rằng những câu chuyện về chủ quán cà phê đóng cửa hoặc người kinh doanh quyết định đóng cửa hoặc chấm dứt hoạt động kinh doanh thường thu hút sự chú ý bởi yếu tố cảm xúc. Qua đó, nhiều người biết đến thương hiệu, tìm mua sản phẩm hoặc trực tiếp đến cửa hàng để ủng hộ.
Tuy nhiên, sự chú ý trên mạng xã hội không đồng nghĩa với khả năng duy trì hoạt động kinh doanh lâu dài. Lượng khách tăng đột biến sau một bài đăng hoặc video có thể giúp doanh thu cải thiện trong ngắn hạn. Để tồn tại, doanh nghiệp vẫn cần có lượng khách ổn định, kiểm soát chi phí và bảo đảm hiệu quả kinh doanh.
Với các mô hình có chi phí cố định lớn như tiền thuê mặt bằng, lương nhân viên và chi phí duy trì máy móc, doanh thu tăng trong vài ngày chưa chắc đủ bù đắp khoản lỗ tích lũy. Nếu sản phẩm chưa phù hợp với nhu cầu thị trường hoặc mô hình kinh doanh không còn hiệu quả, sự ủng hộ nhất thời khó giải quyết được những vấn đề cốt lõi.
Bên cạnh đó, hành vi mua hàng thực tế có thể khác với lời động viên trên mạng xã hội. Nhiều người sẵn sàng chia sẻ, bình luận hoặc bày tỏ tiếc nuối, nhưng không phải tất cả đều trở thành khách hàng thường xuyên. Vì vậy, doanh nghiệp khó dựa vào lượng tương tác để dự báo doanh thu trong tương lai.
Quyết định tiếp tục hay dừng kinh doanh vẫn cần dựa trên dòng tiền, chi phí vận hành, nhu cầu thị trường và khả năng phát triển của mô hình. Làn sóng ủng hộ có thể giúp thương hiệu được biết đến rộng rãi hơn, nhưng để tồn tại lâu dài, doanh nghiệp vẫn phải giải quyết được bài toán kinh tế.

articles.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
articles.text:
President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing off renovations to the White House — but one of them appears to be modified with AI. The picture, which compares an old White House column to a “restored” one, has several discrepancies and was flagged by Google’s AI detector as “made or edited with OpenAI.”
Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
A ‘before and after’ photo of a freshly painted White House column was modified with AI.
As pointed out by users on Reddit, the picture of the “restored” column has an uneven number of steps on both sides of the structure. The number of steps also doesn’t match up with the ones in the “before” photo. Additionally, the before and after photos appear nearly identical in angle and detail; the reflection in the windows is nearly the same, and the protective cardboard at the bottom of the column seems to be in the same spot as well. Not to mention that the “newly-painted” one looks unnaturally smooth.
The Verge can confirm that the photo posted to Truth Social is flagged as AI-generated when uploaded to Google’s SynthID Detector, which scans images, videos, and audio for an invisible watermark that indicates it was “created or edited” with AI.
Real pictures show people painting the front of the White House in June, so it’s possible the column actually did get a fresh coat of paint — the White House didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The SynthID watermark wasn’t detected on other pictures Trump posted, which show the White House facade and heliport. Trump is no stranger to AI tools, though, as he often posts AI-generated caricatures of himself, while the White House has been known to post racist AI memes and at least one photo deceptively edited to make a protester appear distraught.

articles.title: Google launches Universal Cart in the US, with checkout built into Search and the Gemini app
articles.text:
Google launched Universal Cart in the US on Wednesday, a cart that sits inside Search and the Gemini app, holds products from multiple retailers and takes the payment through Google Pay. Its own roadmap names Canada, Australia and the UK for expansion, and never mentions the EU.
Google has put a shopping cart inside Search and the Gemini app that holds products from rival retailers and takes the payment. It launched in the US on Wednesday. Google’s own roadmap names Canada, Australia and the UK next, and never mentions the EU.
Universal Cart runs on the 60 billion product listings in Google’s Shopping Graph, the company said in a post by Suresh Ganapathy. Its I/O announcement in May said checkout would reach Canada and Australia within months, and the UK later.
The cart keeps items from different retailers in one place, sends alerts on price drops and restocks, and reads Google Wallet to suggest which card to pay with. It also surfaces promo codes.
Participating merchants include Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair and Shopify sellers. Each remains the seller of record, and handles confirmations and support.
Checkout runs on the Universal Commerce Protocol, released as an open standard in January. Google’s Agent Payments Protocol, which lets agents buy within preset limits, arrived in September 2025 with more than 60 partners including PayPal and Mastercard.
That May plan put the US launch in the summer. It arrived on 15 October.
Europe’s absence is not an oversight. The Commission issued Google an €890M DMA fine in July, €460M of it for self-preferencing in shopping, hotel, transport and sports results.
Google was given 60 days to stop, or face daily penalties of up to 5% of Alphabet’s average worldwide turnover.
Its answer was to make search worse. Nick Fox, Google’s search chief, said in September that the changes “degrade the user experience for Europeans“.
A Stockholm court separately ordered Google to pay Klarna’s PriceRunner nearly $2B in July, on the Commission’s 2017 Google Shopping decision. EU fines against the company now exceed €9B.
Google already ships agentic features everywhere but Europe. Gemini Spark, the product it said would get the payments protocol first, reached more than 160 countries in July and is unavailable in the EEA, Switzerland and the UK. No reason was given.
A cart inside Google’s own results, holding rival retailers’ listings and taking the payment, is the self-preferencing question in a newer form.
Six comparison-shopping services are already lining up for damages, from Idealo’s €465M award to Moltiply’s €2.97B claim. Google has not said whether the cart will reach the EU.

articles.title: Mexico's president signs decree ordering tech platforms to protect minors from adult content - Engadget
articles.text:
Mexico's president signs decree ordering tech platforms to protect minors from adult content
Platforms have 30 calendar days to implement the mandatory measures.
Mexico's president Claudia Sheinbaum has signed a decree ordering digital platforms to protect children from accessing adult and other types of content, the government announced. Sites have 30 calendar days to implement the mandatory measures, though they won't initially face any punishment if they don't. Mexico isn't the first country to introduce digital child protection measures, but it's unique in issuing the new rules via a presidential decree rather than new legislation.
The rules apply to social media or other platforms that let users create, distribute or share content. It outlaws access by minors to hate speech, violent extremism, sexual abuse or exploitation, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, school violence, harassment, cyberbullying, unlawful conduct and explicit sexual material. the government wrote.
Platforms must identify and remove accounts or content that promote violence, provide age classifications for content along with parental supervision and reporting tools, while applying stronger privacy and safety settings for younger users. It must also "maintain a 24/7 available point of contact" with investigating authorities, preserve evidence and alert authorities when any life-threatening contents identified.
While the degree is obligatory, it will be non-punitive to start with. However, government said it will pursue further legislation if companies don't follow the rules. Compliance will come from Mexico's ADTT (Agency for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications).
Mexico previously considered applying an eight percent tax on violent video games, though Sheinbaum later dropped the idea. Mexico now joins multiple countries and territories implementing digital child protection laws of different kinds, including Australia, Europe and China, along with Florida, Mississippi, Ohio and Texas. Australia's pioneering under-16 social media ban saw early teething problems as minors found ways around platforms' age-verification tools.

articles.title: Amazon's Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon’s personal AI wearable maker, Bee, is announcing its first new products since being acquired by the retail giant last year. The tech company on Thursday introduced the Bee Frontier, the next generation of its device that can be worn on the wrist or pinned to clothes, along with Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-sized device that magnetically attaches to the back of your smartphone.
The latter puts Bee into more direct competition with AI devices like the Plaud Note or Pocket, but at a lower price point — the Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the Plaud Note (or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the Pocket AI device.
The Bee Frontier will come in Onyx, Lavender, and Sage, while the $99.99 Bee Eclipse will be offered in Silver, Midnight, Honey, and Blush.
Like the original Bee, the idea with the new devices is to leverage AI to take notes from your everyday conversations, allowing you to remember the important things that were said, and then turn those into actionable to-dos, summaries, and insights.
For instance, if you discussed making plans with friends, the Bee would remember the date and time you agreed on, then create a calendar invite. You could also use the Bee to take lecture notes in class, or to jot down the care plan you discussed with a doctor, among other things.
All Bee devices can create conversation summaries and recaps for free, and offer 14 days of memory. With an $11.99 per month Bee Pro subscription, users receive unlimited conversation summaries and integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, and third-party applications. Pro users also get suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, and conversation templates.
To make all this possible, Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn’t store the raw audio from your conversations. Instead, audio is processed in real time and then deleted. Transcripts of the conversation are encrypted using keys that your device creates and controls, which means no one else, including Amazon employees, can access those files unless you manually and intentionally share them.
In addition, you can opt to connect the Bee to Alexa, allowing your Echo device to use its ability to identify your voice, a feature called Voice ID, to recognize when you’re speaking. It can then record your conversations to provide Bee’s insights. (This aspect of Bee is optional, and Amazon notes you can delete transcripts and summaries at any time.)
With its new connections to Amazon.com and Alexa, Bee users can make purchases from Amazon or ask Alexa for their Bee insights, summaries, or to-dos hands-free.
Bee also works with your existing productivity software, like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook, so it can draft emails, set up meetings, surface action items, and more.
Plus, you can upload photos to Bee or connect it with Apple’s HealthKit to add a picture of your overall wellness to be integrated into your provided insights.
The Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse both have just one button that turns the device off and on, and include an indicator light when it’s summarizing a conversation. The Frontier also offers IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, USB-C charging, and dual microphones with advanced noise filtering.
All Bee devices come with a companion mobile app, which has also been newly redesigned, plus a new desktop app.
The Bee Frontier is available now on Amazon, and the Eclipse will be available soon thereafter.

articles.title: Chủ sở hữu chung cư chục năm chưa ai nhắc đóng thuế: Thuế Hà Nội chỉ rõ cách xử lý
articles.text:
Thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp với nhà chung cư là bắt buộc
Nhiều người sở hữu căn hộ chung cư băn khoăn liệu mình có phải nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp hay không, nhất là khi đã sinh sống tại căn hộ nhiều năm nhưng chưa nhận được thông báo thuế.
Theo Thuế TP Hà Nội, việc xác định người nộp thuế căn cứ vào quy định pháp luật và từng trường hợp cụ thể.
Điều 4 Luật Thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp năm 2010 và Điều 3 Thông tư 153/2011/TT-BTC của Bộ Tài chính quy định về người nộp thuế. Trong đó, đối với trường hợp Nhà nước giao đất, cho thuê đất để thực hiện dự án xây dựng nhà ở để bán, cho thuê, người nộp thuế là tổ chức được giao đất, cho thuê đất. Trường hợp chuyển nhượng quyền sử dụng đất cho tổ chức, cá nhân khác, người nộp thuế là người nhận chuyển nhượng.
Theo quy định, đất ở tại đô thị, đất ở tại nông thôn, trong đó có đất xây dựng nhà chung cư, thuộc đối tượng chịu thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp.
Đối với căn hộ chung cư, diện tích đất tính thuế được xác định theo hệ số phân bổ nhân với diện tích nhà mà tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân sử dụng.
Như vậy, theo Thuế TP Hà Nội, thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp đối với nhà chung cư là nghĩa vụ tài chính bắt buộc của tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân có quyền sử dụng đất gắn với căn hộ chung cư.
Với trường hợp cư dân đã ở chung cư nhiều năm nhưng chưa bao giờ nhận được thông báo nộp thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp nguyên nhân có thể do chủ sở hữu chưa kê khai hoặc thay đổi chủ sở hữu mà chưa cập nhật thông tin.
Với trường hợp này, Thuế TP Hà Nội khuyến cáo người dân chuẩn bị hợp đồng mua bán, giấy tờ liên quan đến việc chuyển quyền và mã hồ sơ liên thông nếu có; sau đó liên hệ cơ quan thuế nơi có căn hộ để được kiểm tra, đối chiếu thông tin và hướng dẫn xử lý.
Cách tính thuế đất phi nông nghiệp đối với căn hộ chung cư
Theo hướng dẫn của cơ quan thuế, đối với đất ở tại nhà nhiều tầng có nhiều hộ ở, nhà chung cư, kể cả trường hợp vừa để ở vừa để kinh doanh, diện tích đất tính thuế được xác định bằng hệ số phân bổ nhân với diện tích nhà của từng tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân sử dụng.
Đối với nhà nhiều tầng, nhiều hộ ở hoặc nhà chung cư không có tầng hầm, hệ số phân bổ được tính bằng diện tích đất xây dựng tòa nhà chia cho tổng diện tích nhà của các tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân sử dụng.
Trường hợp chung cư có tầng hầm, hệ số phân bổ được tính bằng diện tích đất xây dựng tòa nhà chia cho tổng diện tích nhà sử dụng phía trên mặt đất cộng với 50% diện tích tầng hầm mà các tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân sử dụng.
Đối với công trình xây dựng dưới mặt đất, hệ số phân bổ được xác định bằng 0,5 nhân với diện tích đất xây dựng, sau đó chia cho tổng diện tích công trình của các tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân sử dụng.
Giá 1m2 đất tính thuế là giá đất theo bảng giá đất tương ứng với mục đích sử dụng và được ổn định theo chu kỳ 5 năm, theo quy định về thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp.
Đối với đất ở tại nhà nhiều tầng, nhiều hộ ở, nhà chung cư và công trình xây dựng dưới mặt đất, thuế suất áp dụng là 0,03%.
Số thuế phát sinh được tính bằng diện tích đất tính thuế nhân với giá 1m2 đất tính thuế và thuế suất. Số thuế phải nộp là số thuế phát sinh sau khi trừ khoản được miễn, giảm nếu có.
Như vậy, số thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp liên quan đến căn hộ chung cư phụ thuộc vào diện tích đất được phân bổ, giá đất tính thuế và thuế suất theo quy định.
| Ví dụ giả định do VietNamNet tính toán với một người sở hữu căn hộ 75m2 tại tòa chung cư không có tầng hầm, với các thông số: – Diện tích đất xây dựng tòa nhà: 2.000m2. – Tổng diện tích nhà của các tổ chức, hộ gia đình, cá nhân sử dụng: 20.000m2. – Giá đất tính thuế: 50 triệu đồng/m2. – Thuế suất: 0,03%; không thuộc trường hợp được miễn, giảm. Hệ số phân bổ là: 2.000 ÷ 20.000 = 0,1. Diện tích đất tính thuế của căn hộ là: 75 × 0,1 = 7,5m2. Số thuế phải nộp mỗi năm là: 7,5 × 50.000.000 × 0,03% = 112.500 đồng. Như vậy, với các thông số giả định trên, chủ căn hộ 75m2 phải nộp 112.500 đồng thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp/năm. Giá đất dùng để tính thuế là giá đất theo quy định, không phải giá mua căn hộ hay giá giao dịch trên thị trường. |

articles.title: Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social
articles.text:
Bluesky’s Attie AI tool, which initially launched earlier this year as a way to use AI to build your own feeds, now lets you make “small” social apps like games, polls, and dashboards that you can then share with others as their own websites. In an interview at TechCrunch Disrupt, Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider said to think of Attie as “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”
Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social
Attie launched earlier this year as a way to build your own feeds with AI, but Bluesky is expanding what it can do.
You can make your own Attie app by typing in a prompt. A simple poll I made about Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue took a few minutes to generate. If you want to check out something more full-featured, the Attie website currently highlights a few examples like a “Flappy Butterfly” Flappy Bird clone, a drum machine, a quiz, and an idle clicker about a celery man, and each has a custom link on the attie.site domain and attribution for who made the social app at the bottom of the page. The apps I’ve messed around with are pretty lightweight novelties, though I liked the drum machine.

articles.title: Microsoft says Windows 11 is now up to 20% more responsive and better on 8GB of RAM
articles.text:
Microsoft says months of work have made Windows 11 up to 20% more responsive and that better memory management makes a meaningful difference on PCs with 8GB of RAM. The only published hands-on test found gains on 16GB and larger machines, and none at all on an 8GB PC.
Microsoft says Windows 11 is now up to 20% more responsive, and that memory work makes an especially meaningful difference on 8GB PCs. The one published test of an 8GB machine found no change.
The Verge reported the claims on Thursday. Navjot Virk, corporate vice president of Windows experiences, wrote in Microsoft’s post that Windows can keep up to 2GB more active data in memory instead of moving it to slower storage.
Widgets now load only when opened, which Virk said frees more than 200MB on machines with 8GB or less. Start, File Explorer, Search, Snipping Tool and Edge were all touched.
The taskbar can finally sit at the sides or top of a display. Windows Hello sign-in is faster, and AirPods pair up to 15 seconds faster, on a different build.
The promise is not new. Pavan Davuluri said in August that Microsoft would shrink Windows to fit 8GB machines, naming the memory allocator, WinUI 3 and WebView2.
Microsoft did publish a baseline. The 20% compares build 26300.9550 against 26200.7628, timing Search, Start, right-click, Settings, Snipping Tool and File Explorer. None of those is a memory test.
The reliability half of the plan has a record. June’s update fixed 208 flaws and brought a cascade of bugs, including BitLocker recovery screens on some HP and Dell machines.
The memory claims carry no such measurement. Their footnote says only that they rest on improvements in the same build. Windows Latest tested it this month: a 16GB laptop used about 2GB less, and an 8GB PC nothing at all, still at 96%.
Price is why any of this is happening. Google said in July it was reworking Android to need less RAM, citing Morgan Stanley figures of $2.80 per gigabyte in 2025 against $12 now.
Memory makers have moved capacity to high-bandwidth memory for AI data centres. Samsung does not expect relief until 2028.
Europe is where the squeeze shows. European desktop shipments fell about 20% in the third quarter, with almost 30% forecast for the fourth. Laptops should drop 20%.
Context found that what buying there was came from the end of Windows 10 support, not AI PC features. Europeans replaced machines because the old one died.
Gartner expects the sub-$500 PC to all but disappear by 2028, and the average American machine already sells for more than $1,000. Microsoft is optimising for 8GB because it is becoming the ceiling.

articles.title: Apple I 'Hatfield' computer signed by Woz fetches a record $1.15 million at auction - Engadget
articles.text:
Apple I 'Hatfield' computer signed by Woz fetches a record $1.15 million at auction
It comes with a letter from Steve Jobs asking if the owner wants to upgrade to an Apple II.
The famous Apple I "Hatfield" computer signed by Steve Wozniak just sold to an unknown buyer for a record $1,148,200, the auction house Bonhams announced. The machine, built in 1976 and originanlly sold for $666.60 to a certain Fred Hatfield, is one of only 74 verified Apple I models left (number 48 on the registry) and one of the very few still in working condition.
Along with Woz's signature, it comes with a letter from Steve Jobs encouraging Hatfield to send in his motherboard for an upgrade to the Apple II model. The buyer also receives the original Apple I operation manual, a cassette operating manual, an invitation to join the Apple I Owners Club and a custom power supply, along with a period monitor and keyboards.
The last time this particular machine went up for auction in 2013, it sold for $671,400. To boost interest, Bonhams publicized the auction last month and put it on display in New York. The bidding reportedly came down to two people, who paddled the price well beyond the expected top range of $800,000.
"We are delighted with this exceptional result for the 'Hatfield' Apple I, one of the most important milestones in computing history," Bonham's Ian Ehling told Apple Insider. "It was an honor to offer Apple's first product during the company's 50th anniversary year."
The Apple I was far from consumer-friendly, as it didn't even come with a power supply, let alone a keyboard and monitor. This model was sold with 8KB of RAM and a MOS Technology 6502 microprocessor, enough to run Apple Integer Basic and a few games via the optional Apple Cassette Interface.
The letter from Jobs offering an Apple II upgrade is what makes this Apple I example particularly interesting. "The letter serves as a testament to just how personally involved Jobs and Wozniak were in the early days of Apple, doing everything from designing and producing the products, to running customer support," Bonhams explains in the auction page.
Hatfield fortunately declined and eventually ended up selling the machine for $40,000. He famously used that cash to pay for some nice dinners and nights out on Frenchmen Street in his New Orleans hometown. "I figure I might as well enjoy the money I got from that old machine," he told The New York Times back in 2013.

articles.title: Governments are hacking people with 'zero-click' spyware by showing them online ads | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Security researchers at digital rights unit The Citizen Lab say government spyware makers are abusing global advertising networks to target and hack devices by serving malicious online adverts.
A new report published Thursday by the University of Toronto lab, which investigates surveillance and digital rights abuses, said an Israeli company called Discover-Tech allows spyware makers to use its advertising platform to target specific people or devices almost anywhere in the world with spyware capable of invisibly stealing their data.
The researchers say Discover-Tech presents itself as a legitimate advertising firm, but instead serves as a “bridge between ad vendors and the mercenary spyware ecosystem.”
Citizen Lab said at least two makers of zero-click spyware, Candiru and Bindecy, used Discover-Tech’s platform to target people. Both of these spyware makers provide surveillance products that can infect devices without the victim having to open a message or click on a link.
The researchers found that one attack affected at least 45 Windows computers at media organization Al Jazeera. The devices were apparently hacked in 2024 and 2025 via Candiru’s spyware after being exposed to online ads packed with malicious code.
Citizen Lab said it wasn’t clear which governments were behind the attacks, but said this is the first confirmation of zero-click government-backed spyware attacks being delivered through online ads, potentially putting a vast number of devices around the world at risk of being targeted and hacked.
“There has been a lot of buzz that online ads can be used to identify and automatically hack targets with pinpoint precision, but now for the first time, we have concrete technical evidence showing this process in action,” said Bill Marczak, a Citizen Lab senior researcher, ahead of the report’s release.
Hackers have long sought ways to abuse access to advertising networks, in part because of their ability to reach almost any internet-connected device in the world. Ad networks are designed to help advertisers target certain kinds of people, devices, and organizations with specific ads, but they can also be abused to target specific individuals or devices with malicious code.
While such so-called “malvertising” attacks are not new, using online ads to allow powerful government spyware to silently hack into devices is a notable escalation.
Security and privacy experts have for years encouraged people to install ad-blockers to prevent ads from being displayed on desktop and mobile screens, including within apps. But the ubiquity of online advertising makes it difficult to escape the industry’s clutches entirely.
The researchers said Discover-Tech’s platform, which the company calls Controlium, left some of its source code exposed on its login pages, allowing the researchers to recreate its web-based control panel dashboard without needing to log in. The researchers say the web dashboard “appears to be specifically designed to allow them to push malicious content to individual targeted users alongside advertisements.”
Citizen Lab also found that Discover-Tech’s site had a publicly accessible portion that allowed the researchers to download reams of user login records for the Controlium dashboard without needing a password. Some login details belonged to at least two employees of spyware maker Candiru, as well as some from Bindecy.
The researchers also found billions of ad bidding records left exposed on Discover-Tech’s website, which showed that its ads had ultimately been displayed across tens of thousands of mobile apps and websites between March and June 2026.
The bidding records show that the ads were shown on devices used by militaries, governments, critical infrastructure, and national cyber agencies. However, it’s unclear if the displayed ads resulted in a compromise or infection.
Security researchers with ad quality platform Confiant, which worked with Citizen Lab to investigate, said they found evidence that potentially malicious ads were similarly shown on devices on the networks of the International Atomic Energy Agency and the International Criminal Court.
Citizen Lab’s Marczak said Discover-Tech is “surely just the tip of the iceberg,” and urged people to take defensive action.
“If you might be targeted based on who you are or what you do, it’s time to disable ad tracking on your devices or even block ads altogether,” said Marczak.
Al Jazeera did not respond to a request for comment about the hacks. Neither did Discover-Tech, and Candiru maker Integrity Labs could not be reached for comment.

articles.title: Kế nghiệp nghìn tỷ, doanh nhân thế hệ F2 đối mặt thử thách ‘vượt sướng’
articles.text:
Trong giới kinh doanh, chuyển giao doanh nghiệp gia đình luôn là bài toán khó bởi khác biệt về tư duy và cách quản trị giữa các thế hệ. Với thế hệ F2, gánh vác một di sản nghìn tỷ chưa bao giờ là hành trình dễ dàng.
Áp lực kế nhiệm của người giàu
“Nhiều người nói vượt khổ mới khó, nhưng thực tế vượt sướng khó hơn rất nhiều”, bà Vưu Lệ Quyên, Tổng giám đốc Biti’s, mở đầu câu chuyện khi chia sẻ về hành trình kế nhiệm doanh nghiệp gia đình.
Bà Quyên cho biết vẫn nhớ khoảnh khắc cách đây nhiều năm, khi cha bà, doanh nhân Vưu Khải Thành, yêu cầu bà đưa ra quyết định trong vòng 2 tuần về việc có nhận vị trí Tổng giám đốc hay không.
Thời điểm đó, bà không muốn nhận chức. Cơ nghiệp với hàng nghìn tỷ đồng tài sản, hàng trăm cửa hàng và 8.000 cán bộ, công nhân viên tạo ra áp lực khổng lồ. Đặc biệt, văn hóa doanh nghiệp khi ấy phần nhiều vận hành dựa trên nỗi sợ hãi. Cha bà nổi tiếng nghiêm khắc, đặt yêu cầu cao đối với nhân sự. Trong khi đó, bà nhận thấy mình không thể lãnh đạo bằng sự trừng phạt hay ép bản thân trở thành một người khác.
Tuy nhiên, lời động viên của mẹ rằng bà có thể giúp 8.000 nhân viên có môi trường làm việc "đỡ khổ hơn" đã chạm đến mong muốn làm điều có ích cho người khác. Cuối cùng, bà Quyên quyết định đảm nhận vai trò điều hành, đồng thời tìm cách chuyển đổi văn hóa doanh nghiệp từ sợ hãi sang yêu thương.
Biti’s triển khai các chương trình phát triển kỹ năng hạnh phúc, tập trung vào ba mối liên kết: với chính mình, với người khác và với thiên nhiên. Doanh nghiệp sử dụng bộ khảo sát gồm 118 câu hỏi dựa trên 9 lĩnh vực của mô hình Tổng hạnh phúc quốc gia (GNH). Các cuộc họp bắt đầu bằng hai phút tĩnh lặng; chiều thứ Sáu hằng tuần, nhân viên được dành một giờ làm việc có hưởng lương để thực hành kỹ năng hạnh phúc và chia sẻ những vấn đề gặp phải.
Sau 8 năm, bà Quyên cho hay doanh thu Biti’s tăng trưởng hai con số, lợi nhuận cải thiện so với giai đoạn trước, nhân viên chủ động hơn trong công việc. Bà cũng nhấn mạnh xây dựng môi trường làm việc hạnh phúc không đồng nghĩa với việc bỏ qua hiệu quả hay kỷ luật.
Cũng như bà Quyên, khi tiếp quản gia sản gia đình, ông Hà Quốc Phong (sinh năm 1992), Phó Tổng Giám đốc Cơ điện Tân Hoàn Cầu, kể rằng áp lực lớn nhất là làm sao gìn giữ và phát triển cơ nghiệp mà cha mẹ đã gây dựng trong suốt 20-30 năm.
Theo ông, người ngoài có thể nghĩ con cái tiếp quản doanh nghiệp gia đình chỉ cần đừng làm hỏng những gì có sẵn, nhưng thực tế, việc duy trì và phát triển một doanh nghiệp đã trải qua nhiều năm gây dựng không hề đơn giản.
Trở về từ Canada, ông Phong mong mang những kiến thức và cách tiếp cận mới đưa vào doanh nghiệp. Thế nhưng, khi đưa ra một đề xuất mới, cha ông chưa đồng tình: "Cái này ba thấy không ổn". Thay vì phản bác hoặc cố thuyết phục cha ngay lập tức, ông Phong thường tìm hiểu nguyên nhân khiến đề xuất chưa được chấp nhận, từ đó đưa ra phương án giải quyết phù hợp.
Theo ông, có những cuộc trao đổi kéo dài 1-2 giờ sáng. Ông hiểu rằng cha mình có thể không sử dụng các thuật ngữ quản trị hiện đại, nhưng kinh nghiệm thực tiễn giúp ông nhận ra những rủi ro mà người trẻ chưa chắc đã nhìn thấy. Vì vậy, điều quan trọng không phải là mang kiến thức mới về để phủ nhận cách làm cũ, mà là hiểu vì sao người đi trước đưa ra một quyết định như vậy.
Với ông Phong, những cuộc tranh luận là cơ hội để hai thế hệ giải thích quan điểm, nhìn nhận vấn đề từ góc độ của người còn lại, thay vì để bất đồng tích tụ thành xung đột.
Đổi mới nhưng không để khác biệt thế hệ thành xung đột
Với những doanh nhân trẻ, việc kế nhiệm chưa bao giờ là dễ dàng khi vừa phải tìm cách thay đổi phương thức quản trị truyền thống, vừa không làm gãy đổ nền tảng cũ.
Tại Biti’s, khoảng 16 năm trước, bà Quyên cho hay bà phụ trách dự án chuyển đổi hệ thống ERP (hoạch định nguồn lực doanh nghiệp). Một tháng sau khi đi vào hoạt động, nhiều phản ánh phát sinh. Ông Vưu Khải Thành quyết định cho gần như toàn bộ đội ngũ công nghệ thông tin tham gia dự án nghỉ việc, chỉ giữ lại một người.
Trước tình huống này, bà Quyên âm thầm động viên các thành viên cũ tiếp tục hỗ trợ từ xa, đồng thời duy trì hai hệ thống song song trong thời gian khắc phục sự cố. Theo bà, hệ thống ERP đã vận hành ổn định suốt 16 năm.
Từ trải nghiệm đó, bà Quyên cho rằng việc thay đổi trong doanh nghiệp cần có sự kiên trì và khả năng ứng phó với những phản ứng bất ngờ. Người lãnh đạo không chỉ cần tôn trọng chuyên môn mà còn phải biết khích lệ đội ngũ và giữ bình tĩnh khi khủng hoảng xảy ra.
Trong nội bộ, bà cũng áp dụng sản xuất tinh gọn nhằm giảm lãng phí vật chất, đồng thời từng bước thay đổi cách quản trị, chú trọng phát triển kỹ năng hạnh phúc để hạn chế những lãng phí khó nhận diện như tức giận, sợ hãi, tiêu cực và xung đột nội bộ.
Theo bà Quyên, kế thừa một doanh nghiệp có hàng nghìn nhân sự có thể tạo ra tác động xã hội lớn hơn so với khởi nghiệp với vài chục người. Tuy nhiên, những người sinh ra trong gia đình khá giả cũng có thể đối mặt với thử thách “vượt sướng”. Nếu không có mục đích sống rõ ràng, họ dễ mất phương hướng.
Vì vậy, người kế nhiệm cần trải nghiệm công việc thực tế, chấp nhận va vấp và hiểu những người lao động đang trực tiếp làm việc trong doanh nghiệp.
Ở một doanh nghiệp khác, ông Trần Duy Minh Đạt (sinh năm 1990), Phó chủ tịch HĐQT Duy Tân Group, con trai nhà sáng lập Nhựa Duy Tân, cũng nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc phân định rõ quyền sở hữu và quyền điều hành trong quá trình chuyển giao thế hệ. Theo ông, sự tham gia của các thành viên HĐQT độc lập cũng là một yếu tố cần thiết để nâng cao chất lượng quản trị.
Duy Tân cũng đang xây dựng mô hình Family Office nhằm quản lý tập trung tài sản, rủi ro tài chính và thiết lập lộ trình phát triển cho thế hệ tiếp theo.
Theo ông Đạt, người kế nhiệm có thể tiếp tục làm việc trong lĩnh vực sản xuất, khởi nghiệp hoặc lựa chọn con đường riêng. Vì vậy, chuẩn bị cho thế hệ sau không chỉ là xác định ai sẽ tiếp nhận vị trí lãnh đạo, mà còn phải xây dựng cơ chế quản trị và định hướng phát triển phù hợp cho tương lai.

articles.title: SpaceX's $8B spectrum deal exposes the risk in telecom shares
articles.text:
SpaceX agreed to pay about $8B for nationwide low-band US spectrum, and shares in AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile fell on the news. Europe’s equivalent band comes up for selection in May 2027, with Brussels proposing that two-thirds of it be reserved for European firms and sovereign use.
SpaceX has agreed to pay about $8B for the thing that turns a satellite operator into a phone company. US carrier shares fell hard. The same move is not available in Europe.
Bloomberg reported on Thursday that the sell-off has exposed how little protection telecom stocks offer. Deutsche Telekom is down 8.6% this year, and a gauge of European telecom shares has fallen 18% from a May peak.
SpaceX said on 9 October it would buy nationwide low-band 800 MHz spectrum from investment firm Grain Management. The Wall Street Journal put the price at $8B in cash. The deal needs FCC clearance.
T-Mobile closed down 13.3%, AT&T 9.8% and Verizon 8.8%, according to Axios. It was Verizon’s worst day since 2002.
The band matters because most phones support it and it carries indoors, SpaceX’s remaining technical gap. It had already paid $17B for EchoStar licences, and told IPO investors it was weighing a retail mobile service.
Analysts were calmer than the tape. John Conca of Third Bridge told Bloomberg that SpaceX still needs expensive ground infrastructure in dense markets, and that this is sentiment rather than fundamentals.
Rates did the rest. The 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5% on 15 September, and a dividend stopped being special. T-Mobile was already weak after a 25% slide under Srini Gopalan.
Verizon yields 6.4%, among the ten highest in the S&P 500, against AT&T’s 4.8% and T-Mobile’s 3%. It trades at 8.5 times forward earnings, below its ten-year average.
Europe is the part nobody is pricing. The Commission proposed in May that the bloc’s 2 GHz mobile satellite band be split in three, with two-thirds reserved for a European-controlled operator and for sovereign use.
The current licences, held by Viasat and EchoStar, expire in May 2027. SpaceX and Amazon can bid for the remaining third. Parliament and Council must still approve it.
Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone and Telefonica are in early talks to bid together. Vodafone would have to restructure its 50/50 venture with AST SpaceMobile, which would not count as European-controlled.
Starlink already reaches European phones, but through operators rather than on its own, Deutsche Telekom among them. Without spectrum it cannot sell to them directly.
The third set aside for governments goes to IRIS2, now in deployment, built for secure government traffic rather than consumer phones, with no service until 2030. Friday showed what the 2027 selection is worth.

articles.title: YouTube is reportedly gearing up to offer audiobooks - Engadget
articles.text:
YouTube is reportedly gearing up to offer audiobooks
It could offer audiobooks as soon as next year, according to The Wall Street Journal.
YouTube is preparing to launch an audiobooks feature as soon as next year and has been in talks with publishers over the previous months, according to the Wall Street Journal. You can already find a bunch of channels with audiobook videos on the platform if you look. Some of them feature titles in the public domain, but some of them offer books that aren't legally supposed to be on YouTube. One growing problem on the platform is the spread of unauthorized book recordings made using AI. Ever come across an audiobook on YouTube narrated by a robotic voice? Most likely, it was one of those unauthorized titles we're talking about.
At the moment, YouTube has yet to confirm if it's really looking to have an audiobook section. The Journal says it has considered bundling the feature with its ad-free Premium service that costs $16 a month. Since it's still very early days, we'll have to wait and see whether that price will cover your whole month of listening and if YouTube will offer individual books for sale — if the feature even does launch.
Since there are already other, more established services, its success will all depend on YouTube's library and how competitive its prices will be. Spotify has several options. Its Premium plans come with 15 audiobook listening hours per month, and for an extra $12 a month, you'll get another 15 hours with its Audiobooks+ add-on. It has a standalone plan for $10 a month called Audiobooks Access, which offers 15 hours a month, as well. Plus, you can buy individual books via the Spotify Web Player.
Meanwhile, Audible's $9-per-month Standard membership gives you access to one audiobook a month from its library that you can access as long as you're paying for a subscription. Its $15 Premium membership will give you one credit a month that you can use to buy a title you can keep forever, as well as access to an all-you-can-listen catalog.

articles.title: Withings now charges $100 per year to sync your data to other apps
articles.text:
If you’re a new user of Withings’ fitness-tracking smartwatches or smart scales and want to sync and access your health data through third party apps like Apple Health or Google Health it’s now going to cost you.
Withings now charges $100 per year to sync your data to other apps
The feature will continue to be free for users who created a Withings account on or before October 12th, 2026.
According to a discussion on Withings’ support forums spotted by MacRumors, new Withings accounts created from October 13th, 2026, and onwards will require a Withings Plus subscription to use the “automatic sync to third-party apps” feature. The subscription costs $9.95 per month or $99.50 per year but Withings’ devices come with a free one month trial that includes the option to sync their data to third-party apps. When the trial is over the syncing is paused but the data in those apps isn’t deleted.
Existing users who already have a Withings account created on or before October 12th, 2026, will continue to have access to automatic third-party app syncing for free, according to official comments shared by a member of Withings’ support team. And because the feature is tied to an existing users’ account and not a specific device, the third-party syncing will continue to be available without a subscription if they buy and register new watches, scales, or other Withings hardware.

articles.title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
articles.text:
Meta announced the Muse Spark Open AI model today, claiming that it’s the “most capable US open-weight model to date.” But the company also says that it’s the “the first model in its class” that can “run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.”
Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
Meta and Apple’s CEOs are publicly supporting each company’s work on Muse Spark Open.
Meta and Apple, typically rivals, worked together on the launch and are publicly supporting each other.
“Muse Spark Open -- weights releasing today -- runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple,” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on X.
“Congrats to the team!” new Apple CEO John Ternus said in a reply. “Amazing to run a model of Muse Spark Open’s caliber and scale this efficiently, right from your desk. Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI!”
“We’re excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again,” Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said to Axios, who also noted that the companies have been collaborating over several months.
The new model is a “natively multimodal model” with 816 billion total parameters that “excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning,” according to Meta. Apple also published a new technical post about MLX, an “array framework” for ML tasks on Apple Silicon, Muse Spark Open, and two other open models.

articles.title: Amazon relaunches Bee with two recording devices and a $12 monthly plan
articles.text:
Amazon has launched the $74.99 Bee Frontier wristband and the $99.99 Bee Eclipse phone attachment, and put the companion software behind an $11.99 monthly subscription. Neither device is on sale in Europe, where recording another person’s private speech is a criminal offence in Germany.
Amazon has launched two devices that record and summarise your day, and put the software behind a subscription. The $74.99 Bee Frontier is on sale in the US. Neither is sold in Europe.
Bloomberg reported the launch on Thursday. The card-shaped Bee Eclipse attaches magnetically to a phone and starts at $99.99, with no release date.
Frontier is lighter than the wristband it replaces, rated IP67, and good for seven days. It has dual microphones with noise filtering. The $49.99 Bee Pioneer is no longer sold.
Amazon said both devices run on Bee Private Compute, that audio is processed in real time and deleted, and that transcripts use keys only the device controls.
Bee Pro costs $11.99 a month. It adds unlimited summaries, integrations with Amazon.com, Alexa+, Gmail, Google Calendar and Outlook, and a desktop app that records Zoom calls. Free users keep 14 days of memory.
The paywall is the new part. Bee’s founder says existing customers keep their current features free. New buyers get 30 days of Pro.
Consent is the harder problem. Lawyers in four US states told Bloomberg last month that the Apple Watch’s conversation recaps may break eavesdropping law. Bee needs a button press, and Amazon says users are prompted to ask call participants.
Engadget notes the Eclipse looks enough like a battery pack that its light may not read as a recording signal. Amazon’s own release says that light is what signals a conversation is being summarised.
Meta shipped a palm-sized Muse device and audio-only glasses in September, and is building an AI pendant with a business subscription attached. Plaud added third-party integrations alongside AI earbuds in August.
Amazon discontinued its Halo health trackers in 2023. Bee is its way back into wearables.
The European absence is not a platform problem. Alexa+ has been in early access in Germany and Austria since May, and in Italy, Spain and France since spring. Amazon was beta-testing a Hindi version in June.
It is not a market problem either. Plaud opened pre-orders for $250 recording earbuds in eight countries in August, six of them European, Germany and France included.
Germany punishes recording another person’s non-public speech without authorisation with up to three years. France’s Article 226-1 carries a year and a €45,000 fine, and presumes consent only when a recording is made openly. Amazon’s prompt covers phone calls.

articles.title: Sony made a $5,900 gold-plated Walkman MP3 player
articles.text:
Sony has announced a trio of new Walkman portable media players that start at an already absurd $1,899.99 for the NW-ZX900 and climb all the way up to $5,899 for the gold-plated NW-WM1ZM3. Sandwiched in between is the $2,999.99 Walkman NW-WM1AM3, which is nearly identical to the WM1ZM3, just minus the gaudy gold shell.
Sony made a $5,900 gold-plated Walkman MP3 player
A $6,000 media player slathered is gold is the perfect gift for the millionaire audiophile in your life.
All three devices are aimed squarely at the audiophile market, if the price tag didn’t make that clear. All three feature Sony’s DSD (Direct Stream Digital) Remastering Engine, which upsamples standard PCM audio to an 11.2MHz DSD stream, which it claims delivers a more analog-like sound. They also all feature gold-plating on the rear chassis that’s meant to reduce interference and lower noise.
The higher-end Walkman NW-WM1ZM3 and NW-WM1AM3 add hand-soldered oxygen-free copper (OFC) wiring and upgraded power circuitry to lower noise even further. A milled OFC block isolates the digital circuits from the analog ones to limit potential interference.
What sets the WM1ZM3 apart is that the entire chassis is made of OFC and then gold-plated.
This is not the first time Sony has gone all out on a gold media player. In fact, you can pick up the previous model — the NW-WM1ZM2 — on sale now for just $2,599.99. A veritable steal. Though, an old iPod bought off eBay is still probably the better bargain.

articles.title: XDC Network integrates Concordium identity verification for AI agents
articles.text:
The integration allows AI agents on XDC AI to verify the individuals or businesses behind them, addressing questions of accountability as autonomous agents gain financial capabilities.
XDC Network has selected Concordium as the exclusive identity verification provider for XDC AI, its agent payments marketplace, introducing a system that allows AI agents to prove they are backed by a verified individual or business without publicly revealing the owner’s identity.
The integration adds an identity verification layer to XDC AI, which launched in July 2026 and enables autonomous agents to discover services and make payments in USDC through non-custodial wallets using the x402 payment standard.
As AI agents gain the ability to manage wallets and execute financial transactions, questions surrounding accountability are becoming increasingly relevant. While existing payment infrastructure enables agents to move funds, it does not necessarily establish who is responsible for their actions. For businesses considering the use of autonomous agents in financial operations, verifying the individuals or organizations behind them introduces an additional layer of oversight.
Through the Concordium integration, agents operating on XDC AI can receive publicly verifiable on-chain badges confirming that an authenticated owner stands behind them, while keeping personal information off-chain.
The verification process requires agent owners to complete a passport and liveness check through the Concordium Wallet, conducted by an independent identity provider. Once verified, owners link their XDC wallets using two signatures that do not transfer funds and register their agents to receive the verification badge.
Under Concordium’s identity framework, personal information remains private, with disclosure requiring a court order and joint action by independent Privacy Guardians.
“Agents on XDC AI can already discover services and pay for them in USDC. What institutions need next is to know who stands behind an agent before they trust it with real money. Concordium gives every verified agent an accountable owner without putting anyone’s personal data on-chain, so builders on XDC earn trust from their very first transaction,” says Atul Khekade, Co-founder, XDC Network.
The partnership reflects a distinction between enabling autonomous payments and establishing accountability for the agents conducting them. An agent’s ability to execute transactions does not independently verify the identity of the person or business authorizing its activities, a consideration for institutions exploring AI-driven financial services.
“Payment tells you an agent can spend. It doesn’t tell you who answers for it,” said Boris Bohrer-Bilowitzki, CEO of Concordium. “XDC has built the rails for agents to transact. We make sure a verified person or business stands behind every agent we verify, without making their identity public. EVM or non-EVM, what matters is who is accountable, not which network an agent uses. That’s the assurance institutions need to give agents real authority. XDC is the first of many networks integrating with us.”
Concordium already supports agent verification on Ethereum and Solana, but the XDC partnership marks its first full-network integration. Agents will retain their existing wallets, code and operations on XDC, with Concordium serving as the separate identity verification layer.
The agreement also includes a revenue-sharing model tied to agent verifications. Each verified agent creates a Concordium account linked to its authenticated owner, while sponsored network fees eliminate the need for developers to hold Concordium’s native CCD token.
The verification service is now available at xdcai.tech/agent-verification, with developer documentation accessible at docs.xdcai.tech/wallet/agent-verification.

articles.title: Volvo will use Nvidia’s tech for hands-free, point-to-point driving
articles.text:
Volvo plans to launch hands-free, point-to-point driving by 2030, powered by Nvidia’s latest AI technology. The Chinese-owned, Swedish-designed automaker said Thursday it would use Nvidia’s autonomous driving stack to power a new partially automated driving system similar to Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (Supervised).
Volvo will use Nvidia’s tech for hands-free, point-to-point driving
The system will be similar to Tesla’s Full Self-Driving in that it will enable hands-free, point-to-point partially automated driving on local roads.
Volvo says the new point-to-point system will be Level 2++, meaning it can handle complex urban environments, including traffic lights, stop signs, and unprotected left turns without explicit driver control. In addition to Tesla’s FSD, it will also resemble the Nvidia-powered system that Mercedes-Benz recently rolled out for the all-new CLA sedan, said Ali Kani, VP and general manager of the automotive team at Nvidia, in an interview with The Verge.
Volvo will use Nvidia’s Hyperion platform, which includes the chipmaker’s high-powered silicon, as well as additional sensors mounted around the vehicle so the car can see and perceive its surroundings. The automaker will also utilize Nvidia’s Alpamayo software, which uses “reasoning” models to make sense of complex road conditions and plan where to steer, brake, or accelerate. The setup will not include lidar, though it could include the laser sensor if Volvo decides to add it in the future.
By expanding its preexisting partnership with Volvo, the automaker is trying to correct some of its failed automated driving projects of the past. The automaker had to effectively sideline its Ride Pilot Level 3 unsupervised autonomous driving system in the US after failing to obtain regulatory approval. Volvo also planned to add lidar sensors to some of its models, but that plan fell away after its supplier Luminar went bankrupt.
Volvo is also bringing its own reputation for safety to the table. The automaker wants to combine its safety expertise with Nvidia’s technology to improve the overall system, including contributing its proprietary driver-understanding systems, which analyze driver behavior in considerably greater detail than a basic driver monitoring system, said Alwin Bakkenes, head of global software engineering at Volvo Cars.
“Our brand Volvo is synonymous with safety, and safety is synonymous with trust,” Bakkenes said in an interview. “People get into our cars not expecting anything bad to happen, but they feel intrinsically that if they’re ever in a situation … we will do our utmost to keep people safe, to protect them from harm.”
Another important component is Volvo’s connected safety technology that allows its vehicles to exchange information about hazards and conditions ahead, including roadworks. Sharing this information can effectively extend the system’s awareness beyond what an individual vehicle’s sensors can detect, potentially improving the operating capabilities of the self-driving functionality.
Volvo plans to make the new point-to-point driving system available across its vehicle lineup, from entry-level to high-end versions — though the company didn’t reveal which models will come first. The timeline was also a little vague, with Bakkenes only confirming that it will launch “before the end of the decade.”
Kani also pointed to the commercial implications, noting that point-to-point driving may prove to be more valuable than a system limited to highway assistance. Nvidia sees the partnership as an opportunity not only to advance the technology but also to help Volvo develop its business model around ongoing software-based offerings, he said.

articles.title: Elon Musk helps GOP Senate super PAC raise record $273 million
articles.text:
The Senate Leadership Fund, the Republican Party's leading Senate super PAC, posted the largest quarterly haul in its history and entered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm election with more than $155 million in cash, according to a new Federal Election Commission filing Thursday.
The SLF brought in $272.9 million from July through September, including $209.7 million from donors.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk supplied the bulk of that money, giving the SLF $158 million in September through an affiliated Texas PAC created to support Republican Ken Paxton. His two contributions of $75 million and $83 million are among the largest political donations ever.
Musk's contribution alone also exceeded the Democratic Senate Majority PAC's entire third-quarter fundraising. That super PAC reported raising a record $151 million during the period and ended September with $111.8 million in cash, which the group said was its third-quarter record. The super PAC's FEC filings are not yet available.
The SLF's haul shattered its own previous records. The group brought in nearly $116 million in the third quarter of 2024 and $111 million in 2022. In 2020, when it filed monthly reports, SLF took in roughly $157 million from July through September. Its previous quarterly high was roughly $216 million in the final three months of 2020, according to a CNBC review of FEC filings.
The record influx gives Republicans a sizable financial cushion as they fight to preserve their 53-seat Senate majority across the country that has become increasingly defensive in the closing weeks of the election.
The SLF paused additional advertising in perennial battleground North Carolina this month after spending more than $30 million there — according to AdImpact data — and redirected resources toward Kansas, where Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces an unexpectedly competitive challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton.
In Nebraska, SLF has committed $15 million to defend Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts, including $7 million through the affiliated Cornhusker Majority, The Wall Street Journal reported this week. Trump carried Nebraska by more than 20 percentage points in 2024.
The super PAC has also been central to the Republican intervention in Texas, where Democrat James Talarico has turned what had been expected to be a safe GOP Senate contest into one of the most expensive races in the country.
Republican groups spent roughly $122 million in Texas in September alone and had another $66 million in advertising reserved through Election Day as of the beginning of October, according to AdImpact data.
Talarico announced Thursday that he raised $64 million in the third quarter, the largest third-quarter haul on record for a Senate candidate. Paxton raised $10.2 million, according to a FEC filing.

articles.title: People in China are spending nearly as much of their income as Americans on healthcare
articles.text:
BEIJING — High healthcare costs are a big factor driving people in China to save, rather than spend, their money, the International Monetary Fund pointed out in a new book titled "Toward a New Economic Growth Model for China."
In rural China, 8.7% of disposable income is spent on healthcare — just second to the U.S. among 20 major economies, the research found. The U.S. ranks the highest in the world with nearly 9.9% of disposable income spent on healthcare.
Urban China ranks third, at 5.4%, slightly more than Canada, the data showed.
The level of the healthcare burden in China grows starker when considering per capita disposable income in the U.S. was $68,289 as of the end of last year — more than 10 times more than China's 43,377 yuan in U.S. dollar terms (around $6,400).
The gap widens further when looking at China's countryside, which only officially emerged from extreme poverty in 2020.
Urban China recorded more than twice the disposable income as rural areas, at 56,502 yuan versus 24,456 yuan, according to official data accessed via Wind Information.
Targeted measures to raise government spending on health and social security in rural areas can significantly reduce the savings rate in rural households, the IMF said, citing prefecture-level analysis.
"China's social spending is low compared with international peers, and increasing that spending would lift consumption," wrote Yizhi Xu, economist in the north Asia division of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, and Fan Zhang, the IMF's deputy resident representative in Beijing.
They recorded a savings rate of around 14% for people from rural areas working in China's cities, and about 6% for people with urban "hukou" residency rights, which give them more social welfare benefits than migrant workers from rural areas.
"Declining house prices in recent years continue to weigh on consumption and contribute to elevated household savings," Xu and Zhang wrote in their section of the IMF book.

articles.title: Cramer's lightning round: Buy Reddit

articles.title: Looking for non-AI stocks to own? Jim Cramer thinks these 2 names are worth buying
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Thursday that investors looking beyond the struggling artificial intelligence trade should consider apparel stocks VF Corp and Kontoor Brands.
VF Corp is the parent company of Vans, The North Face and Timberland. Kontoor, which actually spun out of VF Corp in 2019, is behind the Wrangler, Lee, and Helly Hansen brands.
The recommendations come at an unlikely time for consumer stocks, with rising interest rates and oil prices threatening to squeeze household budgets. "Normally, I'd hesitate to recommend apparel stocks at this point in the business cycle, but VF Corp and Kontoor have already come down dramatically from their highs, and they're trading at depressed valuations," Cramer said. "I think the environment's baked in."
Cramer also said compelling new research suggests shifting fashion trends could breathe new life into both companies, creating buying opportunities that investors may be overlooking. "These upgrades have changed my mind about VF Corp and Kontoor," he added. "Down here, I think both stocks are buys."
Truist and Piper Sandler both raised their ratings on VF Corp to buy — and coincidentally, both shops set $20 price targets, implying roughly 17% upside to Thursday's close.
Cramer was particularly encouraged Tuesday by Piper Sandler's note, which accompanied the firm's fall teen survey. The readthrough on what young consumers like showed a growing interest in non-athletic footwear. That could be welcome news for Vans, whose sales have declined for four consecutive fiscal years, including double-digit drops in each of the past three.
Piper Sandler's survey offered signs that Vans may finally be stabilizing — ranking as the seventh-most-popular footwear brand among male teens after years of sinking in the rankings and climbing to ninth among upper-income male teens. The struggling skateboarding sneaker brand has been the biggest obstacle to VF Corp's turnaround under CEO Bracken Darrell, who took over in July 2023. Vans' sales have dropped nearly 50% since fiscal 2022, while The North Face and Timberland have performed considerably better.
Speaking of those other brands, Timberland entered the top 10 footwear brands among upper-income teens for the first time in the survey's history, while The North Face returned to the top 10 athletic clothing brands among that group. "If the teen survey says buy VF Corp, then I have to say [buy, buy, buy]," the "Mad Money" host said.
Truist similarly expects Vans to benefit as consumers shift away from athletic footwear toward more fashion-oriented styles. With VF Corp trading at roughly 16 times 2027 earnings estimates, Cramer said that "if Vans is finally improving, then this one's definitely a winner."
As for Kontoor, Jefferies upgraded the stock to buy from hold and raised its price target to $89, implying 22% upside from Thursday's close.
The analysts argued that a recent resurgence in denim popularity could prove to be a lasting shift. They identified Kontoor as one of two biggest potential beneficiaries, with Wrangler well positioned to capitalize on the trend.
According to Jefferies, Kontoor's planned $400 million accelerated share repurchase program provides another reason to like the stock. The buyback represents roughly 10% of the company's market cap.
Cramer also highlighted Kontoor's acquisition of Helly Hansen last year as an underappreciated growth opportunity. The outdoor apparel brand should become a larger part of the company's business once Kontoor completes its planned sale of denim brand Lee to Authentic Brands. The deal, valued at up to $1 billion, was announced in May and is expected to close later this year.
With Kontoor trading at roughly 14 times 2026 EPS estimates, Cramer said the stock offers an attractive way to capitalize on the denim revival without paying a premium valuation. "That's a smart investment," he said.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says this week's AI sell-off offers a crucial lesson for investors
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Thursday that this week's turbulence in artificial intelligence stocks is delivering a painful reminder of why investors shouldn't put all their money into the market's hottest trade.
After months of AI infrastructure stocks leading the market, Cramer said investors who maintained exposure to other sectors are finally seeing the benefits of diversification. On Thursday, Kimberly-Clark gained 4.7%, Waste Management climbed 3.9% and Eli Lilly advanced 3.6%. For the week, all three stocks are up at least 6%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), meanwhile, posted its eighth-straight day of declines, its longest losing streak in more than a decade.
"We don't talk enough about diversification, in part because it's no fun when one group keeps outperforming the rest of the market," the "Mad Money" host said. "But when that group crashed to earth over the last few weeks, only diversification could save your portfolio."
Cramer pointed to the CNBC Investing Club's Charitable Trust as an example. On Sept. 1, the portfolio exited its position in AI beneficiary Corning, then a day later bought Huggies parent Kimberly-Clark to reduce its exposure to the data center trade. The move initially looked premature as Corning continued climbing and Kimberly-Clark declined, but the recent rotation has begun to vindicate that decision.
"Corning's rolling over while Kimberly-Clark's taking off," Cramer said. Corning shares have fallen almost 5% since the Club's exit. The Club has added to Kimberly-Clark on multiple occasions to reduce its cost basis and is sitting on an unrealized loss of less than 1%. Shares have gained more than 10% from its Oct. 1 low.
Cramer acknowledged that it's unclear how long the rotation away from AI will last. But he warned that investors who become too concentrated in one sector risk losses that could drive them out of the market altogether.
"If you're too concentrated, you'll get blown out, possibly giving up on the entire asset class," he said.
Cramer's Charitable Trust owns shares of INTC, KMB, LLY, NVDA.

articles.title: S&P 500 futures are little changed as index heads for losing week: Live updates
articles.text:
S&P 500 futures were relatively unchanged on Thursday after the S&P 500 posted its first winning session in four, with investors shaking off the latest sell-off in technology stocks.
Futures tied to the broad market average traded just below the flatline, while Nasdaq-100 futures were off 0.3%. Futures linked to the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 10 points.
The three major averages finished Thursday's session in the green as investors rotated out of key tech names and into other parts of the market. The S&P 500 finished up roughly 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite lagged, inching up only about 0.1%. Both snapped a three-day losing streak. The Dow was the leader among the three, jumping more than 500 points, or around 1.1%.
A slide in stocks related to the artificial intelligence trade, especially those in the memory chip space, has weighed on the market this week amid jitters about competition from China. Micron Technology, which finished higher Thursday, is on pace for a decline of more than 9% on the week. Others like Seagate Technology and Western Digital are also pacing for a losing week.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 was poised to rise, with its Chicago futures contract at 65,460, compared with the index's previous close of 64,425.95. Hong Kong Hang Seng index futures were at 24,274, compared with the index's last close of 24,062.72. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was 1.02% higher in early trade.
Investors have also grown concerned that tech companies are borrowing too much for the AI buildout. Neocloud stocks like CoreWeave, which also recovered Thursday from a steep drop in the prior session, is heading for a 15% on the week.
Further, Anthropic has told investors that its third-quarter revenue is $16.8 billion . The disclosure comes as traders fixate on growth in the AI space and whether it's strong enough to back up the recent gains in chipmakers. Chip stocks like Nvidia and Broadcom are in the red this week.
This week's losses have placed the S&P 500 and Nasdaq in negative territory week to date, as the former has fallen nearly 1% in the period, while the latter has tumbled more than 2%. The Dow, on the other hand, is on track for a roughly 1% increase on the week.
"One of the real challenges we've had in AI and technology overall for the last six to 12 months is that so much of what's happening is happening in private markets," Jeff Richards, managing partner at Notable Capital, told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Thursday. He noted that AI-linked companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, among others, going public could help assuage investor concerns.
"Once we get more of the information out there – analyst coverage, detailed information on core metrics – into the market over the course of '27, I think a lot of those fears will ease," he said.
Outside of tech, investors have been grappling with hotter-than-expected inflation data, which has been exacerbated by elevated energy prices in the wake of the U.S.-Iran war. Wholesale inflation this week saw its biggest gain since 2022, while consumer inflation remained well above the Federal Reserve's target of 2%.
Investors are now looking ahead to more earnings results due for release before the bell Friday, including Travelers and Citizens Financial.

articles.title: Netflix Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria is leaving, will be replaced by Peter Rice
articles.text:
Netflix on Thursday announced Bela Bajaria will be replaced as the company's chief content officer by former Disney exec Peter Rice, effective Oct. 26.
Rice most recently oversaw Disney's cable channels, news programming and coverage of major sporting events.
"Peter is one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry," co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in a statement. "I'm excited to welcome him to Netflix as Chief Content Officer as we continue to scale and deliver members more of the stories they love."
Before Rice was at Disney, he held roles at 21st Century Fox and Fox Searchlight Pictures. Netflix in its announcement called him "one of the entertainment industry's most respected creative executives." In his new role, Rice will oversee the company's global content organization, including scripted and unscripted series, film and live events.
"[Netflix has] shown again and again that they're willing to take chances on distinctive voices and fresh ideas, and I'm excited to work with the team to help bring even more great stories to members everywhere," he said in a statement.
Bajaria, who is leaving Netflix after nearly 10 years, most recently led the company's global content team. She had been focused on the company's live sports strategy, looking to create events out of buzzy games and tournaments.
"I'm incredibly grateful for everything she's done to help Netflix entertain the world," Sarandos said in a statement.
The announcement comes a day after Netflix instituted layoffs across its organization, eliminating approximately 6% of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 jobs. Shares of the company are down more than 20% this year, though the stock remained relatively unchanged in extended trading Thursday.
The media company will report its next quarterly earnings on Tuesday.
