articles.title: Trump says Nidal Hasan execution won't be livestreamed
articles.text:
President Donald Trump said Thursday that the planned execution by firing squad of convicted Fort Hood mass killer Nidal Hasan would not be livestreamed, canceling the Pentagon's plans to do so.
Trump's announcement came after growing backlash against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's effort to show the former U.S. Army major's execution live online, with concern that the footage would become a recruiting tool for terrorists.
Hasan, who is paralyzed from the waist down, is scheduled to be executed Dec. 3 by an Army firing squad at 1 p.m. Central Time in Fort Hood, which is located in Killeen, Texas.
Hasan, who during his 2013 court-martial said he was motivated to defend the "leadership of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, the Taliban," could seek to delay the execution with a new legal challenge.
"Nidal Malik Hasan, a former U.S. Army Major turned traitor, is a very bad and evil man," Trump said Thursday in a Truth Social post. The president noted Hasan had killed 13 people — one of whom was pregnant — and injured 32 others in the Nov. 5, 2009, shooting spree.
"With all of that being said, I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote.
"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed."
"That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose," Trump wrote. "They deserve to witness JUSTICE!"
Hours before Trump's announcement, a Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll was released and showed that 80% of Americans said the execution should not be streamed live, versus just 18% who supported the idea.
About 53% of Americans support Hasan's execution by firing squad, according to the poll of 2,545 U.S. adults, which had a margin of error of plus or minus two percentage points.
Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell, in a statement to CNBC after Trump's announcement, said, "President Trump and Secretary Hegseth spoke about the decision to not livestream Hasan's execution ahead of the Truth Social announcement."
"The Secretary supports the President's decision, and they are completely aligned," Parnell said.
On Monday, Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who leads the Catholic Archdiocese for the Military Services, USA, said in a statement that any Catholics assigned to the firing squad should "request to be excused from this action contrary to the teaching of the Church."
The Pentagon on Oct. 5 said Trump had approved a recommendation by Hegseth to have Hasan, 56, executed by an Army firing squad.
Presidential approval is required for military executions under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.
Hasan would be the first member of the U.S. military executed by firing squad since World War II. The execution also would be the first carried out by the U.S. military since 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was hanged at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, for the rape and attempted murder of a girl in Austria.
Hegseth on Oct. 8 said the execution would be at Fort Hood and, "He's going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be."
"And we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public, because people need to understand that ... there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said.
The Pentagon later said it would be livestreamed.
Before Trump's announcement Thursday that the livestream would not happen, it was unclear which major video-streaming platforms, if any, would have aired the execution.
The Verge reported last week that YouTube, Twitch, Meta and X did not respond when asked if they would allow the execution on their sites, while TikTok pointed to the company's policies barring "shocking and graphic content."
Vice President JD Vance raised doubts last week about whether the livestream is "actually going to happen," saying he would not watch it if it did.
"So whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don't forget that this is the guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people," Vance said. "Now, that said, if it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it."
Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., last week said in a post on X that the idea of livestreaming the execution was "beyond disgusting."
"Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," Tillis posted. "It should not be happening in America."
Former Army Sgt. Alonzo Lunsford, whom Hasan shot seven times during the attack, said he opposed the execution being livestreamed even as he said he planned to attend it in person.
"I want to be in the room where I can see him, and he can see me," Lunsford said last week, according to CBS News. "People have to be held accountable for their sins, but I don't want this to be some pay-per-view event, like some John Wick movie."
"As a country, we're better than that."
Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops, condemned the plan to show the execution publicly.
"Our God is the God of life. In no way can [Hasan's] actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered. The word of God exhorts us: 'do not repay anyone evil for evil,'" Coakley said, quoting St. Paul's Letter to the Romans.
"The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people," Coakley said.
CNBC has reached out to the Pentagon for comment on Trump's post.
Nader Hasan, a cousin of Nidal who had spoken out after the Fort Hood shooting, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
University of Notre Dame Law School Professor Richard Garnett said, "The president's decision to abandon the livestreaming plan will, among other things, head off legal challenges that would likely have delayed the scheduled execution."
"As a wide range of officials and citizens have noted, a livestreamed execution would have more likely resulted in brutalization of viewers and coarsening of culture than in deterrence," Garnett said.

articles.title: AWS, Anthropic race to deploy army of specialized engineers key to proving AI spending will pay off
articles.text:
After spending billions building artificial intelligence, Big Tech is now spending heavily to build the human workforce needed to prove the investments are paying off.
Companies are scrambling to find specialized AI engineers who can put the technology to work inside businesses. These specialists — called forward deployed engineers, or FDEs — combine advanced AI and software expertise with an understanding of how corporations operate. They could be the key humans in the loop required to turn powerful large language models into enterprise systems that can deliver measurable business results.
Market concerns that the economics of the AI boom are not sustainable have intensified this week with many top AI-themed and memory-themed stocks from Dell to CoreWeave, AMD and Micron suffering significant short-term losses.
Amazon Web Services has committed $1 billion to a forward-deployed engineering initiative. OpenAI has launched a deployment business backed by more than $4 billion in initial investment. Anthropic is putting $100 million into a program to train 10,000 forward-deployed engineers by the end of 2027. And Accenture and Google Cloud are building a 1,000-person forward-deployed engineering workforce.
"The Street is starting to become impatient with these billions of companies who are spending on AI without getting any business outcomes," said Jeff Christian, founder of executive search firm Christian & Timbers.
Working directly with customers, FDEs navigate existing technology systems, security requirements, and organizational obstacles to turn promising AI experiments into applications companies can actually use.
At Caylent, an AWS consulting partner that embeds FDEs with customers, CEO Val Henderson said the role requires more than technical expertise.
"The hardest thing to teach is the customer EQ, without question," she said, adding that engineers also need to understand customers and businesses, navigate organizational dynamics, and exercise judgment when projects encounter unexpected problems.
A surge in job postings, salaries with scarce talent available
Experienced talent is scarce, and developing that expertise can't happen overnight in a labor market race that recent hiring numbers suggest is accelerating.
U.S. job postings for FDEs surged from fewer than 200 in 2023 to approximately 1,200 in 2025 and more than 7,300 in the first nine months of 2026, according to data from labor market analytics firm Lightcast.
Median advertised salaries reached $195,456 during that period, up 40% from 2023 and more than three times the median advertised salary across all U.S. job postings.
The competition extends well beyond the companies developing AI models. Consulting firms are among the biggest recruiters, reflecting demand for engineers who can help corporate clients implement the technology.
Lightcast counted 872 unique FDE job postings from Deloitte and 688 from Accenture during the first nine months of 2026, followed by Google with 499 and KPMG with 447. The figures represent advertised positions, not completed hires.
"Demand for forward deployed engineers is rising fast, and growing wages suggest employers are competing for a limited pool of talent," said Elena Magrini, head of global research at Lightcast.
But the data also points to a potential solution.
"FDE is not an entirely new role. It shares roughly half of its skills with software engineering, creating an opportunity to tap into a much broader talent pool," said Magrini.
Technology companies and their corporate clients are investing in multiple ways to develop deployment expertise.
AWS is building its own FDE organization, drawing on experienced engineers within Amazon and AWS while also recruiting externally. The company is starting with hundreds of engineers, according to Asa Kalavade, vice president of forward-deployed engineering at AWS.
"We are investing $1 billion now because customers need this hands-on help turning their AI investments into results at speed," Kalavade said.
OpenAI is pursuing a broader enterprise deployment strategy, backed by the $4 billion in initial investment and an agreement earlier this year to acquire Tomoro, an applied AI consulting and engineering firm expected to bring approximately 150 experienced FDEs and deployment specialists into the operation.
AI skills gap is a 'market problem'
Anthropic is taking a different approach, training engineers already employed by its customers and partners. Through its Claude Frontier Academy, the company aims to train 10,000 FDEs by the end of 2027. Its first residency cohorts include engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley, and Novo Nordisk.
"The AI skills gap affects every customer and every partner, so it is a market problem, and Anthropic is committed to helping close it," said Steve Corfield, Anthropic's global head of business development and partnerships.
Accenture and Google Cloud, meanwhile, are building a 1,000-person FDE workforce, relying partly on retraining experienced software engineers for customer-facing AI deployment work.
"The reality is that experienced FDEs cannot simply be recruited at the scale clients need," said Ram Ramalingam, Accenture's FDE and software and platform engineering lead. Depending on their backgrounds, the company's FDE training and onboarding can take 30 to 90 days, Ramalingam said. He added that participants already have substantial software engineering experience; the program is designed to add specialized deployment capabilities rather than train beginners.
AWS also sees an opportunity to develop expertise inside customer organizations. Kalavade said many businesses already employ capable engineers but need help learning how to move AI projects into production. AWS's FDEs work alongside those teams so customers can eventually maintain and expand the systems themselves.
The challenge goes beyond technical expertise, said Corfield. "A skill in short supply is an engineer who can understand how the business works and also build the system that changes it," he said.
Anthropic believes some of that expertise can be developed through structured engineering. Its Frontier Deployed Engineer Residency borrows from medical education, pairing experienced engineers with practitioners and evaluating them on realistic enterprise deployments.
"We modeled the residency on how medicine trains doctors," Corfield said. Participants learn from practicing engineers, work on realistic cases, and are assessed before they practice on their own companies, according to Anthropic. They then receive 12 weeks of mentorship from Anthropic engineers while working on Claude projects. The first full credentials are expected in early 2027.
Too soon to analyze results from deployments
According to Christian, experienced FDEs can help expand the workforce by leading teams of less-experienced engineers. For instance, he said, those who have completed 10 to 15 successful deployments may have the judgment to supervise teams of five or six, passing along expertise gained from working through complicated customer projects.
Christian sees that mentorship model as a way to expand deployment teams without requiring an elite engineer in every position.
But Henderson said the customer-facing judgment required for complex AI deployments is particularly difficult to teach. While technical skills can be developed through training, engineers also need experience navigating real-world customer challenges.
"There is no compression algorithm for experience," Henderson said.
For Christian, the challenge comes back to the pressure from investors to produce business results. He argued that companies need engineers who can work directly with customers to translate increasingly powerful AI systems into practical applications. "The only way you can get AI to work is by human-to-human interaction," he said.
The ultimate test is whether this expanding workforce can help companies generate the return on investment from AI that justifies the upfront costs. To date, the available evidence from FDE projects falls short of confirmation. Some early deployments show productivity improvements but not financial returns, according to company-reported case studies.
At mortgage lender PennyMac, Caylent's FDEs worked alongside product managers and engineers on an AI-enabled mortgage servicing platform. Some engineering tasks were completed as much as six times faster, depending on the task, according to a case study provided by AWS.
Another Caylent engagement involved Smarsh, a communications compliance software provider. A company case study estimated that the project freed $5 million to $10 million in engineering and product capacity that could be redirected to other work. Caylent confirmed that FDEs participated in the project, although the figure does not isolate their contribution or represent equivalent cash savings.
These improvements in engineering productivity and capacity are not independently verified returns on AI investment.
Anthropic's ambitious training initiative has yet to demonstrate measurable results. Corfield acknowledged that it is still too early for outcome data and said the company plans to track how quickly participants' projects reach production and how extensively those systems are used.

articles.title: Tale of two markets: Our 3 biggest winners and losers over the past five weeks
articles.text: Wall Street has become increasingly divided since our last CNBC Investing Club Monthly Meeting . The selling in recent days, however, has intensified on worries about the AI trade, making the likes of Micron among our biggest losers week-to-date and defensives such as Cardinal Health among our biggest weekly winners. As of Wednesday's close, the Nasdaq was down over 2.5% so far this week, with the less tech-exposed Dow Jones Industrial Average up about 1% since last Friday's close. Another hot inflation report Thursday morning and another terrible day for AI stocks were widening the gap between the haves and have-nots. Expectations of at least one more Federal Reserve interest rate hike before year-end are not helping investors feel any better about whether companies are borrowing too much to fund the AI infrastructure buildout. From our Sept. 10 meeting through Wednesday's close, the tech story on aggregate was doing better. Nasdaq was actually 2.3% higher over the period, and the Dow was down nearly 1%. Ahead of our October Monthly Meeting livestream, let's review the winners and losers in our 32-stock portfolio as a baseline as we try to figure out where the market goes from here. Winners CrowdStrike up 19.4% Cybersecurity stocks surged as growing concerns about the risks posed by increasingly powerful artificial intelligence models reinforced the need for companies to protect their networks and data. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's essay calling for frontier AI labs to slow the pace of model development amid growing safety concerns helped fuel the rally. CrowdStrike has more than doubled this year — making us cautious about chasing the stock after its powerful runs. Still, we continue to view cybersecurity as a " cornerstone " of our portfolio, with AI adoption providing another long-term growth driver. Meta Platforms up 14.4% The Facebook and Instagram parent is starting to show investors how its massive AI investments could pay off. Shares have surged since the Sept. 8 launch of Muse, its personal AI agent, which quickly climbed to the top of the app charts. Meta built on that momentum this week with the release of Muse Wonder and the more powerful Muse Wonder Full, demonstrating its ability to compete with leading AI developers. Wells Fargo said Muse Wonder Full has reached the "AI frontier," ranking among the industry's most advanced models. The releases could help Meta Platforms attract more paying subscribers to Muse and its coding tools, opening up new revenue streams beyond advertising. While it's too early to know how meaningful that revenue could become, the steady pace of AI releases is helping ease earlier concerns about whether Meta's billions in AI spending would generate sufficient returns. TJX Companies up 13% Shares of the off-price retailer rebounded from a steep sell-off following disappointing August earnings and broader pressure on consumer stocks from higher inflation and interest rates. Investors had grown concerned after second-quarter results that showed slowing comparable sales at Marmaxx, the company's largest division, which includes TJ Maxx and Marshalls. At the time, the CEO said it was a product mix problem, which was being addressed. However, a recent Morgan Stanley survey suggests the weakness more broadly in Q2 was driven more by consumers pulling back on spending. That's encouraging for our thesis that TJX's value-focused model and ability to acquire excess merchandise at attractive prices should help it navigate a challenging retail environment. We took advantage of the post-earnings weakness to add to our position several times and remain optimistic about the longer-term opportunity, even if a meaningful sales recovery takes another quarter or two. Losers Bank of New York down 15.4% and Goldman Sachs down 13.8% Our financial holdings were among the portfolio's biggest laggards as the Fed's first rate hike in three years back at its September meeting intensified concerns about the outlook for banks. Higher rates can increase funding costs, weaken loan demand, and slow capital markets activity — like mergers and acquisitions (M & A) and initial public offerings (IPOs). Still, investors shouldn't paint the entire sector with the same brush . Despite solid earnings from Goldman Sachs on Tuesday, the stock continued to decline . We view the pullback as a buying opportunity . On Thursday, BNY reported earnings and saw better-than-expected fee growth. Members, watch out in the afternoon for our full Club analysis on BNY's quarter in your texts and emails. FedEx Freight down 12.4% Shares of the less-than-truckload shipping company struggled as the ongoing Iran war drove diesel prices higher. The weakness extended across the transportation sector, with the iShares Transportation ETF falling 3% and trucking company J.B. Hunt sliding 13% since our last Monthly Meeting. While we remain optimistic about FedEx Freight's long-term prospects, we'll be looking for signs of improving shipping demand and the company's ability to manage elevated costs before becoming more constructive on the stock's near-term outlook. Boeing down 9.8% The plane maker has come under pressure amid rising fuel prices, broader concerns about the aerospace industry and a software issue affecting certain 737 Max aircraft. Higher oil prices threaten airline profitability and could weigh on demand for new planes, adding to investor anxiety about the manufacturer's recovery. Boeing also disclosed a software glitch that could affect certain landing procedures, raising questions about the certification timeline for the 737 Max 10, which Boeing and airlines expected to come in early fall. However, the Federal Aviation Administration determined Oct. 2 that the issue does not pose a flight-safety concern , clearing a potential obstacle to certification. articles.title: Small-cap stocks quietly slide into correction territory
articles.text: Tech is getting all the headlines this week — and rightfully so — but other parts of the stock market are faring even worse. The Russell 2000 , which tracks the performance of small-cap stocks, fell into correction territory on Wednesday, ending the day down 11% from an Aug. 14 record close. For the week, the benchmark is down 2.8%, slightly underperforming the Nasdaq Composite's 2.5% decline. Several factors are going against small caps right now. First, inflation shows no signs of slowing. The consumer and producer price index reports released this week came in hotter than expected. And while Treasury yields have pulled back sharply this week, investors are increasingly betting the Federal Reserve will have to raise rates at least once more before year-end . Second, sentiment among small businesses has deteriorated. The NFIB Small Business Optimism index fell to 97.9 in September from 98.7 in August . .RUT YTD bar Russell 2000 in correction territory To be sure, strategists at BCA Research noted Wednesday that smaller firms are "not yet feeling the bite from higher rates." "Among single most important problems reported by small business owners, the quality / availability of labor and inflation remain the top 2 concerns, both of which increased in September," they wrote to clients. "Despite a significant rise in bond yields, there is no appreciable increase in the number of small businesses reporting financial conditions or interest rates as their number one problem." That said, they noted that the "impact of rising rates showed up with a lag in 2021 and 2022, and small businesses may only be starting to feel the impact of rising yields." The outlook for stocks in general seems shakier as well. Earlier this week, legendary investor Paul Tudor Jones noted that next year "is going to be really, really challenging for the stock market." "You've probably got the most negative flow picture for the U.S. stock market that we've had, say, since 2002," he told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Tuesday .

articles.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Thursday
articles.text: My top 10 things to watch Thursday, Oct. 15 1. Fulcrum day. Is it too early for a crescendo sell-off? Seeing a huge flight to quality this morning. But the AI trade is under pressure again after yesterday's brutal sell-off. Inflation is still running hot, with this morning's wholesale producer price index coming in way above expectations. The geopolitical problems in the Middle East and with the Russia-Ukraine war also haven't abated at all. 2. If you want real-time analysis of what's happening in this fast-moving market, with real money on the line, sign up to join the Investing Club before our October Monthly Meeting today. Kicks off at noon ET. Hourlong program. I will talk about the big forces driving the action, and then my partner Jeff Marks and I will cover each stock in our portfolio and debate whether we need to make any moves. 3. South Korea's Kospi remains the epicenter of the AI hardware problems, plunging over 7% today. SK Hynix is down another 6% in the U.S. premarket. Shares of the South Korean memory giant closed yesterday back under their $149 July initial public offering price. These Kospi moves overnight have been the tail wagging the U.S. artificial intelligence trade dog. 4. CoreWeave shares continue to deteriorate — down roughly 4% this morning after yesterday's nearly 15.5% decline. CoreWeave's bonds are also selling off, pushing yields into the stratosphere. This is the nexus of bond/financing cost fears. CoreWeave stock is approaching its Situational Awareness blow-up lows of just above $60 in late July. Battleground: Deutsche Bank said buy the dip, while Bernstein doubled down on its sell call. 5. Anthropic disclosed a roughly 45% sequential increase in third-quarter revenue to $16.8 billion, according to CNBC sources . Healthy growth. But much slower than the 146% revenue gain from Q1 to Q2. Still, some investors expect Anthropic to hit an annualized revenue rate north of $100 billion by year-end, per The Wall Street Journal . So, maybe we should not overstate the slowdown? 6. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. sees no end in sight for chip demand. Sixth straight quarter of record net profit for TMSC, paired with strong guidance. In this anti-AI market, however, maybe it's not strong enough. Shares of the world's largest chip fabricator are down this morning following declines in six of the past seven sessions. 7. Microsoft is now loved again (along with many other software stocks). UBS issued a big price target hike: $675 from $525. Expectations are rising for its Azure cloud unit and M365 software suite into earnings, but analysts said they still expect Microsoft to clear these higher bars. There are important investing lessons to learn from Microsoft's road back to its first record close in almost a year. We covered them yesterday in a piece for the Club. 8. Top and bottom line beat for Club name Bank of New York , sending shares up almost 2% premarket. Will the move hold? Been a chilly reception to bank earnings this week, even when the prints were good. BNY's numbers certainly look good and better than rival State Street , with both net interest income and fee revenue topping consensus. Conference call kicks off at 11 a.m. ET. 9. Penske Automotive Group agreed to be taken private by its two biggest shareholders — Penske Corp and Mitsui — at an enterprise valuation of $16.3 billion. Notable because Wells Fargo was one of the financial advisors on the deal. CEO Charlie Scharf has been building up its investment banking business, strategy we love for this Club holding. We upgraded our rating on Wells after earnings Tuesday. 10. Mizuho Securities cut its price target on Honeywell Technologies to $255 from $265 ahead of earnings. Kept its buy rating on the stock. We had owned this one for the Club for years, but yesterday we decided we'd had enough and sold the rest of our stake, which we had cut in half last month. articles.title: You may never work with an Elizabeth Holmes—but here's how to handle a co-worker who makes false claims
articles.text:
Elizabeth Holmes spent some of her last days out of prison with a film crew. She was trying, it seems, to clear her name.
"You really feel you did nothing wrong?" Nathan Fielder, who co-directed the film "You Can See Everything," asks Holmes in the trailer. "I did not," she answers. Slated for theatrical release on Friday, the documentary had a surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in September that brought Holmes back into the public eye.
Holmes built the now-dissolved blood-testing company Theranos to a multi-billion-dollar valuation and assembled a luminary-filled board of directors on the back of revolutionary promises, some of which never materialized. She was convicted on multiple counts of fraud in 2022 and sentenced to 135 months, or more than 11 years, in prison.
She argued in her trial defense that she believed Theranos' fledgling technology worked. In a Sept. 27 post on X, Holmes doubled down, writing: "I am fighting to prove my innocence."
Though it's impossible to see inside someone's head, onlookers have debated over the years whether Holmes was sincere in believing her own outlandish claims.
You may never work with someone as infamous and enigmatic as Holmes. But how do you handle a co-worker who appears to believe their own false statements? They might be charming, charismatic and earnest. You, and others, might desperately want to believe what they're saying. But when a pattern starts to emerge, you can't ignore it, because you could be left holding the bag when things unravel.
I've consulted for major companies including Google and Microsoft, and taught executive education for more than a decade at Columbia Business School and Duke University's Fuqua School of Business. I've seen how difficult it can be to deal with a colleague who just can't seem to be straight with you, whether they never deliver their work as promised or constantly misrepresent situations.
When you don't have the power to personally remove them from their position, you have to find creative workarounds, so you can get your own job done. Here are five strategies you can use when you're dealing with a co-worker who seems a little delusional.
1. Separate the person from the behavior
One of the most confusing parts about having a co-worker behave this way is that you might genuinely like them. It often feels inspiring to be around people who have a vision and a can-do attitude. That energy can mobilize a team around big goals and lead to genuine progress, even if you don't hit your boldest targets.
But it's helpful only up to a point. A repeated pattern of unrealistic expectations and broken promises damages trust and hurts your entire organization. You don't have to see the person as a villain to recognize that their behavior is causing problems.
2. Build in a margin of error
Think back to the promises your colleague has made to you, write them down and compare them to the outcome. Did they promise to get you a report and then deliver it a week late without apologizing or even acknowledging they missed the deadline? Did they assure you they were on track for 100 new customers by the end of the quarter and only deliver 25 without explanation?
Look for patterns in their over- or under-estimations. Are they inaccurate about speed, volume or sentiment? With that data in mind, you can begin to translate what they're telling you to create your own, more realistic estimates. If they tell you something will be ready in a month, you'll know to plan for two. Their wild overconfidence won't cause downstream problems for your team, because you'll already be prepared.
As you do this exercise for yourself, start documenting. Keep track of communications and outcomes that don't match in case you need them later to escalate the situation up to your boss, leadership or HR.
3. Create checkpoints
The problems that affect you most are the ones you never saw coming. It's hard to pivot last-minute when you're blindsided by unforeseen developments. So put a monitoring system in place to avoid surprises, as much as possible, from an unpredictable colleague.
If you're working on a joint project, identify checkpoints when you'll establish where things really are. For instance, if your co-worker promised you a prototype in six weeks, you can create a checklist of milestones ranging from "customer surveys" to "design mockups" to "sourcing materials" to "fabrication of device."
If they're assuring you everything is on track at week four, but no design mockups have even been created, it's reasonable to assume they'll miss the deadline — and you can prepare now, rather than scrambling later.
But ultimately, there are only so many ways you can personally compensate for a colleague's poor performance or broken promises. The next step is to involve others.
4. Get external support
When someone is feeding you inaccurate information one-on-one, they can pretend you misunderstood. That's much harder to do when there are witnesses. Actively involve your manager or co-workers in planning sessions so that any commitments are made publicly, and your manager can handle follow-up and accountability.
Your colleague might think twice about making grandiose promises if they understand that a failure will be visible to everyone. But sometimes, even the risk of public embarrassment isn't enough to stop them.
5. Escalate and extricate yourself
You probably don't have the authority to fire your co-worker, and it can be tricky to actively try to get them fired. Rather than pushing for their ouster — and risking their wrath if they find out — you can concentrate on a different goal you have much more control over: limiting your dependence on them. 
Because you've already involved your manager, by now they're well aware of that person's shortcomings. So they won't be surprised, and will likely be sympathetic, when you come to them and say: "I need your help. My team has been delayed three times because Jeremy told us he'd have the mockups ready, and it hasn't happened. It's unsustainable for us to rely on him. Can we think creatively about how to ensure my team's work is able to proceed?" 
There are at least three potential outcomes:
- You'll get support for a creative solution. Let's say your boss can't fire the hypothetical Jeremy either, whether it's because he's outside their chain of command or because he has "protected status" in the organization as the protege of a top leader. But your boss will want to help you get your own work done, so they might let you partner with outside vendors or bring in a new team member to work around Jeremy.
- Your co-worker will get fired. Alternatively, it's possible your appraisal may be the evidence your boss wants and needs to make the case that Jeremy should go, and they'll be grateful you provided the impetus.
- You've protected yourself. If your boss literally can't do anything, you've at least flagged the problem so that any future failures will be contextualized — "of course, they were relying on Jeremy" — rather than seen as your own inability to deliver.
It's incredibly challenging to deal with a colleague who seems to believe their own false claims. But these strategies will help you avoid getting dragged down when their lies and exaggerations are finally discovered.
Dorie Clark taught executive education for more than a decade at Columbia Business School and Duke University's Fuqua School of Business. She is a keynote speaker, former presidential campaign spokeswoman, and bestselling author of "The Long Game." You can subscribe to her e-newsletter here.

articles.title: The Diesel Crunch Will Persist Well into 2027 | OilPrice.com
articles.text:
The recent rise in crude oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz isn’t solving the world’s most pressing fuel problem—the diesel crunch and record diesel prices that start to feed into the wider economy.
While Middle East crude oil flows are nearing pre-war levels, global diesel supply is much lower due to refinery constraints in the Middle East and Russia that the rest of the world cannot offset.
The diesel squeeze hiked wholesale and retail prices to record highs in the middle of September as the market realized that crude oil supply does not equal refined product supply, and demand for middle distillates started rising seasonally from agriculture, road freight, and the coming winter.
There isn’t an easy fix to the crunch, neither the G7’s promised release of 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, nor the controversial Trump-Putin deal for the U.S. to buy Russian diesel.
The global diesel squeeze will end when markets return to some kind of normality, which is months away, at best, and certainly not before the U.S. midterm elections on November 3.
Diesel Tightness To Extend into 2027, IEA Says
The current crunch in the diesel and gasoil markets is set to extend into the middle of next year, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly Oil Market Report published this week.
Counter-seasonally, gasoil and diesel markets tightened in the third quarter of 2026, amid prolonged disruptions in refinery operations in the Middle East and Russia, the agency noted.
“Combined with much heavier-than-normal inventory declines in 2Q26, this has deprived global gasoil markets of crucial stock cover ahead of the peak winter demand season,” the IEA said.
But the relatively price-inelastic diesel demand has remained strong, supported by government measures aimed at easing the impact of high prices on consumers, according to the agency.
“Falling inventories, soaring cracks, and steepening levels of backwardation have signalled the need for additional supplies,” the IEA said.
Even if refinery throughput recovers rapidly into the end of this year, gasoil supply will fall short of meeting demand this quarter, “suggesting that the replenishment of lost inventories, outside of typical seasonal fluctuations, is unlikely before 2H27.”
Global diesel exports fell by 700,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September from a year earlier, as a 1.3-million-bpd loss from Russia and the Middle East was only partly offset by higher supply from other sources, the IEA has estimated.
“As the Iran war manifests itself through restricted product availability, soaring fuel prices and a deteriorating economic outlook, diesel will register 25%” of the expected 2.6 million bpd decline in global oil demand this year, the agency noted.
Global diesel prices have eased from the all-time highs of more than $200 a barrel reached in September, but diesel benchmarks remain nearly double the price of crude oil and their pre-crisis levels, the IEA said.
Crude Oil Supply Doesn’t Mean Diesel Supply
While growing volumes of crude oil have moved out of the Persian Gulf and the Middle East in recent weeks, the barrels come at a high cost and high risk, Ole Hansen, Head of Commodity Strategy at Saxo Bank, wrote in an analysis this week.
“Depleted inventories, elevated freight costs and persistent geopolitical risks explain why crude prices have remained stubbornly high despite improving physical flows,” Hansen said. Related: Europe’s Gas Prices Close to 2022 High as Hormuz LNG Flows Remain Limited
The diesel market, however, is a whole new ball game. Additional crude oil exports cannot ease the reduced refinery output in the Middle East, which was a major diesel and jet fuel supplier before the war.
“While crude shipments have recovered substantially, refined-product exports remain severely constrained,” Hansen said.
“The clearest evidence that the market remains far from normal is the continued strength in refined products, particularly diesel.”
Both U.S. ultra-low sulfur diesel (ULSD) and European gasoil futures moved back to trade above $200 per barrel equivalent this week, “reflecting a shortage that additional crude exports alone cannot resolve,” the strategist said.
This shortage cannot be solved with high crude oil exports. The global energy system needs normalization in all major supply chain components from production to transportation and refining for prices to ease. The oil crisis has now turned into a shipping crisis and a refining bottleneck, which add to the supply squeeze in products and to inflation pressures.
Economic Spillover
“Record diesel prices are already having broad economic consequences by raising the cost of goods and impacting real incomes, economic activity, and inflation,” the IEA warned in its report.
The diesel price shock is extending from transport through supply chains, analysts at Oxford Economics said earlier this month.
Some of the costs transferred to customers have started to emerge in the U.S. This year has seen a renewed surge in operating-cost pressures for U.S. trucking, driven overwhelmingly by diesel, while freight trucking producer prices have also begun to rise, Oxford Economics says.
“This suggests carriers are passing at least part of the fuel shock onto customers rather than absorbing it entirely through margins, shifting some of the burden toward the freight-intensive industries.”
U.S. inflation accelerated in September, with the consumer price index up by 3.7% from a year earlier and 0.6% compared to August, the last inflation numbers before the midterms showed on Wednesday.
“The index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all-items increase. The energy index increased 5.2 percent over the month following a 2.1-percent increase in August,” the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics said.
By Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com

articles.title: Exxon’s Oil Boom Could Keep Guyana’s Gas at Home | OilPrice.com
articles.text:
Guyana has turned into something of an oil celebrity with billions of barrels discovered by Exxon off the coast of the tiny South American country. With the oil riches came gas, too, and there were plans to add LNG to Guyana’s export goods. Yet now the government is considering keeping the gas for the domestic market.
Guyana’s crude oil exports are about to end the year on a high note and a daily rate of over 1 million barrels, according to a recent report by Bloomberg. It only took the country 10 years to go from no oil production to that rate of exports, after Exxon and its partners in the Stabroek Block—Hess Corp and CNOOC—made a string of discoveries with reserves estimated at over 11 billion barrels.
Production ramped up fast, with Exxon and partners bringing in a total of four floating production, storage, and offloading vessels to the Stabroek Block. As a result of this fast development, by September this year, wells in the block had yielded a cumulative 1 billion barrels of oil. Exxon and CNOOC, plus new partner Chevron, are not stopping, either. By 2030, Exxon eyes production capacity of 1.7 million barrels daily from eight offshore projects. This is what is interfering with natural gas plans.
Two years ago, the government of Guyana launched a tender for companies interested in developing its gas reserves. It would have been faster and probably easier to just bet on the Exxon-led consortium again, but the authorities in Georgetown made it clear at the time they would like some diversification. The tender, however, ended in a somewhat odd way. Of the 17 companies that submitted proposals, Guyana’s government picked one called Fulcrum LNG—set up by a former Exxon executive just a year earlier.
Fulcrum was selected by the government of Guyana to develop an LNG export project, whose price tag was at the time calculated at up to $30 billion. The choice of LNG developer was considered odd, as Fulcrum competed with established LNG market players. Since that tender, Guyana’s LNG plans have not exactly advanced much—and one big reason for this is the availability of natural gas for liquefaction.
Exxon needs some 2 billion cu ft of natural gas daily to inject into its wells to stimulate production, Reuters reported this week, citing unnamed sources, who also said the company had informed the Guyanese government about this. The gas injection is necessary so Exxon can meet oil production targets set for its existing projects in Guyana. In other words, there does not seem to be enough natural gas getting produced in Guyana at this point to make an LNG export project feasible.
One option for the government is to keep the gas that Exxon, Chevron, and CNOOC produce in the Stabroek Block for domestic consumption, including power generation and petrochemicals production. The other is to cut the annual capacity of the planned LNG facility from 6 million tons to 3 million tons, according to Reuters sources.
Yet at this point it is not even clear how much gas the fields in the Exxon consortium bloc can yield. The supermajor is reportedly working on this right now, along with estimates on the cost of extracting that gas, and how soon it can start. The current production of gas from Guyana is associated gas from the Exxon fields in Stabroek.
“We're working with the government of Guyana on development plans that maximize resource recovery and value to the country,” an Exxon spokesperson told Reuters earlier this week, adding that gas supply in Guyana must develop alongside demand.
By Irina Slav for Oilprice.com

articles.title: U.S. Nuclear Fuel Independence Edges Closer as Urenco Expansion Hits 75% | OilPrice.com
articles.text:
The only commercial-scale uranium enrichment plant in the United States is now three-quarters of the way through its latest expansion, a milestone for the country's push to build out a domestic nuclear fuel supply chain. Urenco USA said Oct. 8 that the sixth of eight new centrifuge cascades at its National Enrichment Facility in New Mexico has started production, with the seventh due later this year and the last in spring 2027. As the Trump administration works to reestablish the country as the global leader in nuclear energy, cutting reliance on foreign nuclear fuel imports is a priority for the domestic sector.
The National Enrichment Facility, located in Eunice, New Mexico, currently has a capacity of 4.3 million separative work units (SWUs) of enriched uranium and is installing 700,000 SWUs of new capacity through the eight-cascade project. Urenco aims to expand its capacity to more than 7 million SWUs over the next decade, including a new plant that would start construction in 2029. At present, the plant fulfills about one-third of the country's enriched uranium demand, but that demand is set to increase in coming years as a nuclear renaissance takes hold in the United States and abroad.
After years of plateaued energy demand growth, projections for future energy needs in the United States are skyrocketing, driven by the artificial intelligence boom and data center hyperscalers. In order to meet that demand without completely derailing progress toward the tech sector’s decarbonization pledges, nuclear is emerging as one of the most promising energy development options. Not only is nuclear fission low in greenhouse gas emissions, it produces energy around the clock, making it an especially attractive option for energy security.
However, the country’s reliance on external sources of nuclear fuel could compromise that energy security. Though the United States is the world’s largest producer of nuclear energy, it is not currently a major producer of nuclear fuel. Only five plants in the world operate large-scale uranium conversion today, and nearly half of global enrichment capacity is controlled by Russia, resulting in a major resource bottleneck and significant geopolitical vulnerabilities.
And, making matters worse, prices for uranium are soaring on the global market thanks to a global nuclear energy resurgence. The World Nuclear Association projects that worldwide demand for uranium will climb 28 percent by 2030 and more than double by 2040, leading to increased competition for scarce resources.
As a result, U.S. nuclear energy “faces fuel supply chain vulnerabilities, with tight uranium supplies, geopolitical risks, and rising costs,” threatening both existing reactors and advanced reactor development, according to a January report from Stanford Energy.
For this reason, the recent capacity expansion and planned further developments at the National Enrichment Facility are significant for the United States’ energy autonomy as a whole, and could even help the country move toward being an exporter of enriched uranium, in line with the Trump administration’s ambitions to “produce lasting American dominance in the global nuclear energy market.”
“We are consistently delivering new capacity to help fuel the U.S. nuclear industry and allied nations, and our teams are doing it ahead of schedule and on budget,” said Jody Blackshear, Managing Director of Urenco USA, the firm behind the National Enrichment Facility, in a recent press release. “This experience will support our larger capacity programs in the years ahead as we look to increase our enrichment production by more than 50% to meet the needs of our customers with traditional and advanced reactors.”
The United States has also made progress in boosting domestic uranium recovery, with the same goal of reducing reliance on global uranium supply chains. In April, Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE American: UEC) began production at its Burke Hollow project in South Texas, the first new in-situ recovery (ISR) uranium operation in the country in more than a decade. The company calls it the largest greenfield ISR project to enter production in that time. With Burke Hollow online, UEC now has ISR platforms producing in both Texas and Wyoming, and it plans to start up its Ludeman project in Wyoming in 2027.

articles.title: 6 Countries Pledge Faster Cargo Transfers on Eurasia-Europe Land Bridge | OilPrice.com
articles.text:
Eurasianet is an independent news organization that covers news from and about the South Caucasus and Central Asia, providing on-the-ground reporting and critical perspectives on…
Railway officials from Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan signed a protocol in Tashkent to cut transit times at intermodal nodes on the CASCA+ corridor.
The agreement focuses on faster cargo transfers at Caspian and Black Sea ports, plus simpler tariff regimes and quicker customs clearance.
Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan and Georgia are separately in talks with Romania on a supplemental Black Sea route to extend CASCA+.
Six states participating in an initiative to improve a Eurasia-to-Europe trade corridor have agreed on measures to reduce transit times at intermodal nodes along the route.
Meeting in Tashkent on October 11, railway officials from Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan signed a protocol to enhance the cost competitiveness of the CASCA+ corridor. The six states pledged to work on achieving efficiencies in transferring cargo from one mode of transport to another at Caspian and Black Sea ports.
The protocol also calls on the participating states to simplify tariff regimes and improve customs clearance procedures.
“This approach can attract new volumes of cargo and strengthen CASCA+’s status as one of the most reliable and fastest land bridges in Eurasia,” according to a commentary published by the Turkmen government-aligned news outlet Orient.tm.
The concept for the six-state CASCA+ route dates back to 2019, but efforts to develop the route got underway in earnest in June 2025. Meanwhile, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, and Georgia have engaged Romania is discussions to create a supplemental route to CASCA+ that stretches across the Black Sea.

articles.title: Phát hiện lính cứu hỏa lương 41 triệu đồng/tháng sở hữu hơn 30 BĐS, kiếm hơn 64 tỷ đồng/năm từ việc cho thuê
articles.text:
Phát hiện lính cứu hỏa lương 41 triệu đồng/tháng sở hữu hơn 30 BĐS, kiếm hơn 64 tỷ đồng/năm từ việc cho thuê
Từng làm lính cứu hỏa với mức lương khiêm tốn, người đàn ông Mỹ dần gây dựng khối tài sản lớn nhờ đầu tư, hiện nắm trong tay hơn 30 tài sản nhà ở và thương mại.
- 15-10-2026Phát hiện 1 doanh nhân lương hơn 1 tỷ đồng/năm, quyết định bỏ việc về bán đặc sản quê, thu nhập tăng gấp 16 lần
- 14-10-2026Phát hiện 1 người học chưa hết cấp 3 nhưng có 26.000 tỷ đồng ở tuổi 25
- 14-10-2026Phát hiện 1 nhân viên văn phòng bỏ việc hơn 10 triệu đồng/tháng về bán nước vỉa hè: Mỗi ngày bán 400 cốc, lợi nhuận gần gấp 3 lần lương cũ
Khởi nghiệp để tăng thu nhập
Trong phần lớn 35 năm đầu sự nghiệp, Jeremy Barker ở tại bang Utah, Mỹ, liên tục nhảy việc, từ xây dựng, nhân viên cấp cứu đến lính cứu hỏa, đồng thời thử sức với một số dự án kinh doanh để tìm ra điều mình thực sự yêu thích là công việc cứu hỏa. Đáng tiếc, nghề này không mang lại cho anh thu nhập cao.
“Tôi không muốn sống với mức lương thực nhận chỉ 1.600 USD/tháng (hơn 41 triệu đồng)”, Barker chia sẻ với Business Insider.
Không muốn từ bỏ hoàn toàn công việc lính cứu hỏa, anh quyết định tìm thêm nguồn thu nhập. Ý tưởng khởi nghiệp đến với Barker từ một dự án tự làm rạp chiếu phim tại nhà cho các con. Trong quá trình đó, anh nảy ra ý tưởng sản xuất bản lề dành cho cửa ẩn, loại cửa có thể được thiết kế để hòa vào tường hoặc hệ thống tủ, tạo cảm giác như một phần của nội thất.
Từ ý tưởng này, Barker thành lập Murphy Door.
“Công việc kinh doanh phát triển rất nhanh trong giai đoạn 2013–2016. Chúng tôi ký được hợp đồng với Home Depot, rồi quy mô công ty tăng trưởng mạnh”, anh kể.
Murphy Door tạo thêm nguồn thu nhập cho Barker, nhưng phần lớn lợi nhuận ban đầu được anh tái đầu tư vào doanh nghiệp. Chỉ khi tình cờ bước chân vào thị trường bất động sản, tài sản của người đàn ông này mới bắt đầu tăng trưởng nhanh hơn.
Dùng hợp đồng thuê để huy động vốn mua nhà
Ngoài căn nhà riêng tại bang Utah, Barker gần như chưa có kinh nghiệm mua bán bất động sản. Tuy nhiên, khi Murphy Door phát triển vượt quá diện tích mặt bằng ban đầu, anh cùng môi giới bắt đầu tìm kiếm một tòa nhà lớn hơn để phục vụ hoạt động kinh doanh.
Người môi giới sau đó tìm được một tòa nhà có diện tích 8.361 m², được rao bán với giá 3 triệu USD (hơn 77 tỷ đồng). Theo người này, đây là cơ hội khó có thể bỏ qua, đồng thời mặt bằng đủ lớn để doanh nghiệp của Barker tiếp tục mở rộng trong tương lai.
Barker ban đầu cho rằng đề xuất này quá sức với mình. Tuy nhiên, người môi giới khuyên Barker ký thư bày tỏ ý định mua bất động sản, đồng thời hứa sẽ giúp ông tìm cách huy động vốn.
Tối hôm đó, Barker tìm hiểu trên YouTube về cách tài trợ cho các thương vụ bất động sản thương mại. Anh nhanh chóng nhận ra 2 vấn đề quan trọng: số tiền tiết kiệm 30.000 USD (hơn 776 triệu đồng) chưa đủ để thanh toán khoản trả trước, nhưng phần lớn diện tích tòa nhà lại có thể cho thuê để tạo nguồn thu.
Cụ thể, Murphy Door chỉ cần sử dụng một phần nhỏ mặt bằng, trong khi khoảng 6.503 m², có thể được cho các doanh nghiệp khác thuê. Barker cũng tìm hiểu quy trình ký thư bày tỏ ý định mua, hợp đồng mua bán và khoảng thời gian từ khi ký thỏa thuận đến lúc hoàn tất giao dịch. Anh nhận ra mình có thể tận dụng giai đoạn này để tìm người thuê trước khi chính thức nhận chuyển nhượng tòa nhà.
Sau nhiều lần thương lượng với bên bán, Barker được đồng ý đưa mặt bằng ra thị trường cho thuê trước ngày hoàn tất giao dịch. Sau khi ký hợp đồng mua bán, anh đặt biển cho thuê bên ngoài tòa nhà. Chỉ trong 24 giờ, Barker tìm được khách thuê đầu tiên với diện tích khoảng 2.044 m². Vài ngày sau, một khách thuê lớn khác cũng đồng ý thuê mặt bằng.
Trước khi hoàn tất thương vụ, Barker đã có danh sách hợp đồng thuê đủ để tạo ra khoảng 140.000 USD (hơn 3,6 tỷ đồng) doanh thu cho thuê mỗi năm tại phần diện tích này.
Các hợp đồng thuê đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc giúp Barker huy động số vốn còn thiếu cho thương vụ. Anh cần thêm vài trăm nghìn USD để thanh toán khoản trả trước, trong khi số tiền tiết kiệm ban đầu chỉ là 30.000 USD.
Nhờ có danh sách khách thuê và dòng tiền dự kiến, Barker có thể trình bày với các nhà đầu tư về khả năng tạo thu nhập ròng từ hoạt động cho thuê. Những dữ liệu này cũng giúp anh thuyết phục ngân hàng cấp khoản vay thế chấp. Trong vòng 12 tháng, anh tái cấp vốn thông qua Golden West Credit Union và rút ra 2 triệu USD (hơn 51 tỷ đồng), dù số vốn tự có ban đầu chỉ là 30.000 USD.
Barker cho biết anh đã hoàn trả tiền cho các nhà đầu tư trong vòng 24 tháng. Sau khoảng một thập kỷ, giá trị tòa nhà cũng tăng lên hơn 4 lần so với mức giá mua ban đầu. Thương vụ này giúp anh nhận ra tiềm năng tích lũy tài sản từ bất động sản. Sau đó, Barker tiếp tục áp dụng cách làm tương tự để mở rộng danh mục đầu tư.
Sở hữu danh mục bất động sản mang về 2,5 triệu USD mỗi năm
Chiến lược của Barker tập trung vào những bất động sản bị thị trường bỏ qua hoặc định giá thấp. Anh ưu tiên các tòa nhà đã được rao bán trong thời gian dài, bởi người mua có thể có lợi thế hơn khi thương lượng giá và điều khoản giao dịch.
Một yếu tố quan trọng khác là đàm phán khoảng thời gian đủ dài từ lúc ký hợp đồng đến khi hoàn tất mua bán. Khoảng thời gian này giúp anh chủ động tìm kiếm khách thuê, xây dựng dòng tiền dự kiến trước khi chính thức nhận tài sản.
Theo Business Insider, tính đến tháng 6/2025, Barker sở hữu hơn 30 bất động sản thương mại và nhà ở. Barker từng trải qua hai lần phá sản trong giai đoạn đầu sự nghiệp. Khi bắt đầu đầu tư bất động sản, ông không có nhiều tiền tiết kiệm và buộc phải tìm cách tiếp cận khác biệt.
“Tôi biết mình phải suy nghĩ vượt ra ngoài những cách làm thông thường”, anh nói.
Thay vì dùng tiền để tạo lợi thế cạnh tranh, Barker dành nhiều thời gian nghiên cứu thị trường. Anh tìm hiểu giá thuê, đặc điểm từng loại tòa nhà và chi phí vận hành để đánh giá một thương vụ có khả năng sinh lời hay không.
Sau khi tìm được bất động sản phù hợp, Barker chủ động tiếp cận những người có thể đầu tư trong mạng lưới quan hệ của mình. Anh thẳng thắn thừa nhận bản thân không có nhiều vốn nhưng sẵn sàng dành thời gian và chia sẻ một phần quyền sở hữu để đổi lấy nguồn tiền thực hiện thương vụ đầu tiên.
Barker cho rằng nhà đầu tư cần tự tin khi trình bày cơ hội, nhưng không nên phóng đại kiến thức hay năng lực của mình. Điều quan trọng là hiểu rõ thị trường, nắm được những con số cơ bản và giải thích được vì sao thương vụ có thể tạo ra giá trị.
Theo chia sẻ của Barker, danh mục bất động sản đã giúp anh đạt được độc lập tài chính từ nhiều năm trước, với doanh thu hằng năm khoảng 2,5 triệu USD (hơn 64 tỷ đồng). Nguồn thu này cho phép anh chủ động hơn trong việc sắp xếp thời gian, tiếp tục làm lính cứu hỏa bán thời gian và điều hành Murphy Door.
Đối với Barker, trở ngại lớn nhất khi đầu tư đôi khi không nằm ở việc thiếu tiền hay chưa có kinh nghiệm, mà ở việc quá tập trung vào những lý do khiến một thương vụ không thể thực hiện. Barker cho rằng người muốn bước chân vào thị trường bất động sản cần dành thời gian nghiên cứu, phân tích ngược các yếu tố cấu thành giá và xác định cơ hội thực sự nằm ở đâu.
“Khi người khác không nhìn thấy cơ hội, nếu nhìn vấn đề từ một góc độ khác, có thể bạn sẽ tìm ra cơ hội ở đó”, anh nói.
(Theo aol.com)
Sức khỏe 24h

It took Ukraine just hours to turn President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s “we’re done” into a refinery fire.
Ukrainian drones struck Russia’s Ryazan refinery on Thursday, ending Kyiv’s brief pause in attacks on Russian energy infrastructure after Zelenskyy said Moscow had ignored the ceasefire promoted by U.S. President Donald Trump.
The Rosneft-owned refinery sits about 300 kilometers southeast of Moscow and accounts for nearly 5% of Russia’s refinery throughput. Ryazan Governor Pavel Malkov confirmed a fire at the facility following what he described as a major Ukrainian drone attack. The extent of the damage is still being assessed.
Ukraine had suspended refinery attacks for three days following Trump’s Sunday announcement that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop hitting energy infrastructure.
But more than 500 Russian drones were launched overnight into Thursday, according to Ukrainian authorities. State-owned Naftogaz said a gas production facility in the Poltava region was damaged and operations there were suspended.
Zelenskyy told the Financial Times Thursday that the restriction on refinery attacks was finished.
“The block is out. We’re done,” he said.
For the diesel market, the end to the ceasefire is painful.
Trump has pressured Kyiv to stop attacking Russian refineries as global diesel supplies tighten and U.S. diesel prices remain above $6 per gallon. Russian refining has already been repeatedly disrupted by Ukrainian drone attacks, reducing fuel production and exports.
Ryazan has been hit before, making Thursday’s strike another potential setback for a refining system that has spent much of 2026 repairing damaged units while trying to maintain fuel supply.
The attack turns an announcement made early Thursday into an actual change on the ground. Hours after Zelenskyy said refinery strikes would resume, one of Russia’s largest refining centers was burning again.
By Julianne Geiger for Oilprice.com

articles.title: Doãn Quốc Đam nhận sai, xin lỗi bạn diễn vì cảnh quay ngoài kịch bản
articles.text:
Doãn Quốc Đam nhận sai, xin lỗi bạn diễn vì cảnh quay ngoài kịch bản
Trước những ý kiến trái chiều về diễn xuất trong phân cảnh bạo lực ngoài kịch bản ở phim giờ vàng, Doãn Quốc Đam lên tiếng giải thích, thừa nhận sai sót.
- 23-09-2026Mỹ nhân phim giờ vàng VTV đi diễn 7 năm mới nổi tiếng, đóng chung với Doãn Quốc Đam, Mạnh Trường: "Tôi là minh chứng cho việc dậy thì không thành công"
- 13-04-2026Khôn ngoan như Doãn Quốc Đam, Thanh Sơn
- 10-03-2026Hành động khó hiểu của Doãn Quốc Đam trong rạp chiếu phim khiến MXH xôn xao
Diễn viên Doãn Quốc Đam vừa lên tiếng về phân đoạn bạo lực gia đình trong phim Căn nhà không mái che, sau khi những hình ảnh gây nhiều tranh cãi.
Nam diễn viên thừa nhận chưa trao đổi kỹ với bạn diễn trước khi ghi hình. Anh cho biết thường không tập trước toàn bộ diễn biến nhằm giữ phản ứng bất ngờ, tự nhiên của người cùng diễn. Tuy nhiên, Doãn Quốc Đam nhìn nhận cách làm này cũng là thiếu sót của bản thân.
Phân cảnh Bình (Doãn Quốc Đam) đánh vợ - Hạnh (Huyền Lizzie) thủ vai trong “Căn nhà không mái che”.
Theo Doãn Quốc Đam, trong quá trình làm nghề, anh từng gặp những trường hợp bạn diễn biết trước hành động hoặc tình huống sắp xảy ra, khiến phản ứng trên màn ảnh thiếu tự nhiên. Vì vậy, anh thường chỉ tập trước khoảng 60%, thay vì trao đổi toàn bộ ý đồ diễn xuất.
Nam diễn viên cho rằng nếu biết trước tất cả, bạn diễn có thể phản ứng hoặc thoại trước khi hành động của nhân vật được thể hiện đầy đủ. Dù vậy, anh thừa nhận mong muốn giữ yếu tố bất ngờ không thể thay thế việc trao đổi cần thiết giữa các diễn viên.
Về cảnh đập mâm vào lưng bạn diễn, Doãn Quốc Đam cho biết đã tính toán vị trí ngồi, tay vịn ghế và góc máy nhằm hạn chế lực tác động trực tiếp. Theo anh, tay vịn ghế có tác dụng cản lực, trong khi góc quay tạo cảm giác hành động mạnh trên màn ảnh. Tuy nhiên, nam diễn viên thừa nhận cạnh mâm vẫn có thể va vào người bạn diễn gây đau. Do cảnh quay được thực hiện từ nhiều góc máy, các diễn viên phải thực hiện lại nhiều lần.
Với cảnh nhét cơm, Doãn Quốc Đam cho biết khi tập, tổ thiết kế chưa bày đầy đủ đạo cụ vào khuôn hình. Đến lúc quay chính thức, sau khi đạo diễn góp ý rằng hành động chưa đủ mạnh để khắc họa nhân vật khiến khán giả phẫn nộ, anh đã tăng mức độ thể hiện.
Doãn Quốc Đam cũng bày tỏ sự buồn bã khi những đoạn phim được cắt riêng để chia sẻ trên mạng xã hội khiến một số khán giả cho rằng anh cố tình làm đau bạn diễn hoặc có mâu thuẫn cá nhân. Nam diễn viên nhận trách nhiệm: “Tôi sai khi đã làm vậy. Rất xin lỗi vì các bạn diễn đã phải chịu tổn thương về thân thể khi làm chung cùng với tô i”.
Ngay dưới bài đăng của Doãn Quốc Đam, Huyền Lizzie bình luận: “ Em còn cảm ơn anh không hết. Không có anh làm sao em đẩy được cảm xúc cao trào như thế. Còn về việc bị đau thì có đập vào người tí nào đâu mà đau. Ai xem tinh thì đều thấy đập vào ghế mà. Cái quan trọng là anh diễn rất đỉnh như thật, anh quá tuyệt vời”.
Trước đó, nữ diễn viên cho biết khi tập, những hành động như đập mâm vào lưng, đạp vào người hay nhét cơm vào miệng cô không có trong kịch bản. Những chi tiết này được Doãn Quốc Đam sáng tạo khi vào set quay.
Theo Huyền Lizzie, việc không biết trước những hành động tiếp theo của bạn diễn khiến cô thực sự rơi vào trạng thái sợ hãi, hoảng loạn cùng nhân vật Hạnh. Cảm xúc này giúp cô thể hiện chân thực hơn tâm lý của người phụ nữ bị chồng bạo hành.
Huyền Lizzie cho biết sau khi cảnh quay kết thúc, Doãn Quốc Đam và các thành viên đoàn phim đều hỏi thăm cô có đau hay bị thương ở đâu không. Nữ diễn viên khẳng định không bị tổn thương về thể chất vì Doãn Quốc Đam là người diễn hình thể rất tốt, không gây tổn hại.
Khán giả tranh luận về cảnh bạo lực
Trong Căn nhà không mái che , Doãn Quốc Đam vào vai Bình, người đàn ông sa vào cờ bạc, rượu chè và thường xuyên bạo hành vợ là Hạnh (Phan Minh Huyền). Hai nhân vật có hai con là Thơ và Khang.
Ở tập đầu, Bình nổi giận, đánh đập vợ trước mặt các con sau khi phát hiện Hạnh gửi đơn ly hôn. Đặc biệt, phân đoạn nhân vật nhặt cơm dưới đất nhét vào miệng vợ khiến nhiều khán giả phẫn nộ.
Bên cạnh những ý kiến tranh luận về mức độ dữ dội của cảnh quay, nhiều khán giả lên tiếng bênh vực Doãn Quốc Đam, cho rằng cần phân biệt hành vi của nhân vật Bình với diễn viên ngoài đời. Không ít người cũng khen nam diễn viên nhập vai tốt, thể hiện được sự hung hãn và tính cách đáng trách của người chồng vũ phu.
Phan Minh Huyền nhận được nhiều lời khen nhờ diễn xuất chân thực người phụ nữ nghèo, hiền lành, chịu thương chịu khó, nhiều lần nhẫn nhịn vì muốn giữ mái ấm cho hai con.

articles.title: U.S. Targets Central Asia's Energy and Critical Minerals in Major Trade Push | OilPrice.com
articles.text:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will meet the foreign ministers of the Central Asian republics - Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan - in Samarkand, Uzbekistan on 19 October 2026. Rubio will be accompanied by a delegation of more than 100 U.S. companies. Washington has framed the agenda around economic connectivity, energy security, and shared regional priorities. The meeting should convert earlier political commitments into financed projects, while managing the region's balancing act between the U.S., Russia, and China. The choice of Samarkand is symbolic as it hosted the first C5+1 ministerial in 2015.
The C5+1 was launched in 2015 and organizes U.S. engagement with the five republics around three pillars: economics, energy, and security; the Critical Minerals Dialogue operates in parallel. The Central Asian foreign ministers visited Washington in November last year, where Rubio said he intended to visit the region in 2026. The size of the business delegation signals that Washington wants commercial results rather than another declaration and may be seeking to lock down its influence in the region which escalates the conflict with neighboring Iran.
The key issues
Critical minerals and processing. Central Asia holds significant deposits of tungsten, uranium, rare earths, copper, and other strategic minerals. The practical questions are which projects are bankable, who provides geological data and financing, and how much processing happens in the region rather than abroad. The republics want value-added production, not raw-ore exports, and Uzbekistan has said this explicitly, though the region’s water deficit may limit processing opportunity. Ministers should identify a short list of flagship projects with named partners and timelines and agree on transparent licensing and investor protections.
Connectivity and trade corridors. The Trans-Caspian International Transport Route ("Middle Corridor") across the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, and Georgia, and onward to Europe via Turkey, offers an alternative to routes via Russia, but it is constrained by port capacity, rail interoperability, customs delays, and tariff stacking. Issues to address include harmonized customs procedures, digital trade documentation, financing for rolling stock and port upgrades, and coordination with Caucasus transit partners. Ministers need a concrete corridor roadmap, not general language on improving connectivity. Related: Europe’s Gas Prices Close to 2022 High as Hormuz LNG Flows Remain Limited
Energy security. Central Asia needs reliable power for its own growth and has export potential in hydropower, solar, wind, and natural gas. Priorities include grid integration and regional power trade, U.S. technology and investment in generation and storage, and nuclear and natural gas-related cooperation where relevant. Winter supply reliability and aging Soviet-era infrastructure remain acute vulnerabilities.
Water and climate resilience. Water is tied directly to energy: upstream states (Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan) want hydropower, while downstream states (Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan) need irrigation flows. Glacier melt and drought are intensifying the pressure. The U.S. should offer data, monitoring, and technical assistance, and can support regional frameworks without taking sides on specific dams or allocation disputes.
The region is in the midst of a water crisis and faces a “water debt” - a financing gap of over US$12?billion by 2030 to modernize water and sanitation infrastructure. A lack of water will endanger the region’s ambitious development plans and may become a source of political instability.
Investment climate and business follow-through. The American delegation will want clarity on regulatory predictability, contract enforcement, dispute resolution, currency convertibility, and favorable tax treatment. For Washington, financing tools such as the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation and the Export-Import Bank of the United States are Washington key tools to secure deals. For Uzbekistan, World Trade Organization accession and improved trade access are priorities. Ministers should set up a mechanism, ideally a standing business council or working group, to track which announced deals actually close.
Security, Iran, Afghanistan, and counterterrorism. Security cooperation covers border management, counterterrorism, counter-narcotics, and information sharing. Afghanistan is the hardest question: the republics view the Taliban relationship pragmatically and are deepening trade, transit, and energy links with Kabul, while the U.S. wants to avoid steps that legitimize the Taliban. The republics actively trade with Iran and Trump’s threat to “annihilate” the Islamic Republic is causing anxiety in the region. A frank exchange on red lines, trade, projects such as transit and electricity lines, and shared threat assessments is a must.
Strategic balance and sanctions. The republics value the C5+1 as a way to diversify partnerships, not to choose sides as the region is newly independent and not part of someone else’s empire for the first time since the 18th Century. Russian and Chinese influence is deeply embedded through trade, labor migration, energy infrastructure, cultural, and security ties. Sanctions compliance, particularly re-export of restricted goods to Russia, is a sensitive issue that should be raised privately rather than publicly. Washington should present itself as offering options, not demanding alignment with its grievances with its superpower competitors.
Governance and civil society. The rule of law, judicial independence, media freedom, and civil society underpin long-term investor confidence. The Trump administration prioritizes commercial and security interests, but language on institutional reform tied to investment protection can address governance without public confrontation or the appearance of American meddling.
The path to success
The republics expect investment and market access; U.S. companies expect predictability. Both sides risk disappointment if announcements outpace deal closings. The five capitals work to present a united front, but they do not always agree. Turkmenistan is “permanently neutral” and is more cautious about regional frameworks.
Moscow and Beijing will watch the meeting closely. Tweeting about it as anti-Russian or anti-Chinese would complicate the republics’ positions. Washington should seek commitments on human rights improvements. Omitting governance entirely could draw criticism from the U.S. Congress and civil society, while pressing too hard (and publicly) could reduce regional goodwill.
Washington must be clear that it is a reliable, long-term, commercial and security partner that respects the sovereignty of each state and offers real alternatives, not conditions, and won’t press-gang the republics into its conflicts with China, Russia, Afghanistan, and Iran. The republics should stress that regional cooperation, especially on water, transit, and customs, multiplies the value of external investment and strengthens bargaining power with all partners.
By James Durso for Oilprice.com

articles.title: Đúng 3 ngày nữa - 18/10, dịch vụ này miễn phí cho toàn bộ người dân Việt Nam
articles.text:
Đúng 3 ngày nữa - 18/10, dịch vụ này miễn phí cho toàn bộ người dân Việt Nam
Dịch vụ đang được nhắc tới cụ thể là gì, áp dụng đến bao giờ là điều nhiều người quan tâm.
Theo trang Thông tin Chính phủ, vào lúc 15h30 Chủ nhật (18/10/2026), Hãng phim Tài liệu và Khoa học Trung ương sẽ tổ chức buổi chiếu miễn phí bộ phim tài liệu mang tên "Nữ Bộ trưởng Ngoại giao đầu tiên của Việt Nam". Đây là cơ hội để người dân và du khách đang có mặt tại Hà Nội thưởng thức một tác phẩm điện ảnh giàu giá trị lịch sử mà không phải trả phí.
Buổi chiếu diễn ra tại Hãng phim Tài liệu và Khoa học Trung ương, địa chỉ số 465 Hoàng Hoa Thám, phường Ngọc Hà, Hà Nội. Bộ phim có thời lượng 55 phút, tập trung tái hiện những dấu mốc quan trọng trong cuộc đời và sự nghiệp ngoại giao của bà Nguyễn Thị Bình, nguyên Phó Chủ tịch nước Cộng hòa xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam.
Điểm nhấn của tác phẩm là vai trò của bà Nguyễn Thị Bình trong quá trình đàm phán và ký kết Hiệp định Paris năm 1973, một sự kiện có ý nghĩa đặc biệt quan trọng đối với lịch sử dân tộc. Thông qua những thước phim tư liệu, hình ảnh của nữ chính khách hiện lên với trí tuệ, bản lĩnh và sự kiên định, góp phần khắc họa dấu ấn của ngoại giao Việt Nam trong cuộc đấu tranh giành độc lập và hòa bình.
Đáng chú ý, đây không phải là bộ phim mới được sản xuất trong năm 2026. Tác phẩm đã được giới thiệu tới công chúng từ nhiều năm trước. Bộ phim từng nằm trong danh sách những tác phẩm điện ảnh được tặng thưởng về chủ đề học tập và làm theo tấm gương đạo đức Hồ Chí Minh năm 2010.
Việc giới thiệu lại tác phẩm vào ngày 18/10, chỉ hai ngày trước Ngày Phụ nữ Việt Nam 20/10, càng tạo thêm ý nghĩa cho hoạt động này. Thay vì chỉ tiếp cận những thông tin lịch sử qua sách báo, khán giả có dịp nhìn lại hành trình của một nữ chính khách tiêu biểu qua ngôn ngữ điện ảnh và những hình ảnh tư liệu.
Người dân và du khách cần làm gì để được xem phim miễn phí?
Chương trình không thu phí tham dự, song người có nhu cầu xem phim cần thực hiện đăng ký trước để ban tổ chức sắp xếp chỗ ngồi.
Cụ thể, người dân và du khách có thể truy cập fanpage Facebook chính thức của Thông tin Chính phủ, tìm bài đăng thông báo về buổi chiếu phim "Nữ Bộ trưởng Ngoại giao đầu tiên của Việt Nam" ngày 18/10. Tại phần bình luận của bài viết, ban tổ chức hướng dẫn đăng ký thông qua đường dẫn được cung cấp. Người tham dự cần truy cập đường dẫn và làm theo các bước đăng ký.
Tuy nhiên, do sức chứa của phòng chiếu có hạn, ban tổ chức sẽ đóng đường dẫn đăng ký khi đã đủ số lượng người tham dự. Vì vậy, những người quan tâm nên chủ động đăng ký sớm, đồng thời kiểm tra thông tin xác nhận để tránh trường hợp đến nơi nhưng không có chỗ.
Đối với du khách đang có kế hoạch tham quan Hà Nội vào dịp cuối tuần, cần lưu ý buổi chiếu chỉ được tổ chức tại một địa điểm, vào khung giờ 15h30 ngày 18/10. Người tham dự nên chủ động tìm hiểu đường đi, sắp xếp lịch trình và có mặt trước giờ chiếu để thuận tiện cho việc ổn định chỗ ngồi.
Chương trình phục vụ công chúng trong phạm vi số chỗ được bố trí, do đó khán giả cần theo dõi thông báo chính thức để cập nhật tình trạng đăng ký.
Nhiều chương trình chiếu phim miễn phí từng được tổ chức trước đây
Thực tế, đây không phải lần đầu tiên Hãng phim Tài liệu và Khoa học Trung ương tổ chức hoạt động chiếu phim miễn phí phục vụ công chúng. Tháng 5/2026, đơn vị này đã triển khai chuỗi chiếu phim tài liệu hàng tháng mang tên "Việt Nam chưa kể hết", mở đầu bằng bộ phim "Việt Nam – Hồ Chí Minh" dài 60 phút, nhân kỷ niệm 136 năm Ngày sinh Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh.
Tiếp đó, từ ngày 24–27/7/2026, Hãng phim tổ chức chiếu miễn phí 9 tác phẩm tài liệu tại số 465 Hoàng Hoa Thám nhân kỷ niệm 79 năm Ngày Thương binh – Liệt sĩ. Chương trình mở cửa phục vụ đông đảo người dân, trong đó có cán bộ, chiến sĩ, thương bệnh binh và thân nhân liệt sĩ.
Không chỉ tại địa điểm này, nhiều hoạt động tương tự cũng được triển khai ở Hà Nội. Gần đây nhất, theo Cổng thông tin điện tử Bộ Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch, từ ngày 7–9/10/2026, Viện Phim Việt Nam đã tổ chức chiếu miễn phí ba bộ phim "Em bé Hà Nội", "Ngày về" và "Đào, phở và piano" tại Rạp Ngọc Khánh, số 523 Kim Mã, nhân kỷ niệm 72 năm Ngày Giải phóng Thủ đô.
Những hoạt động này góp phần tạo thêm cơ hội để người dân tiếp cận các tác phẩm điện ảnh có giá trị lịch sử và văn hóa. Buổi chiếu ngày 18/10 tới đây tiếp tục mang đến một lựa chọn trải nghiệm miễn phí cho công chúng, đồng thời giúp thế hệ trẻ hiểu thêm về cuộc đời và những đóng góp của một nữ chính khách đặc biệt trong lịch sử Việt Nam.
Sức khỏe 24h

articles.title: IEA Speeds Emergency Oil Release | OilPrice.com
articles.text:
China is financing Qatar's LNG…
Trump announces a potential $70–80…
The International Energy Agency will release more than 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible and accelerate the rest of its emergency oil draw,
Total releases are now set to exceed the 400 million barrels pledged in March.
About 330 million barrels have already been released since the Strait of Hormuz crisis triggered the record coordinated stock draw. IEA members still have roughly 100 million barrels left to deliver under the March action, with some countries having released more than their original commitments and others still holding barrels back.
The diesel portion disappointed the market.
IEA members had discussed releasing as much as 50 million barrels of diesel as part of a broader 100-million-barrel package of crude and refined products. European gasoil prices moved higher following Thursday’s announcement, with traders apparently hoping for a bigger immediate injection.
The United States wanted more, too. U.S. officials have pressed other IEA members to make additional emergency barrels available as diesel prices remain near record levels ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
Spain will release another 4.4 million barrels from strategic reserves in October. It has so far delivered 3.7 million barrels of the 11.5 million barrels it pledged in March.
Diesel remains the weak spot in the global fuel system.
Refinery disruptions in the Middle East and reduced Russian fuel production have trimmed diesel exports, even as Persian Gulf crude shipments have begun to recover.
Governments have already put roughly 330 million emergency barrels into the market, with another 100 million or so still scheduled.
And while more than 20 million barrels of diesel are now being moved up in the timeline, the market was clearly hoping for more.
By Julianne Geiger for Oilprice.com
